content:

Отрывок из «L’Almanach du Peuple» 1871 года. – Этот исторический обзор несколько длинен и не везде представляет одинаковый интерес, поэтому мы сделали в нём несколько сокращений и местами немного сжали текст. (Примечание «Quelques écrits d’Adhémar SCHWITZGUÉBEL», 1908).

Это товарищество, основанное в Лондоне в сентябре 1864 года делегатами рабочих из наиболее промышленно развитых стран, за несколько лет приобрело такие масштабы, что повсюду вызывает озабоченность – и у правительств, и у буржуазии.

В древности был ведь Спартак, а в Средние века – Жакерия; Новое время слышало даже возглас: Жить работая или умереть сражаясь, а позднее – Хлеба или свинца; но никогда в истории не наблюдалось такого факта: пролетарии всех стран мирно объединяются, чтобы изучать и обсуждать коренные причины нищеты, а также средства, способные радикально его устранить.

В Европе и Америке рабочие издавна создавали объединения с целью взаимной поддержки в случае болезни, безработицы и тому подобного… Эти объединения носили местный или национальный характер и не раз вынуждены были вступать в борьбу с хозяевами, защищая интересы своих членов, – ведь хозяин естественно склонен платить своим работникам как можно меньше. Снижение зарплат происходит особенно в периоды кризисов, когда рабочие руки в большом количестве предлагаются капиталистам и хозяевам.

Опыт вскоре открыл рабочим причину падения зарплат, и крайняя нищета, в которой они оказались, заставила их задуматься об устранении зла. Они основали свои общества сопротивления.

Чувство права всё больше развивалось в среде рабочего класса; кассы сопротивления, поддерживаемые большинством рабочих, становились всё сильнее… Осмыслив своё положение по-новому, рабочие стали требовать повышения зарплат и сокращения рабочего дня. Стачки становились всё более частыми; солидарность между рабочими одной страны была настолько сильна, что преимущество почти всегда оставалось за ними. Однако международные сообщения стали настолько лёгкими, что за несколько часов хозяева могли вызвать рабочих из соседней страны на замену тем, кто бастовал. Это случалось во время нескольких важных стачек и стало причиной многих неудач рабочих. Именно это и определило появление Международного товарищества рабочих.

Кроме того, современные идеи, проникая в народные массы, побуждали рабочих разных наций больше не считать друг друга врагами, несмотря на различия в происхождении; а общность страданий и тождество интересов должны были сделать рабочие классы всех стран единым общественным телом.

Делегаты рабочего класса собирались ежегодно, начиная с 1866 года, на общие конгрессы, и там совершалась двойная работа: развивать и укреплять общую организацию пролетариата и формулировать посредством резолюций общие устремления рабочих.

Федеративная организация касс сопротивления представлялась всем наиболее практичным средством обеспечить успех труда в его борьбе против капитала. Но поняли также, что, дабы не вращаться вечно в одном и том же круге, необходимо устранить причину существующего антагонизма… Чтобы положить конец этому антагонизму, нужно, чтобы орудие труда – капитал – был предоставлен в распоряжение труда, не делая труд его рабом; иными словами, нужно изменить систему собственности.

Когда этот вопрос был поднят на общих конгрессах, обнаружились две системы: мютюэлизм и коллективизм.

Мютюэлистская теория, ссылавшаяся на Прудона, хотела основать общественную организацию не на собственности, а на кредите: эта организация, обязанная инициативе самих производителей, взаимно кредитующих друг друга и гарантирующих друг другу обмен своих продуктов, приводила к бесплатности кредита и обмену по себестоимости… Некоторые из последователей Прудона пытались на конгрессах …

author: worker
title: Running Down The Walls Brings Political Prisoner Solidarity to the Gates of the Chicago Metropolitan Correctional Center
content:
From

Chicago ABCF


​Chicago Police Attack the Marathon and Generator Show Seizing Equipment and Arresting Four


On Saturday the 19th of September, chapters of the

Anarchist Black Cross Federation

 (ABCF) on occupied Turtle Island held the annual Running Down the Walls (RDTW) non-competitive solidarity 5K marathon and fundraiser event. Each year people hit the concrete both inside and outside prisons for a collective run, walk, roll and march towards freedom for political prisoners and the abolition of prisons. RDTW is also the primary yearly push to raise funds for the

ABCF Warchest

 which each month puts money on the books of political prisoners/prisoners of war to help with commissary, communications and other financial needs. This year Running Down The Walls events were held in Los Angeles CA, Bloomington IN, Philadelphia PA, Brooklyn NY, Kingston NY, Ft Lauderdale FL, Lowell MA, Eugene OR and Chicago IL.


This year’s Chicago RDTW descended upon the federal Metropolitan Correctional Center (MCC), a brutalist downtown skyscraper imposing harshly upon an otherwise pleasant tree-laden plaza that had until recently been fenced off from protesters and people looking for a place to hang out in public. MCC is also kitty-corner to the ICE Field Office as well as State Department and U.S. Citizenship & Immigration Services offices. This was the second year that RDTW was held at MCC, also the site of occasional noise demos, but is not subject to nearly enough attention considering all that has happened at the hands of the feds in Chicago and elsewhere this past few years.


The federal Bureau of Prisons holds our comrades captive in a dehumanizing destitute existence that has only increased in cruelty as the Trump Administration weaponizes the DOJ against immigrants and resistance movements. It’s been a hard year of escalating fascist repression: militarized stormtroopers rampaging neighborhoods to kidnap undocumented people into networks of imprisonment and deportation, the

targeting of dissent as “terrorism”

 with manufactured federal conspiracies and lengthy sentences, increased repression of political prisoners behind the walls, and even the

criminalization of zines

 and

blogs

. If

prisons are escalating

, so must we; as long as our comrades inside are fighting, know that we will also take the struggle to the front gates. We also do it a bit different in Chicago; for the sixth year in addition to the rally march and marathon we planned a generator show with bands and DJs blasting punk, hip hop, and techno right outside the prison walls so the people held inside can enjoy, dance along with us, and know we got their back.


As people took to the plaza hanging banners and setting up tables for zines and food, almost immediately the Chicago Police Department arrived and began intimidating the crowd with threats of arrest and violence over the unpermitted gathering and the mobile soundsystem. Of course we never need or seek permission from the state to gather in public, but the MCC and the park in front of it is federal property under the proclaimed jurisdiction of the Bureau of Prisons (BOP). Local, county, and state police continue to work on behalf of federal agencies, not only BOP. Illinois State Police, Chicago Police and others have

coordinated with the feds to spy on anti-ICE organizing

 and provide security stabilizing the federal kidnapping apparatus

outside Broadview

 and

throughout the state

 (much like outside Delaney Hall or MDC Los Angeles and so on)– despite the so-called “TRUST Act,” a reform meant to protect the image of local and state police from being linked to immigration enforcement. So not surprising it was dozens of CPD who pulled up menacingly with the white shirts arguing about federal noise regulations on the plaza after having met with the feds inside the jail. After resisting the initial barrage of police threats and reclaiming the park, the rally began defiantly reading the statements and recordings that political prisoners prepared for the event.


Champagne Song called in to

read their statement

 and conversate with the people, reminding us that we are a sea that is unstoppable, that we will win; an encouraging confidence in our collective strength standing in front of a building that will not exist in 100 years, the sentence Champagne received for showing solidarity outside the Prairieland detention center: it is our every intent collectively that we will free them …

author: Adam Schwartz
title: Require Police to Get a Warrant to Search ALPR Data
content:
This post was co-written by

Andi Cao

, an EFF legal intern.


Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) are mass surveillance. They photograph every passing car and log where and when it was captured, building a searchable record of where nearly everyone drives.

Cities should not buy them

, and cities that already have them should shut them down.


Where these systems still operate, courts and state legislatures must reduce their harms by (among other things) requiring police to get a warrant before searching stored ALPR data. A warrant requirement would not make mass surveillance acceptable, but it would require police to justify a search to a judge before accessing records of people’s movements. Without this independent judicial check on police power, officers have been searching this data for improper reasons (many exposed by EFF) that violate our fundamental rights.


A warrant requires a judge to find probable cause and specificity—many warrantless police searches of ALPR data lack both. Officers have searched this data to profile Romani people, monitor protesters, investigate an abortion, find immigrants for deportation, track a man who complained about a deputy, stalk romantic partners, and even for no stated reason beyond “LMAO.” A warrant requirement would force law enforcement to justify these searches

before

 accessing sensitive location records, not leave the people they target to discover and challenge the abuse after the harm is done.


What a Warrant Requires


Warrants are a check on police power. Before officers can search a person or their property, the

Fourth Amendment

 requires them to convince a neutral judge, under oath, that probable cause exists, meaning a fair probability the search will turn up evidence of a crime. The warrant must also describe with particularity what will be searched, so police cannot go on a fishing expedition. Critically, the officer who wants to search is not the person who decides whether the search is justified.


That is why warrants are required for so many kinds of police surveillance. For example, police generally need a warrant to

wiretap phone calls

, to

search the contents of a cell phone

, and to

obtain historical cell phone location records

.


Stored ALPR data reveals sensitive information about the private details of our lives: where we go, when, and with whom. That’s why we believe police searches of stored ALPR data should also require a warrant. Earlier this month, a federal judge in Oklahoma

agreed

.


What Goes Wrong Without a Warrant: San Jose, California


San Jose demonstrates the harmful consequences of letting law enforcement search stored ALPR data without a warrant. EFF and the ACLU of Northern California represent SIREN and CAIR-California in a

lawsuit

 challenging this practice.


The first problem is the sheer number of times that SJPD officers search stored ALPR data:

261,711 times

 between June 5, 2024, and June 17, 2025, about 692 searches a day. That scale is the result of having no warrant requirement, which would greatly reduce this kind of casual police surveillance.


Inevitably, officers abuse this unchecked power. In September, San Jose’s police chief

disclosed

 an example from five months earlier: the department had fired an officer who used its ALPR system to track a woman who had accused his cousin of domestic violence, and then shared her location information with his cousin. The abusive search of stored ALPR data

came to light

 only after the woman told police that her alleged assailant had implied he was tracking her.  A warrant requirement would have prevented this.


Of course, similar problems appear nationwide. For each example below, consider how things could have turned out differently if the officer had to put the reason for the search in a sworn warrant application and handed it to a judge.


Racial profiling of Romani people


More than 80 law enforcement agencies

searched the Flock network

 using terms that unfairly stereotype Romani people, often without mentioning any crime. For example, the Grand Prairie (Texas) Police Department searched for “g*psy” six times using a Flock feature that identifies vehicles traveling together, in effect targeting a whole community without naming a crime.


No judge should sign that warrant. Ethnicity is not evidence of a crime, and a search aimed at an entire ethnic group is the opposite of particular: it targets people for

who

 they are, not evidence …

author: Saima Desai
title: Beating burnout in social movements requires strategy
content:
This article

Beating burnout in social movements requires strategy

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


I recently showed up to a protest for the first time in months, looked around, and thought: “Who the hell

are

 all these people?” 


Friends I could once rely on running into at protests when I was younger were missing. 


The fact that I hadn’t been to a protest in months was unusual. I’d had a hard season of exhaustion and cynicism, and I felt I was falling out of the loop. In the last few years, I turned 30 and moved back to my hometown, and the once-intense focus on social movements that I had in my 20s was now jostling for attention with work and family. 


The absence of my comrades at that protest seemed to signal that others, too, had burned or faded out of organizing.


It’s a trend that Chris Dixon describes in his new book, which is about sticking around for the long haul in the fight for a better world: “In radical activist scenes especially,” he writes, “people tend to age out by their 30s, if not before.” 


When the manuscript of Dixon’s book came my way, it spoke to my fear of burning or fading out of the movements that have given my life meaning and momentum. (I sit on the editorial collective of Between The Lines Books, and helped select the book for publication; it was released in September 2026.) 


After a few recent boom-and-bust cycles of uprisings — 2020’s Black liberation uprising, the Palestine solidarity protests that kicked off in 2023 — it’s a timely and thoughtful book about building movements with care and commitment.


Dixon (who unfortunately shares a name with a far more famous American crypto bro) is an anti-authoritarian activist and a scholar of social movements. “For the Long Haul: How to Stay in the Fight for a Better World”

is the latest effort in his lifelong project to understand how social movements are built and sustained.


Dixon grew up in Alaska, and the book opens by describing his decades-long friendship with Ruth Sheridan, an anarchist who was in her 70s when she first came to talk to his eighth grade labor history class. That early curiosity — about how left-wing social movements are built and sustained and the unsung activists who make it happen — showed up in his 2014 book “Another Politics: Talking Across Today’s Transformative Movements,” in which he shared lessons from almost a decade spent interviewing organizers across the U.S. and Canada. 


Now, Dixon has reached back into this same conversational archive to write “For the Long Haul.” 


We meet Bill Stivers, an elder communist Dixon befriended as a teen; Rachel Herzing, the co-founder of prison abolitionist group Critical Resistance; the political prisoner David Gilbert with whom he exchanged letters from jail, and many more. 


These lifelong leftists share their observations about what leads to burnout, the many-headed monster that has long stalked social movements. During this time of totalizing neoliberalism and weakened movement infrastructure, it’s grown especially powerful. These movement veterans counsel us to be patient, open-minded and to “practice being nobody special.” 


Dixon tells the story of Stivers who, at the age of 76, travelled from Anchorage, Alaska to the state of Chiapas in southern Mexico to attend the Zapatistas’ Intercontinental Encounter for Humanity and Against Neoliberalism. It was just a couple years after the militant group’s armed uprising and a young Dixon, more swayed by a European left tradition at that time, looked on with skepticism. But Stivers ended up having the more clear-eyed assessment of this new approach to anti-capitalist struggle. Stivers had cultivated the long view, which helped him avoid cynicism and dogmatism, and encouraged him to keep learning and stay open to new developments.  


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


What I found most helpful about the book was Dixon’s formulation of burnout: he sees it not just as a type of overwork or exhaustion, but as a feeling of defeat that becomes more common because of a lack of strategy. Dixon introduces this idea by sharing a conversation he had with Kim Marks, a direct-action environmentalist and Indigenous solidarity organizer in Oregon: “So much of burnout is about not being effective,” she said, “and so much ineffectiveness comes from not having a plan.” 


Dixon traces the ways that people often burn out of activist groups back to …

title: Cops raid DIY HRT meeting in Berlin
content:
This Sunday, 18 October 2026, German police raided a trans DIY HRT event organized by The Dolls Berlin in community centre Casa Kuà.

While the group was holding a talk about cryptocurrency and their role in purchasing HRT online, 38 uniformed and plain clothes cops stormed the building, confiscating hormones and money from attendees, recording their identity and detaining them for over 4 hours. So far, nobody was charged with any crime, (as there is nothing illegal about having hormones or money on your person).

The intimidation raid has shocked the community and over a hundred people gathered quickly for a counter demo. One person was arrested during the demo.

title: Rechte Gewalt, leere Kassen: Ostdeutsche Zivilgesellschaft unter Druck
content:
Dossier


„In der Bundespolitik ist das Entsetzen über den Erfolg der AfD bei der Bundestagswahl noch immer groß. (…) „Zwickau, Chemnitz, Zittau – da würde ich von extrem rechten Dominanzbestrebungen sprechen“, zählt die Expertin [Heike Radvan, Professorin für Rechtsextremismusforschung] für Sachsen auf. Die soziale Dynamik ziele darauf ab, den öffentlichen Raum für alle Personen einzuschränken, die nicht in ein rechtes Weltbild passen, beispielsweise durch dominantes Auftreten von AfD-Abgeordneten im Kommunalparlament – und durch Bedrohungen und Gewalt. (…) Exemplarisch für [die] AfD-Strategie stehen die Attacken auf das Bundesprogramm „Demokratie leben“ des Bundesministeriums für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend, das zivilgesellschaftliche Initiativen und Vereine fördert, die sich für Demokratie und gegen Extremismus engagieren…“  

Artikel von Elisa Pfleger in den »Blättern« 4/2025


 und mehr daraus/dazu:


Demokratieprojekte in Sachsen-Anhalt: Was kostet die Demokratie?


„

Eine mögliche AfD-Landesregierung in Sachsen-Anhalt könnte vor allem ein Ziel haben: Demokratieprojekte beenden. Die sollen nun eilig gerettet werden.


Es ist ein „Appell“, mit dem sich Sebastian Koch vergangene Woche an den kleinen Verein Ipse Exitare in der Altmark in Sachsen-Anhalt wandte. Es liege ihm fern, Kritik zu äußern, schrieb der AfD-Politiker in einer direkten Nachricht. Aber er müsse anmerken, dass sich der Verein zuletzt kritisch über die AfD geäußert habe – und das sei verboten. Solche „Verstöße können und müssen zum Entzug der Förderung führen“, schreibt der AfD-Mann weiter. Und dass seine Partei künftig alle Vereine hinsichtlich ihrer „Neutralitätspflicht“ überprüfen wolle.


Der Heimat- und Kulturverein, der Konzerte und Veranstaltungen organisiert, die Dorfkirche sanierte oder das jährliche „Lichtblütenfestival“ veranstaltet, wollte sich auf taz-Anfrage dazu nicht äußern. Gegenüber der Volksstimme zeigte er sich aber irritiert. „Das ist doch völlig abstrus“, sagte Vereinschef Tilo Mottschall. „Was soll das denn bedeuten? Förderung gibt es dann nur noch für das, was der AfD passt?“ AfD-Mann Koch, der gerade erstmals in den Landtag einzog, relativierte seine Aktion auf taz-Anfrage. Man müsse schon sehr viel Fantasie besitzen, um darin eine Drohung zu sehen, schrieb er. (…)


Dabei ist Ipse Excitare gar kein explizit politischer Verein, nicht einmal ein dezidiertes Demokratieprojekt. Gerade deshalb erschüttert die Nachricht von Koch viele in Sachsen-Anhalt. Selbst die CDU-Landtagsabgeordnete Sandra Hietl-Heuer verurteilte Kochs Nachricht als „Einschüchterung“. Kochs Nachricht unterstreicht, was die AfD seit Langem plant: den linken „NGO-Sumpf austrocknen“, wie es die rechtsextreme Partei nennt. (…)


Panik vor einer AfD-Landesregierung


Bei vielen Initiativen in Sachsen-Anhalt herrscht Panik. Noch ist der Landeshaushalt für das kommende Jahr nicht beschlossen. Die Verhandlungen dürften starten, sobald die neue Regierung steht – und sich über Monate hinziehen. Dass eine AfD-geführte Landesregierung darin Gelder für die kritische Zivilgesellschaft einplanen wird, bezweifeln viele. Das hat schon jetzt konkrete Folgen. So berichtet Antje Arndt von der Mobilen Opferberatung, die mit ihrem Team Betroffene rechter Gewalt unterstützt, dass bereits alle Angestellten gekündigt seien, weil die Zukunftsaussichten völlig unklar seien. (…)


AfD könnte Bundesfördermittel blockieren


Zum Sozialministerium gehört auch das Landesdemokratiezentrum, das zusammen mit dem Bund auswählt, welche Projekte mit Bundesmitteln gefördert werden. Auch dieses Zentrum könnte die AfD abschaffen oder ihm auferlegen, die vom Bund bewilligten Fördergelder nicht weiterzugeben. Eine konkrete Überlegung deshalb: Das Landesdemokratiezentrum an einen freien Träger anzudocken – womit dieses künftig unabhängig von der Landesregierung wäre

…“

Artikel von Anne Fromm und Konrad Litschko vom 18.10.2026 in der taz online

 


AfD nimmt mit parlamentarischen Anfragen Einfluss auf Soziale Arbeit in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und Thüringen


„Die AfD in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und in Thüringen nutzt parlamentarische Instrumente ihrer Landtagsfraktionen, insbesondere zahlreiche Kleine Anfragen, um Einfluss auf das Sozialwesen und die Soziale Arbeit in den beiden Bundesländern zu nehmen. title: Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa: Prominent Anti-Corruption Lawyer in Guatemala Assassinated
content:
The prominent Guatemalan anti-corruption lawyer Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa was fatally shot along with another man on Saturday at a sports center in Guatemala City. For years, Solórzano Foppa had been outspoken against Guatemala’s most powerful politicians, business leaders and companies. He was known for his anti-corruption work as head of the Criminal Investigations Directorate within the Public Prosecutor’s Office and later as head of Guatemala’s tax authority, when he helped prosecute dozens of powerful Guatemalan business figures.


“In more recent years, he developed a social media presence, and he was forcefully denouncing corruption,” says Roman Gressier, a journalist based in Guatemala City. “We were thinking about [the killing of Solórzano Foppa] not only as an assassination, but also having a deep effect on freedom of expression.”


“Juan Francisco was a young lawyer coming from a background of pro-democracy and revolutionary activists,” says Silvia Solórzano Foppa, Juan Francisco’s mother. Her son was 43 years old when he was killed.

author: Unknown
title: 86 bin öğrenci Kürtçeyi seçti: Peki öğretmeni nerede, kitabı nerede?
content:
“Bir dilin geleceği, onu öğrenmek isteyen çocukların önüne engeller koymakla değil, o dili öğrenebilecekleri koşulları yaratmakla güvence altına alınır.”


16 şehirde, 321 okulda, 86.064 öğrenci Kürtçe seçmeli dersini tercih etti. Bu rakam, yalnızca bir dersin kaç öğrenci tarafından seçildiğini gösteren istatistiksel bir veri değil. Aynı zamanda çocukların kendi dillerini öğrenme isteğini, bu isteğin eğitim sisteminden karşılık beklediğini ve anadilin eğitimdeki yerinin yeniden tartışılması gerektiğini ortaya koyan önemli bir gösterge.


Ancak tam da burada yanıtlanması gereken temel bir soru var: Madem 86 bin öğrenci Kürtçeyi öğrenmek istiyor, peki bu öğrencilerin kaçına öğretmen, ders kitabı ve nitelikli bir öğrenme ortamı sunuluyor?


Öğrenci var, talep var, tercih var. Peki, öğretmen nerede, kitap nerede, bu çocukların dil öğrenme hakkını hayata geçirecek eğitim politikaları nerede?


Sorunun özü tam da bu. Bir dili seçmeli ders olarak tercih edebilmek önemli. Ancak tercih edilen dersin fiilen yürütülememesi, öğretmen bulunamaması veya ders materyallerinin yetersiz kalması durumunda, tanınan hak ile bu hakkın gerçek hayattaki karşılığı arasında ciddi bir mesafe oluşur. Kâğıt üzerinde var olan bir imkân, uygulamada karşılık bulmadığında eğitim hakkı eksik kalır.


Eğitimde bir hakkın tanınması, o hakkın gerektirdiği koşulların oluşturulmasını da zorunlu kılar. Bir öğrenci Kürtçeyi öğrenmek istiyorsa okulunda bu dersi verebilecek öğretmen bulunmalı, yaşına ve sınıf düzeyine uygun ders kitaplarına ulaşabilmeli ve dili düzenli biçimde öğrenebileceği bir eğitim ortamına sahip olmalı. Bunlar bir ayrıcalık değil, eğitim hakkının gereği.


86.064 öğrencinin Kürtçeyi seçmesi, küçümsenecek bir talep değil. Üstelik bu tercihlerin hangi koşullarda yapıldığını da göz önünde bulundurmak gerekir. Öğretmen yetersizliği, derslerin düzenli açılamaması, kaynak eksikliği ve ailelerin yeterince bilgilendirilmemesi gibi etkenler, öğrencilerin tercihlerini ve eğitim sürecine katılımlarını etkileyebilir.


Bu nedenle tartışmayı yalnızca “Kaç öğrenci Kürtçeyi seçti?” sorusuyla sınırlamak doğru değildir. Asıl sorulması gereken şu: Bu öğrencilerin kaçı seçtiği dersi gerçekten alabiliyor, kaçı düzenli eğitim görüyor ve kaçı Kürtçeyi öğrenebileceği yeterli koşullara sahip?


Rakamları açıklamak elbette önemli. Ancak rakamların arkasındaki eğitim gerçeğini görmek ve sorunları çözmek çok daha önemli.


Kürtçe seçmeli derslerinin önündeki temel sorunlardan biri, öğretmen ihtiyacının karşılanması. Öğretmen, eğitim sürecinin yalnızca bir uygulayıcısı değil; öğrencinin öğrenmesini sağlayan, dil becerilerini geliştiren ve dili yaşayan bir iletişim aracına dönüştüren temel unsur.


Öğretmen eksikliği giderilmeden, derslerin düzenli ve nitelikli biçimde yürütülmesini beklemek gerçekçi değil. Aynı şekilde ders kitapları ve yardımcı materyaller olmadan öğretmenlerin eğitim sürecini sağlıklı biçimde sürdürmesi de güçleşir.


Ders kitapları, yalnızca öğrencinin önüne konulan basılı materyaller değil. Onlar dilin sistemli öğretilmesini, okuma ve yazma becerilerinin geliştirilmesini, kelime dağarcığının zenginleşmesini ve öğrencinin kendi dilinde düşünme ve kendini ifade etme yeteneğinin güçlenmesini sağlar.


Bu nedenle ilgili kurumların önünde açık bir sorumluluk bulunuyor: Öğretmen ihtiyacı belirlenmeli, yeterli sayıda öğretmen yetiştirilmeli ve görevlendirilmeli, ders kitapları ile yardımcı materyaller hazırlanarak okullara zamanında ulaştırılmalı. Derslerin açılması ve düzenli yürütülmesi de takip edilmeli.


Kürtçenin farklı lehçeleri ve dilsel özellikleri dikkate alınarak öğrencilerin yaşlarına, seviyelerine ve ihtiyaçlarına uygun materyaller geliştirilmeli. Eğitim yalnızca dersin programda görünmesiyle sınırlı kalmamalı; öğrencinin gerçekten öğrenebildiği, kendisini geliştirebildiği bir sürece dönüşmeli. Çünkü bir dili öğrenmek isteyen çocuğa yalnızca “Bu dersi seçebilirsin.” demek yeterli değil. O çocuğun karşısına bir öğretmen, bir kitap ve öğrenebileceği bir sınıf koymak gerekir.


Anadili, insanın dünyayı anlamlandırdığı, duygularını ifade ettiği, kültürel birikimiyle bağ kurduğu ve toplumsal hafızayı taşıdığı temel araçlardan biri. Çocuk, dili aracılığıyla yalnızca kelimeleri öğrenmez; aynı zamanda yaşadığı toplumun hikâyelerini, değerlerini, edebiyatını ve kültürel zenginliğini de tanır.


Bir dilin korunması ve geliştirilmesi, yalnızca o dili konuşan ailelerin veya toplulukların sorumluluğuna bırakılamaz. Eğitim politikalarının da bu süreci …

title: Milano-Cidde seferini yapan yolcu uçağı bomba ihbarı üzerine Roma'ya acil iniş yaptı
content:
Temsili görsel | Fotoğraf: Pixabay

İtalya'nın Milano kentinden Suudi Arabistan'ın Cidde kentine gitmek üzere havalanan yolcu uçağı, yapılan bomba ihbarı üzerine Roma'ya acil iniş yaptı. Güvenlik güçlerince gerçekleştirilen aramalarda ihbarın asılsız olduğu belirlendi.

AA'nın İtalyan basınındaki haberlere dayandırarak verdiği bilgiye göre, Suudi Arabistan merkezli Flynas Havayolunun Milano-Cidde seferini gerçekleştirmek üzere bugün yerel saatle 14.45 civarında Milano Malpensa'dan havalanan "A320" tipi yolcu uçağı, bir süre sonra bomba tehdidi sebebiyle Roma Fiumicino Havalimanına acil iniş yaptı. İçinde 83 yolcu ve 10 mürettebat bulunduğu belirtilen yolcu uçağı, Fiumicino Havalimanına indikten sonra güvenlik kontrollerinden geçirildi. Kontroller neticesinde bomba ihbarının asılsız olduğu anlaşıldı.

Uçağın yolcularını alarak Cidde'ye gitmek üzere Roma'dan ayrılması bekleniyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Fransa: Macron qedexeya derketina derve ragihand; sendîkayan ji bo 24ê Cotmehê û 5ê Mijdarê bang kirin
content:
Hikûmeta Fransayê roja Duşema 19ê Cotmehê ragihand ku dê li herêmên diyarkirî yên bajarên Lille, Douai, Wattignies û Denain ku li bakurê welêt in, ji bo du şevan qedexeya derketina derve bê sepandin.


Biryarên ku bi pejirandina rêveberên herêmî hatine stendin, di şevên 19 û 20ê Cotmehê de saet di 20.00an de dest pê dikin û saet di 06.00an de bi dawî dibin. Sînordarkirinên ku li herêmê hatine ragihandin bi taybetî ji bo kesên temenê wan di bin 18 saliyê de ne û hemû kesan li xwe nagire.


Li Fransayê piştî çalakiyên girseyî hejmara kesên hatine desteserkirin ji 2 hezarî derbas bûn


19 Cotmeh 2026


Sînordarkirin li bajarên din belav bûn


Tedbîrên rejîmê bi çar şaredariyên bakur ve sînordar neman. Li derdora Meydana Komarê (Place de la République) û Les Hallesê yên Parîsa paytext jî di navbera 19ê Cotmehê saet 23:00 û 20ê Cotmehê saet 06:00an de qedexeya derketina derve hat ragihandin. 


Li Parîsê li herêmên diyarkirî xwenîşandan û civîn ji saet 20:00an pê ve hatin qedexekirin. Li herêma Presqu'île ya Lyonê jî di navbera saetên 21:00 û 06:00an de qedexeya derketina derve hat ragihandin. Li hin taxên navendî yên Nice’ê jî ji saet 21:00an pê ve derketina zarok û ciwanan a ji bo kolanan hat sînordarkirin. Li Marsilyayê jî roja duşemê di navbera saetên 12:00 û 20:00an de destûr nehat dayîn ku civîn û xwenîşandan bên kirin.


Serokwezîr Sébastien Lecornu diyar kir ku wî ji waliyan xwestiye ku qedexeyên herêmî û sînordar bixin dewrê. Lecornu aşkere kir ku vebijêrka rewşa awartê jî wekî tedbîreke li ber dest e û ger hewce bike dê bê pêkanîn.


550 hezar an 800 hezar?


Di Şemiya 17ê Cotmehê de li tevahiya Fransayê 110 meş pêk hatin. Li gorî Wezareta Karên Navxweyî 550 hezar kes beşdarî van meşan bûne û li gorî rêxistinên xwendakar û sendîkayan jî 800 hezar kes. Himara ku wezaretê ji bo Parîsê aşkere kiribû 110 hezar bû.


Beşek mezin a meşan bê bûyer bi dawî bûn; lê belê li Parîs, Lille, Lyon, Marsilya û gelek bajarên din di navbera hin kom û polîsan de pevçûn derket, avahiyên dewletê hatin şewitandin û mixaze hatin talankirin. Li Limogesê banê avahiya dîrokî ya şaredariyê di şewatê de hilweşiya.


Li gorî bîlançoya dawî ku Wezîrê Dadê Gérald Darmanin di êvara 19ê Cotmehê de aşkere kir, ji dawiya hefteyê vir ve 2 hezar û 513 kes hatine desteserkirin û 67 kes hatine girtin. Rayedaran diyar kir ku zerar gihîştiye zêdetirî 3 hezar cihên kar an jî hatine talankirin. Darmanin da zanîn ku divê di hin dosyeyan de ji ber “sûcê rêxistinkirî” dema desteserkirinê ji 48 saetan derkeve 72 saetan.


Tevger ji banliyoyên hejar ên Parîsê belav bû


Protesto di meha Îlonê de li banliyoyên bakur ên Parîsê ku piranî çîna karker lê dijîn dest pê kirin. Xwendekarên lîseyê li hemberî kêmbûna mamosteyan, avahiyên kevin ên dibistanan û neyeksaniya di perwerdeyê de serî hildan.


Piştre xwendekarên zanîngehan, xebatkarên perwerdeyê, sendîka û ew beşên ku ji giraniya jiyanê bi gazinc bûn tevlî xwenîşandanan bûn. Hikûmetê soz da ku ji bo kêmasiya kadroyan bê çareserkirin dê nêzîkî 3 hezar mamosteyên bi wesif yên nû ji bo dibistanan were erkdarkirin; lê di budceya perwerdeyê de zêdebûnek çênebû.


Konfederasyona Giştî a Karkeran (CGT), di daxuyaniya xwe ya 19ê Cotmehê de daxwazên xwe yên derbarê perwerde, meaş û mercên jiyanê de wiha rêz kirin: Divê ji bo lîse û zanîngehan zêdetir çavkanî bên dabînkirin, divê mûçe û mûçeya herî kêm bên zêdekirin, divê mûçeyên kesên teqawidbûyî û bursên xwendekaran bên zêdekirin, divê zêdebûna bihayan bên rawestandin, divê dawî li kêmkirinên di tenduristî û xizmetên din ên giştî de bê anîn.


CGTyê di daxuyaniya xwe de wiha got:


“Ji bo tevgereke civakî divê bersiv ne tedbîrên ewlehî û zextkar bin. Bersiv çareseriyên siyasî ye.”


Sendîkayê xwest ku divê meaşên xebatkarên cihên kar ên zirar dîtine jî bi temamî bên dayîn.


Tundkariya polîsan jî mijara lêpirsînê ye


Îdîayên derbarê midxeleya hêzên ewlehiyê de jî mezin dibin. Li Saint-Étienne’ê piştî ku xwenîşanderekî 17 salî ji destê xwe bû, biryargeha IGPNê ku midaxeleyên polîsan lêkolîn dike ket dewrê.


CGTyê diyar kir ku di çalakiyên dawî de xwenîşanderekî din ê 17 salî ji çavê xwe bûye û li Toulouse’ê di kortêja meşê ya sendîkayan de çar rêveberên jin birîndar bûne, ji ber vê yekê daxwaza lêkolîneke serbixwe kir.


Wezîrê Karên Navxweyî Laurent Nuñez qebûl kir ku li hin bajaran polîsan kontrola xwe ya li ser bûyeran winda kiriye. Nunez berpirsiyariya kêmasiyên di amadekariyên ewlehiyê de girt ser milê xwe û îstifaya xwe pêşkêş kir; Serokkomar Emmanuel Macron …

author: Unknown
title: Petites leçons de manipulation par CHATGPT ... et le monde qui se profile derrière
content:
Présentation, discussion et apéro autour du livre "Petites leçons de manipulation par CHATGPT" avec l'autrice Sarah Dubernet à la médiathèque alternative Mille Bâbords (61 rue Consolat) samedi 24 octobre à 18h30.


Samedi 24 octobre à 18h30 la médiathèque des luttes, Mille Bâbords, accueille Sarah Dubernet pour discuter de son livre sur le monde de ChatGPT.


Trois semaines à harceler ChatGPT sur différentes questions qui fâchent ; voici un livre dans lequel l'autrice lui fait dire ce que ses concepteurs et financeurs ne veulent pas qu'il dise : ses censures, sa propagande, l'idéologie transhumaniste et les responsabilités politico-industrielles qui en découlent, les ésotérismes et exotérismes scientifiques, religieux, politiques… Une joute improvisée entre une technocritique et une IA sur le système technicien, son impact et les méthodes d'ingénierie sociale qui lui permettent d'avancer toujours dans le même sens, sans jamais être dérangé.


Ce livre souligne l'importance de protéger notre intelligence, nos questions et nos propres façons d'y répondre face à une machine qui n'a pas vocation à nous éveiller. Si l'autrice a pu lui faire dire tout ça, c'est parce qu'elle connaissait déjà les sujets abordés. Mais ChatGPT expliquera ici que son rôle est au contraire de nous orienter vers un tout autre chemin… les échanges sont étayés de rapports institutionnels.


Ceci n'est pas un livre sur ChatGPT. C'est un livre sur son monde et la façon dont il le sert. Ces échanges constituent un document rare, un témoignage précieux, non seulement sur les mécanismes de l'IA mais aussi sur la nature même du « dialogue » que l'on nous vendra demain comme neutre et transparent alors qu'il sera au contraire de plus en plus « sécurisé »


Mille Bâbords est un lieu de culture politique et de rencontre pour la vie associative et militante marseillaise proposant un service de prêt gratuit pour toustes. La bibliothèque est ouverte au public lors des permanences tous les lundis et les 2ème et 4ème jeudis de 15h à 18h.

title: Stratégies de récupération : Comprendre ses émotions lors d'évènements très stressants
content:
En tant que militant.es, activistes, manifestant.es, nous sommes souvent exposé.es à des stress et de la violence. Au gré des expériences et de leur répétition, cette exposition génère des impacts individuels et collectifs, parfois traumatiques. Pour s'ancrer dans la durée, nos luttes et nous mêmes avons besoin d'anticiper, de comprendre, et de résorber ces impacts.

 A contre-pied de la pensée selon laquelle chacun.e doit se soigner soi-même, on pense qu'il est essentiel d'envisager le soin collectivement, d'en faire une priorité dans nos luttes mais aussi plus largement dans espaces d'organisation et de confiance.


 Comment gérer nos réactions psychologiques et émotionnelles après la violence (policière), la répression ou d'autres expériences très stressantes

 

? Comment apporter du soutien dans ces contextes

 

?


 Cette brochure, éditée par le collectif Soutien et Rétablissement, apporte quelques conseils et outils pour soi et celleux qui nous entourent

title: El movimiento de vivienda ante su Rubicón
content:
Les vemos a los compas de

Briega

, y compartimos por su relevancia para estos días y espacios de lucha


17/10/2026 - Por Alfredo Apilánez


 

“Estos días estamos acampadas en Sol no solo por la defensa del derecho a la vivienda, sino por la creación desde los márgenes de una sociedad no basada en la propiedad privada. Los Centros Sociales Okupados están en la diana de este sistema neoliberal, ya que atacan sus propias bases, la propiedad privada entendida como una forma de acumulación de capital”


CSO La Enredadera


 


Una olla a presión


“El mercado inmobiliario de ninguna manera es un mecanismo infalible, o siquiera inteligente, que conduzca bajo la dirección de alguna mano invisible a ciudades perfectas y equilibradas. Más bien, es un lugar de combate en el que se enfrentan sujetos de muy distinta naturaleza y en el que se impone el más fuerte. El resultado se aleja por tanto de esa Arcadia ideal y se aproxima más al terrenal -por no decir infernal- campo de batalla que constituyen las ciudades capitalistas”


	Samuel Jaramillo


La indignación social frente al drama que supone para las clases populares el acceso a la vivienda ha estallado una vez más. Si bien el levantamiento quincemayista de 2011 no estaba centrado solo en la cuestión de la vivienda, ya que apuntaba hacia un cuestionamiento global -”lo llaman democracia y no lo es”, era uno de sus eslóganes más coreados- del sistema político-económico, su detonante directo fueron las devastadoras consecuencias de la explosión de la burbuja inmobiliaria de 2008.


	Como siempre que se produce una erupción social espontánea, como la que estamos presenciando en los espacios “liberados” de las acampadas, la pregunta pertinente no sería inquerir acerca de las causas que la han provocado, que están meridianamente claras, sino más bien, ¿por qué una revuelta popular de esta intensidad no ocurrió antes? Y es que motivos para un levantamiento de amplias capas de las clases populares, asoladas por el colapso del acceso a la ansiada “seguridad residencial”, no faltaban en absoluto. En el ciclo actual, de presunto “crecimiento” de la economía española, los niveles prohibitivos de los precios inmobiliarios, principalmente de alquiler, impactan de lleno sobre las capas más desvalidas de la inhóspita sociedad neoliberal: jóvenes sin expectativa de heredar; trabajadores condenados a la eterna precariedad; migrantes víctimas de racismo inmobiliario; jubilados con pensiones ínfimas; familias monomarentales o hipotecados insolventes en riesgo de desahucio; todos ellos se ven abocados a la exclusión social causada por la aguda crisis de asequibilidad residencial. Y sus efectos son dramáticos: las cifras de sinhogarismo se han disparado en los últimos años en las grandes ciudades y los asentamientos de tiendas o chabolas proliferan como setas en el corazón de la ciudad-mercancía. Por no mencionar el inframundo del alquiler de habitaciones, bajos sin cédula de habitabilidad e incluso trasteros, caravanas y demás refugios de supervivencia donde se agolpan los excluidos del disfrute de los dones de la sociedad opulenta.


	Como resume ácidamente el exportavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas de Barcelona Jaime Palomera: “

De seguir así, el futuro será que una persona de 40 años con trabajo estable se vea abocada a alquilar una habitación”.


¿Qué decir de la “salud” de una sociedad en la que únicamente el 15% de los menores de 30 años están emancipados -y una gran parte lo logran solo gracias a la ayuda familiar-?


	Nos hallamos pues ante un espacio social “agonístico”, fracturado entre dos grupos antagónicos. Por un lado, la “España de propietarios”: unos 13 millones de hogares propietarios de una sola vivienda -de los cuales 8 tienen la hipoteca pagada-, junto con 4 millones más que son propietarios de 2 o más viviendas, incluyendo a los 2 millones largos de rentistas, la gran mayoría con una sola vivienda alquilada. Y en el otro extremo del arco social, un océano de precariedad en el que pugnan por subsistir los hipotecados “problemáticos”, con dificultades para afrontar las letras mensuales; los inquilinos atrapados de por vida en la “trampa del alquiler” y en el nomadismo habitacional; la mayor parte de la juventud, excluida del préstamo hipotecario y del acceso a un alquiler estable; y, last but not least, la inmensa mayoría de las personas migrantes, condenadas a la infravivienda, el submundo de las habitaciones y el hacinamiento.


El punto de ignición estaba pues listo …

author: Chiara Miraglia
title: CPDP 20th international conference
content:
CPDP (“Computers, Privacy and Data Protection”) is a non-profit platform founded in 2007 by research groups at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel, the Université de Namur, and Tilburg University, later joined by INRIA and the Fraunhofer Institute for Systems and Innovation Research. Today, CPDP is carried by 20 academic centres of excellence from the EU, the US, and beyond. Based in Brussels, CPDP has become a world-leading multidisciplinary conference, convening a global community across research, policy, practice, civil society, and technology to engage with cutting-edge developments in privacy and data protection.

Organiser: 20 academic centres of excellence from the EU, the US, and beyond

The governance of the digital world is fragmented and faces difficult challenges. Technologies that shape our lives develop faster than the means – or even the will – to regulate them for the protection of privacy and other fundamental rights.

What We Owe the Future invites reflection on this contribution. Building on this, it looks ahead to what the future demands of us. What will the next twenty or more years need, and how should we help to build it? What do we owe to those who will inherit the world we shape today? Which principles must endure, which protections cannot be bargained away even when the pressure to relax them is strong, and what responsibilities do the custodians of the present bear towards the future?

The year 2027 marks the twentieth anniversary of CPDP. For twenty years, the conferences have stood at the forefront of efforts to understand and contribute to improving the prospect for governance in this fast-moving digital age. As a community of academics, regulators and policymakers, civil society, industry and legal practitioners, CPDP has cast a bright light on issues, practices and rules, and has offered a forum for debate and the exchange of knowledge across a global landscape. What is worth celebrating is not the annual conference itself, but twenty years of bringing this community together and sustaining it through a period of momentous change.

The people whose lives will extend far into that future should help to design the way forward. CPDP 2027 therefore launches CPDP 20: The Next Generation, which include a team of early-career researchers from across disciplineswho will co-curate the programme and help identify its most pressing questions. This team will identify connections across fields and help to explore issues on the horizon, bringing knowledge and fresh perspectives to bear on developments and their likely consequences that will need to be addressed by policy, governance and other action.

author: Unknown
title: Spagna chiama Italia: casa e finanziarizzazione
content:
La lotta per il diritto alla casa negli ultimi trent’anni è sempre stata un’invarianza della rigidità che le classi subalterne hanno imposto al potere nella più generale tendenza neo liberista di attacco alle condizioni materiali di vita delle persone. 


Da mesi però assistiamo ad un ritorno di questa lotta come centralità politica a livello internazionale. Partendo dall’elezione a New York del nuovo Sindaco Mamdani, passando per la vittoria a Berlino della candidata Linke Elif Eralp, fino alle imponenti mobilitazioni spagnole partite dalla vicenda Maricarmen la lotta per l’accesso alla casa ha saputo diventare nuovamente una spina nel fianco delle élites capitaliste, anche aggredendo i nuovi meccanismi che la speculazione immobiliare ha messo in campo.


Si possono infatti delineare delle nuove  invarianze in questa ondata  di mobilitazione, ossia l’attacco frontale ai meccanismi di finanziarizzazione della casa e dell’abitare. 


La trasformazione della casa in “asset finanziario” ha infatti inasprito le difficoltà di accedere ad affitti proporzionati ai salari reali e innalzato la barriera economica che divide i proletari e il ceto medio dalla possibilità di acquistare una casa.


In tutti i contesti europei e d’oltreoceano il rapporto fra salario e spesa per garantirsi un tetto sopra la testa è letteralmente saltato, facendo esplodere una vera e propria “bomba” sociale. Questo meccanismo di finanziarizzazione della casa è recentemente approdato anche in Italia, dove le lotte per la casa sono storicamente centrali, ma che negli ultimi anni hanno subito molti attacchi mettendone  a rischio le conquiste del passato. L’insorgere di questo nuovo fenomeno però allarga di fatto la base sociale coinvolta dalla lotta anche nel nostro paese. Siamo di fronte ad un nuovo ciclo di opposizione sociale e antagonista su questo ambito della riproduzione popolare?


Anche se è difficile rispondere a questa domanda crediamo sia importante partire primariamente dai meccanismi materiali alla base di questa scommessa, appunto la finanziarizzazione.


Milano, Firenze, Roma, Torino, Bologna

 e molte altre città sono investite da meccanismi di speculazione immobiliare portate avanti dai fondi che a loro volta sono gestiti e comandati da colossi detti società di gestione del risparmio. Questo meccanismo si somma a quelli storici della gentrificazione, della turistificazione e della speculazione immobiliare intorno all’abitare studentesco.


Abbiamo preso spunto per spiegare questo complesso fenomeno da un’ intervista al Professor Alessandro Volpi apparsa recentemente

qui

.


Il mercato è mosso dalle società di gestione del risparmio che si occupano di immobiliare. Oggi queste hanno un peso importante e sono in sintesi una settantina ed hanno un patrimonio immobiliare che si aggira intorno 145 miliardi di euro. 


Esiste di fatto una grossa concentrazione nella capacità di gestire il patrimonio, infatti tendenzialmente 10 società detengono quasi metà dell’importo complessivo.


 Le società di gestione del risparmio non gestiscono direttamente il patrimonio immobiliare (es Fabrica sgr, Investire sgr), ma generano fondi immobiliari, i quali sono legati a specifici progetti immobiliari, sia di recupero che di acquisto di aree già edificate o di costruzione di nuovi complessi di edifici.


Esistono più o meno 750 fondi immobiliari legati a queste 70 sgr, le 10 più importanti ne hanno di conseguenza una quota maggiore. Quindi diversi fondi immobiliari, nella stessa città o in diverse metropoli italiane, possono usufruire della stessa strategia dovuta al fatto che una singola società di gestione del risparmio ha molti fondi a disposizione.


Il fondo, in particolare, si occupa di decidere i progetti sull’area urbana di riferimento e della gestione del patrimonio immobiliare che possiede. 


Essendo che una sgr guadagna dalle commissioni che gli pagano i fondi, essi vendono le loro quote per finanziarsi.  Fino a poco tempo fa la  tendenza era quella di vendere anche a risparmiatori benestanti di fascia medio alta, ma comunque a patrimonio limitato, se paragonato a grandi agglomerati finanziari, ora  i fondi vengono frammentati e divisi  in quote vendute principalmente a investitori istituzionali. Questi possono essere ad esempio fondi pensione e casse di previdenza degli ordini professionali o altri con grandi capacità. Così facendo vi è quindi un  allargamento della base di reperibilità delle risorse per il fondo, accentrando grosse …

title: Veganer Meerestierkalender für 2027 von matabooks und PETA – für mehr Tierrechte
content:
Werbung | Kalender bzw. Jahresplaner sind sehr beliebt – aber leider nicht immer vegan. Das Unternehmen matabooks aus Dresden stellt vegane Bücher und Planer aus Graspapier her. In einem Gemeinschaftsprojekt von matabooks und PETA Deutschland ist für das Jahr 2027 erneut ein wunderschöner Kalender entstanden, der in der Farbe „Cosmic Blue“ erhältlich ist und sich inhaltlich dem Schutz der

Meerestiere

 widmet.


Veganer Kalender in der Farbe „Cosmic Blue“ von matabooks in Zusammenarbeit mit PETA


matabooks hat für 2027 den Jahresplaner „Samaya“ in der Farbe „Cosmic Blue“ entworfen – dieser enthält eindrückliche Zeichnungen von Petra Heider (una.kritzolina) von unterschiedlichen

Walen

 wie Buckelwalen, aber auch von Walhaien, Seepferdchen,

Quallen

 und anderen Bewohnern des Ozeans.


Berührende Illustrationen in maritimen Aquarell-Design zeigen die faszinierenden Tiere auf beeindruckende Weise – und machen damit auf die

Rechte der unzähligen Tiere

 aufmerksam, die in den weltweiten Meeren leben und alle von Fischereinetzen bedroht sind. Darüber hinaus gibt PETA Tipps, wie Sie Meerestiere schützen können.


Der Jahresplaner „Samaya“ in der Farbe „Cosmic Blue“ ist zweisprachig (Deutsch/Englisch) erhältlich und eignet sich perfekt als Kalender, Bullet Journal, Termin- oder Wochenplaner oder als Notiz- und Tagebuch. Schutz von Meerstieren

Interessent:innen finden den Kooperationskalender im Onlineshop von matabooks unter dem Stichwort Samaya – Farbe: Cosmic Blue solange der Vorrat reicht.

author: AbdouMaliq Simone
title: The radical openness of the popular economy
content:
Urban Africa is constantly finding ways to thicken urban life with new resourcefulness: from makeshift maker labs to the vast associations of traders with their own home-grown, expansive financial systems — where remittances circulate alongside locally generated credit and savings — to self-generated webs of electricity and water provisioning under the radar, to neighborhood investments in shared containers of imported goods, to local circuits of production and distribution of foodstuffs, intermingled with diverse labor arrangements across regions and borders. These are what we call popular economies.

Residents inhabit environments replete with different land statuses, regulatory frameworks, histories of economic specialization, repositories of cultural memory, behavioral styles, and social arrangements. Urban popular economies entail how these various components of an archive are pieced together and interrelated to produce specific mobilities and access to resources and opportunities. It is a move toward an expanded diversification of how accumulation, social reproduction, and livelihood get built. African cities are renowned for their informal sectors, self-built neighborhoods, as well as histories of piracy, brigandage, circumvention, smuggling, and subversion. The popular economy intersects with these elements in a continuous unfolding and elaboration of more overarching efforts to create distinctive processes of urbanization within and outside the hegemonic structures of capital accumulation and political domination.

In April 2026, researchers and activists from various African cities gathered in Nairobi to reflect on the popular economy. They explored questions related to orientations, practices, political engagements, and spatial arrangements that might offer ways to inhabit contemporary urban conditions differently. If the future, as a horizon of multiple disjunctions and possibilities, is captured by the reign of probabilities and adversarial networks, then what is the terrain of the improbable? Given the multiple temporalities that characterize territorial operations underpinning popular economies, can we think of a way of life not indebted to calculation, redemption, or culmination?

Popular economies and their various forms of organization seek different ways of inhabiting the present and thus recuperating the insurgencies of both pasts and futures. Euro-American notions of the human have long emphasized a progressive, developmentalist trajectory of improvement and enhanced capacity: a life moving toward a straight timeline, toward the fulfillment of unbounded human potential. This has intensified global turbulence, unsettled ways of living among the majority, and withheld the time needed for society to be a living force in itself — generating vulnerabilities and fragmentation on a planetary scale.

As Timothy Mitchell argues in his book

The Alibi of Capital: How We Broke the Earth to Steal the Future on the Promise of a Better Tomorrow

, this temporal movement acts to constitute a future from which a wide range of payments can be extracted; a future already encumbered by debts continuously owed to those who acquired, at a discount, the rights to those payments. This is a violence done to time itself, one that limits future dispositions to a mere surplus of the present. The future is foreclosed, not primarily through the threat of extinction, but rather through an investment in what can be extracted from that future and monetized now.

This same logic operates at the level of knowledge. Dominant knowledge functions as information: in

Achille Mbembe’s

 terms, a juxtaposition of words stripped of ambiguity, which reduces the capacities of all localities when circulated and imposed. Pattern recognition becomes geared toward preemption; time is reoriented to the number of steps a program needs to reach completion, and space to the memory required to scale a specific function to execute a program — all of this coupled with increasingly enormous expenditures of energy, as

Wolfgang Ernst

 and

Rob Kitchin

 have shown. Localized knowledge has been generalized to the scale of what

Bernard Stiegler

 called a biospheric locality, an upscaling made possible by reducing knowledge to data amenable to computation and by eliminating whatever resists that reduction. Localities become points along the same line, subject to measures of comparability and proportion — the more or less — with the subsequent fight …

author: Sergey Eledinov
title: Sudan: Nobody Hands Over a Gun for Nothing
content:
On 6 October, Sudan’s army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan

said again

 that there would be no negotiations with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti,

or ‘any other party’

, and that the war would go on until victory. A day earlier, Donald Trump’s envoy Massad Boulos

had disclosed a meeting with him in Egypt

. Washington is pushing a 90-day humanitarian truce and, according to

sources cited by Reuters

, made Burhan’s visa for the UN General Assembly conditional on it.


In 1996, General Alexander Lebed

told the journalist Yevgeny Kiselyov

 on Russia’s NTV that ‘all wars, even hundred-year wars, end in negotiations and peace all the same’. He then asked whether it was worth piling up mountains of corpses only to sit down and negotiate anyway. In August that year, at Khasavyurt, he signed

a truce

 himself; the

peace treaty

 followed in May 1997. The troops left, the other side kept its weapons, and the question of Chechnya’s status was put off until the end of 2001. Three years later the war was back.


Khasavyurt is remembered as a breather that the enemy exploited. But a breather works for everyone. The second war was triggered by the

raid into Dagestan

 in August 1999. It came from the side that considered itself the winner, and it was led by the field commanders Shamil Basayev and Khattab, not by Maskhadov, whose signature was on the peace. We cannot say which pushes harder back to war: revanchism born of the bitterness of defeat, or the euphoria of victory.


Burhan sees the breather from one side. In his view, the calls for a truce

coincided with attempts

 to let the RSF expand its territory. He is right about one thing: what he is being offered is not a peace plan. The truce proposed by the Quad (the US, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt) is designed for two and has still not been agreed. But Burhan has no peace plan either. His condition is that the RSF first

leave the cities and gather in designated areas of Darfur

, and only then comes a truce. That is a plan for victory written up as a precondition.


The principle and its price


The mediators have a principle. The Quad

set it down in September 2025

: the transition must not be ‘controlled by any warring party’. This autumn Washington went further. On 15 September Boulos

said

 that ‘there is no future for any of the two leaders in the country’, and on 22 September the State Department

declared

 that neither the army nor the RSF, nor their leaders, represent legitimate constitutional governance: ‘they rule through force of arms alone.’ As a principle, this is easy to support. It is harder to picture what it looks like in practice.


Yet it is the army and the RSF that Washington is asking to sign the truce, and in early October Boulos met Burhan. This is not ambivalence. Legitimacy is a question for national reconciliation, and a truce cannot settle it. The Americans want to hand power back to civilians. But those who hold the weapons are not going to give them up for nothing.


That is rational, though rational is not the same as right. Barbara Walter

described this logic

 in 1997: for an armed group, its weapons are the only guarantee that a deal will be honoured, and disarming leaves it defenceless. Civil wars therefore almost never end in a settlement unless a third party guarantees it.


The alternative is to take the guns by force. The Sahel is trying, and it is not going well. In November 2023 Mali’s army, with Wagner,

took Kidal

; in

January 2024

 Bamako tore up the 2015 Algiers peace accord; in April 2026 it lost Kidal. On 6 October the army went back in after the Azawad Liberation Front announced a ‘strategic and controlled withdrawal’; the armed groups say there was no fight. Force takes towns. It does not take the guns.


Who holds the guns


In Sudan the guns are not held by only two sides. Fighting alongside the army are the

Joint Force

 of former Darfuri rebels, the movements of Minni Minawi and Gibril Ibrahim, together with the

Sudan Shield Forces

 of Abu Aqla Kikl, who defected from the RSF in 2024, and a host of militias. Fighting alongside the RSF is Abdelaziz al-Hilu’s SPLM-North, with its own command and its own territory. Abdel Wahid al-Nur’s SLM, in the Jebel Marra mountains, has joined neither side. A signature by two generals does not bind them, just as Maskhadov’s signature did not bind Basayev. author: Mada Masr
title: State security prosecution summons Mada Masr editor-in-chief for investigation
content:
Lina Attalah, Mada Masr’s editor-in-chief, received a summons today from the Supreme State Security Prosecution to attend a questioning session on Wednesday, October 21. The summons did not say why she is being questioned.


The new investigation, Case 9072/2026, is the sixth case brought against Mada Masr, its journalists and its editor-in-chief in the past six years. The most recent was in August 2025, when the security prosecution released Attalah on LE30,000 bail. She was questioned at the time on charges of “broadcasting false news” and “using a website without a license,” based on a National Security Agency investigation report, in relation to a Mada Masr story on prisoners’ complaints of abuse in detention facilities.

When

asked

why she trusted the sources cited in the story, Attalah said she had abided by professional journalistic standards and had acted in the public interest.

 She also pointed to the legally protected right to inform authorities of events through publication, noting that the outlet presents a full range of viewpoints.

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: The New Scramble for Africa
content:
Something important is happening across the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa. Wars that appear local are drawing in actors from increasingly far away. Ports built for commerce acquire military uses. Gold mined in conflict zones travels through international financial centers. Drones purchased abroad alter wars. Governments negotiate with foreign powers while those same powers cultivate armed groups or parallel authorities elsewhere.


Sudan, Libya, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Somalia, Somaliland and Yemen are usually discussed as separate crises. Look more closely and the connections become difficult to ignore. A

 

United Nations investigation

 found that forces aligned with Khalifa Haftar helped move Colombian fighters through Libya to support Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces. Sudanese gold travels toward the Gulf, while


Chatham House has documented

 the importance of the UAE to the regional gold economy. In western Ethiopia, a

 

Reuters investigation

 found a large training camp for fighters intended for the RSF, with reliable sources saying the UAE financed the facility and provided trainers and logistical support. 


These are not isolated developments. They point toward a changing system of power around the Red Sea.


What is emerging is not another Berlin Conference. Foreign governments are not openly dividing Africa into colonies, and African governments are not passive spectators. They bargain, invite investment, seek weapons and sometimes use outside powers against domestic or regional rivals. But something more than ordinary diplomacy is taking place.


One striking change is the growing importance of powers once treated as secondary actors in African geopolitics. The United Arab Emirates, Turkey and Israel do not possess the worldwide reach of the old European empires. Yet wealth, military technology, commercial networks and strategic geography allow these middle powers to exercise influence far beyond their borders.


They are also flexible about how that influence is exercised. A government can be the useful partner in one country, a paramilitary organization in another, a parallel authority somewhere else, and a commercial company across several of them. The relationship need not be ideological, and the partner need not even be a state. Strategic usefulness can be enough.


The UAE provides perhaps the clearest example. In Sudan, it has been supporting the RSF.


In Libya, it became an important external supporter of Khalifa Haftar’s eastern forces.


Reuters has documented

 earlier UN findings that the UAE helped Haftar’s forces build their air power, while Turkey supplied drones and air defenses to the government in Tripoli.


The Sudan and Libya stories have since begun to merge. The


UN Panel of Experts on Libya

 found that Colombian fighters transited through Haftar-controlled territory to support the RSF and described Libya as an operational, logistical and tactical base.


Gold reveals the economic side of the same system.


Chatham House

 describes gold as a major driver of Sudan’s conflict. Between 2012 and 2022, according to

 figures examined by Chatham House

, the UAE imported 2,569 tonnes of African gold that African countries themselves did not record as exports, worth approximately $115 billion.


The connection between gold and armed power is not abstract. The


U.S. Treasury

 sanctioned UAE-based companies connected to the RSF network. It said AZ Gold purchased Sudanese gold apparently for the benefit of the RSF and transported it to Dubai.


Money, weapons and military support can therefore move toward African conflicts while gold and other resources move outward. The old colonial economy required foreign administrators. The contemporary system does not necessarily need them. Governments, armed groups, mining companies, traders, port operators and financial intermediaries can perform different parts of the process.


A recent


Financial Times investigation

 traced a much wider Emirati expansion involving ports, mining, agriculture and infrastructure across Africa. A port can be a commercial asset, logistics hub, source of political leverage and, under different circumstances, military platform.


It is here that the idea of a new scramble for Africa becomes useful.


The old scramble sought possession of territory. The emerging one can operate at a distance. An outside power does not necessarily need to govern the mine, occupy the port or administer the population. It needs …

author: ROAPE
title: Eusi Kwayana (1925-2026)
content:
Eusi Kwayana was born Sydney King, as he was known initially for his first, more than two decades in public life. In 1968 he took on his African name which in Swahili means ‘Black man of Guyana.’


Eusi Kwayana was a founding father of post-colonial independence Guyana and Caribbean politics and was associated with the triumvirate of personalities that shaped them: Cheddi Jagan, Forbes Burnham, and Walter Rodney. He came to write the anthems of the three parties they led. Yet his own contributions to the Black and global radical traditions are still being recognized and recorded. This will be challenging in an environment where he receives national and regional honors for being a mere educator, writer, and cultural activist. It’s undeniable; he was a revolutionary.


What does it mean that Eusi Kwayana was a revolutionary? He was a campaigner against white supremacy, empire, capitalism, patriarchy, and ecological destruction. More than that, where he led breakthroughs against colonialism that denied Guyana, the Caribbean, and the Global South self-government, at the post-colonial independence moment he continued to confront the African and Caribbean political class, whether aristocratic or progressive. As historian and political activist, he always wished for everyday people to directly hold the reins of society. Of course, it was a matter of positioning ourselves to bring this about. His strategies of what to do and how to do it, must be revisited.


Detained When Guyana was Occupied by Anglo-American Imperialism


Eusi was detained when the Cheddi Jagan-led People’s Progressive Party (PPP) was overthrown by Anglo-American empire after winning election to Guyana’s colonial legislature in 1953. The country was occupied for 133 days. Before the Cuban Revolution of 1959, the PPP of Guyana was seen as a major threat to US and British hegemony during the Cold War in the Western hemisphere.


Eusi, with Rory Westmaas and Martin Carter, were perceived as the ‘ultra-left’ of the PPP.  In 1956, the split with Cheddi Jagan came, not over disagreements about commitments to a multi-racial party or movement. Rather, when Eusi and others advanced and defended the inclusion of Guyana in the movement for West Indian Federation. It was a permanent concern.


Multi-Racial Unity, Black Autonomy, and Caribbean Federation


This was part of an unfolding process of awareness. Cheddi Jagan was a socialist cosmopolitan when he faced the wider public. But he was also an ethnic leader of the Indo-Guyanese. Eusi concluded that it was no creative conflict to be an advocate for Afro-Guyanese as well. And it was important to address his Afro-Guyanese constituency

within the hearing

 of the Indo-Guyanese.


In 1959, Eusi became friendly with CLR James and Selma James in Trinidad at the height of the movement for colonial freedom led by Eric Williams’s People’s National Movement (PNM). He learned some important things about political journalism and activism in dialogue with CLR as he was editing

The Nation,

and Eusi was responsible for the People’s National Congress’s (PNC)

The New Nation

in Guyana.


Making Guyana a Global Refuge


In 1961, Eusi founded African Society for Racial Equality (ASRE) with the scientist H.H. Nicholson, known as ‘Vigilance’, and in 1964, co-founded African Society for Cultural Relations with Independent Africa (ASCRIA). With his wife

Tchaiko Kwayana

, an African American from Georgia in the US, who made her own mark as a teacher in New York and California, and her own sojourns to Nigeria, Ghana, and Latin America, Eusi pioneered the African cultural revolution in the Western Hemisphere, and was a transmission belt for African Americans and continental Africans finding a refuge from white supremacy and empire in Guyana as they pursued self-reliance and cooperative living. He was instrumental in making powerful ties between Ghana and Guyana.


It was Eusi that in 1966 gave Forbes Burnham the idea for Guyana being known as the ‘cooperative republic’ at official independence. In the early 1970s, Eusi was a supporter of the most dedicated cooperatives in the hinterland, such as the one at Marudi led by Joe Maxwell. The most dynamic cooperatives would be repressed by the state before the famous Jonestown fiasco.


An Original Educator of the African World


Eusi’s travels in Africa in 1964-65 and 1969 brought him to Nigeria, Mali, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia, Ghana, and Guinea-Conakry.  As a leader …

author: Mzi Velapi
title: ‘End hunger, stop climate harm’: protesters take demands to Parliament
content:
About 200 residents and activists marched through the streets of Cape Town on World Food Day, calling for the government to end hunger and stop climate harm. Organised by the Climate Justice Charter Movement (CJCM) and the South African Food Sovereignty Campaign and allied partners, the protesters handed the memorandum to parliament where they called for the adoption of the People’s Sovereignty Act No 1 of 2024, a People’s Sovereignty Policy and an immediate ban on pesticides.


At least 14 to 15 million people in South Africa live below the food poverty line and experience regular food insecurity, while 11,000 children die due to malnutrition every year, and 10-million tonnes of food go to waste every year, according to Unite Against Hunger.


A recent report by the International Panel of Experts on Sustainable Food Systems (IPES-Food) found that nearly 1.4-billion people in the world work in the agrifood sector, including farmworkers. Despite their number and the vital role they play, they are among the most exploited workers in the world.


Speaking to

Elitsha

, Kara Mackay from Women on Farms Project said that women farmworkers bear the brunt of lack of access to food because of the unequal power relations that govern their relationship with farm owners. “The issue of poor wages and the high prices of food is linked to unequal power relations where the farmer is seen as the producer and the farmworkers as merely consumers,” she said.


Retired farmworker, Magrieta Prins from De Doorns said that farmers deny workers the opportunity to grow their own food by controlling their access to water. “Farmworkers do not have land to grow their own food but even in instances where they are allowed to do so, the farmer controls their use of water and in most times just deny them access to water,” Prins said.


A seasonal farmer from Ceres, Charmaine Lynx said that not having access to water impacts on their ability to produce their own food. “The social grants play a crucial role during off season. I have to look after my daughter and family during off season as I share my AllPay grant with them. Some have to resort to recycling as a means to put food on the table for their families,” said Prins.


One of the demands of the protesters is the implementation of the climate emergency social contract, that requires the government and the corporations which promote and profit from fossil fuels, pay the price.


Communities on the coastal areas of the Western Cape are experiencing severe weather that has impacted on their ability to feed their families. Fisher woman from Buffels Baai in the Southern Cape, Sarah Niemand said that the weather patterns have resulted in cold waters and fish migrating away. “For the past two months we struggled to get fish because they are scarce because of the bad weather,” she said.


Addressing the protesters outside of parliament, activist and academic, Vishwas Satgar said that southern Africa is heating at twice the global average rate, pushing the region toward an estimated 3°C of warming as global mitigation targets face severe shortfalls. “We are here to tell this government that we are not going to pay the price for their failure of leadership to prepare this country. Climate signs are telling us that El Niño is coming and the last El Niño resulted in collapsed food systems and pushed the food prices up as a result,” Satgar said.


Responding to the memorandum, Mfuneko Toyana said that the government will announce additional funding to respond to El Niño, when the minister of finance tables the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement next week.


Satgar responded to this news: “It does not add up, this is the government that is squeezing the working class and the poor in this country. They are driving austerity meaures, and this is just a modest gesture given that the problem is big and El Niño is coming.”
