author: Charlotte Reck
title: Amazon ‘Uses AI in Warehouses to Predict Whether Workers Will Join Unions’
content:
Amazon has been accused of using AI to track employees and rank how likely they are to form unions.


The online retail giant uses a tool called Atlas in an apparent bid to predict acts of dissent by workers in the UK, the US and Canada, a

document

 released as part of court proceedings between Amazon and Canadian union Unifor show. 


The document, which appears to be a training manual for company leaders, has led the

GMB Union to accuse Amazon

 of using “Orwellian” AI tools to spy on workers. 


“Workers deserve to be able to work free of the fear of excessive surveillance,” said GMB organiser Rachel Fagan.“If Amazon bosses are using Atlas or similar AI-fuelled systems in the UK, the British public deserve to know”.


The document also contains pointers for managers on listening to workers’ concerns without “over-sympathising”. 


Atlas gives warehouses a risk score of between 100 and 900 for union activity, with a lower score meaning it believes workers are more likely to unionise. A higher score is “better” for leaders at the company, the document says.


This “makes it clear that they think the union is bad”, Michael Newman, a partner at London-based law firm Leigh Day, told openDemocracy. 


Atlas is described in the document as a “labour risk framework to clarify how Amazon evaluates emerging workforce issues, labour union targets and internal or external labour threats.”


It outlines a five-tier scale – where tier one denotes workplace disruption and “imminent” worker action, while tier five merits “no immediate perceived risk”. 


The scale can be used to determine staffing decisions, resource planning and action to “mitigate risks” while avoiding reduced productivity or profits, the document says.


In the UK, two Amazon warehouses have been listed in tier one, while 14 others in the US and Canada were named in this high-risk tier.


At a warehouse near Coventry named BHX4, there has been an “active organising campaign” while previous strike action has been recorded at another at EMA4 Sutton Coldfield. 


Newman said that the findings relay “a very different story” to Amazon’s claim that it has no desire to deter workers from joining a union.  


An Amazon spokesperson denied that Atlas is used to counter union activity and refuted the characterisation of the technology as surveillance of individual employees. 


“This is site/building level activity only,” they told openDemocracy, adding that the company does not “track individual employees’ opinions, affiliations or union membership”.


Atlas is used to “help us understand where associates need more support and to ensure we’re addressing issues that they raise”, they added.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: ‘Burnout and hardship’: Nunavut teachers struggle with loss of student support workers
content:
Teachers in Nunavut have access to fewer student support assistants this year after school-related requests became ineligible for funding under the Inuit Child First Initiative.


The federal funding program, similar to Jordan’s Principle, is designed to ensure Inuit children across Canada have equal access to health, social and educational supports.


In the 2024-25 school year, the Inuit Child First Initiative allowed Nunavut’s 27 district education authorities to pay the salaries of 88 casual student support workers. The staff worked in elementary and high schools, according to figures provided to Nunatsiaq News by Nunavut’s Education Department.


Last year, the department approved 75 casual workers, said department spokesperson Kuthula Matshazi in an email.


He declined to say how many casual support workers are working in Nunavut schools this year. Instead, he characterized it as a “limited number.”


“When that funding was readily available,” said Nunavut Teachers Association president Justin Matchett in an interview, “there were a lot of schools that were accessing that and getting additional support staff.”


Student support workers join classroom teachers to help deliver curriculum, with a particular focus on students who require accommodations.


In February 2025, Indigenous Services Canada annoucned that requests for student support assistants would no longer be eligible for funding under the Inuit Child First Initiative, except for in exceptional cases.


Nunavut’s classrooms look very different without that funding, Matchett said.


“There’s a lot of behaviour needs, a lot of medical diagnoses that need and deserve special attention,” he said. “It definitely causes a lot of stress, burnout and hardship on the teachers when they’re trying to manage all of that on top of teaching the curriculum.”


The Nunavut Employees Union, which represents the GN’s permanent student support staff, isn’t opposed to the government hiring fewer casual student support assistants, said president Jason Rochon in an email.


He has been concerned about support staff roles going to non-unionized workers.


“These were casual, lesser paid and non-unionized roles for essentially the same work as unionized [support] positions under our collective agreement with the GN,” said Rochon.


“All [support] positions should be unionized and covered by the NEU’s collective agreement with the Government of Nunavut,” he added. “We encourage the employer to ensure that enough [support workers] are hired across Nunavut schools.”


Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty promised in November 2025 to revamp Inuit Child First Initiative and make it permanent. She

announced

 a $115-million, one-year extension in February.


The $115-million top up ensures “continuity” while the department works on a long-term approach for Inuit Child First Initiative, said Carolane Gratton, spokesperson for the department, in an email to Nunatsiaq News.


In the interim, all funding for school-related needs are reviewed on a case to case basis.


“Although the Inuit Child First Initiative can support child-specific education-related requests, such as psycho educational assessments, technology supports, and tutoring to meet individual student needs, it is not intended to replace existing federal/provincial or territorial universal programs,” Gratton said.

author: anred
title: De España a Francia y de Portugal a Italia, pasando por Albania: estalla la juventud europea sin futuro
content:
Foto: Martin Barzilai


En alianza con otros sectores y movimientos de otras edades y trayectorias, una juventud politizada y harta de no tener futuro trae a Europa los ecos de las revoluciones de la Generación Z.

Por Martín Cúneo (@MartinCuneo78), para El Salto Diario.


Desde mayo de 2025 y hasta julio de este año, la llamada Generación Z, jóvenes nacidos cerca del cambio de milenio, impulsaron o se convirtieron en la cara más visible de revueltas que sacudieron la vida política de países tan dispersos y diversos como Bangladesh, Nepal, Indonesia, Marruecos, Madagascar, Perú, Bulgaria, Filipinas, Camerún, Timor Oriental o India.


En

Nepal

,

Madagascar

,

Bangladesh

 y

Bulgaria

 contribuyeron o causaron directamente la caída del Gobierno. En otros casos, las revueltas consiguieron que se retiraran privilegios (

Timor

 o

Indonesia

), conquistaron aumentos nunca vistos en servicios públicos (

Marruecos

) o lograron dimisiones de ministros (

India

).


No fueron solo los jóvenes quienes se movilizaron, pero en todos estos casos se convirtieron en el centro de coaliciones más amplias con otros sectores descontentos para protestar contra la desigualdad, los privilegios, la corrupción, el deterioro del nivel de vida, la pobreza y la crisis económica.


Esta fórmula se está replicando este otoño en muchos países europeos, una región que apenas había sentido los movimientos sísmicos de aquellas revueltas.


Aunque las protestas por la vivienda tuvieron en un inicio un carácter intergeneracional, las acampadas fueron protagonizadas por jóvenes que ya nacieron en el siglo XXI y que miran con recelo su futuro


España, al igual que hace 15 años, se ha convertido en foco de inspiración para otros países con la revuelta por la vivienda iniciada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas tras el desahucio de Maricarmen el pasado 23 de septiembre. Aunque las protestas tuvieron en un inicio un carácter intergeneracional, las acampadas fueron y siguen siendo protagonizadas por jóvenes que nacieron ya en el siglo XXI

, 

que no superan los 25 años y miran con recelo su futuro, su capacidad de independizarse o de construir una vida propia.


El movimiento de vivienda —que va mucho más allá de la Generación Z— ha conseguido establecer alianzas con otros grandes movimientos de los últimos años: la lucha por la

sanidad

 y por la

educación públic

a. Estas causas han confluido en las últimas semanas en movilizaciones históricas con una importante presencia de trabajadores y pensionistas, pero también de una marea de jóvenes nacidos en este siglo, una diversidad que desafía las definiciones simplistas. Las movilizaciones en el marco de la huelga educativa en Madrid, especialmente en la Universidad Complutense han dejado imágenes de encierros, bloqueos, piquetes, manifestaciones, protestas y

una represión policial desatada

.


Las alianzas se han extendido también al mundo del trabajo con la convocatoria de la

huelga general del 11N

 y la creación de centenares de comités para la preparación del paro. Aunque no lo explican todo, tanto en la vivienda como en la educación, la llamada Generación Z y en algunos casos la Generación Alfa —nacidos después de 2010— están jugando un papel determinante con muestras de una juventud mucho más politizada y dispuesta a movilizarse de lo que los estereotipos y los grandes medios apuntaban. Más claro aún es el caso de Francia y la revuelta de los liceos.


Francia


Además de España, el otro 

gran polo de protestas

 en Europa es Francia, donde la respuesta de los estudiantes al paquete de recortes ha vuelto a poner al primer ministro Emmanuel Macron ante una crisis de Gobierno. El movimiento iniciado por los estudiantes de secundaria del norte de París —pertenecientes más bien bien a la Generación Alfa— se extendió a más de mil institutos, llegó a las universidades y prendió en los sindicatos de trabajadores y las asociaciones de padres y madres de alumnos. El martes 6 de octubre, más de medio millón de personas salía a las calles para protestar contra las medidas neoliberales de Macrón.

author: cnt.es
title: CNT convoca huelga general el próximo 11 de noviembre contra los intereses especulativos que golpean a la clase trabajadora
content:
El clamor popular ha señalado el camino. El próximo 11 de noviembre, la clase trabajadora volverá a mostrar su músculo a través de una de sus herramientas más contundentes: la huelga general. La Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT) y el resto de los sindicatos llaman a un paro de 24 horas en todos los sectores para luchar contra el parasitismo del rentismo y los salarios escuálidos que abocan a las clases populares a una vida de sometimiento y explotación.


Desde CNT nunca olvidaremos de dónde venimos. Somos todas aquellas encarceladas por luchar por sus derechos, somos los padres y madres que se partieron el lomo por intentar que las generaciones futuras tuvieran una vida mejor. Y aquí estamos, dispuestos y dispuestas a volver a defender en la calle, en las aulas y en los centros de trabajo todo lo que es nuestro, todo lo que nos ganamos únicamente con el sudor de nuestra frente.


La situación de la vivienda en España ha sido la chispa que ha encendido toda una hoguera. Ni siquiera un Gobierno pretendidamente de izquierdas ha sido capaz en ocho años de mejorar y proteger la vida de la mayoría social. A las huelgas en sectores como la educación y la sanidad, ahora se suma el colectivos de vivienda, cada vez más organizado y concienciado de los culpables de su miseria. Todos los golpes que recibe la clase trabajadora parten del mismo lugar: un empresariado obcecado en exprimir al máximo a sus empleados y empleadas que no duda en recurrir a los elementos más reaccionarios de la sociedad para defender al capital.


Lo vemos todos los días. Mientras la Policía se abraza con la ultraderecha y el Ejército tortura a migrantes en Ceuta, grupos neonazis crecen al albor de una apatía y de un nulo entusiasmo que se expande entre algunas personas de las generaciones más jóvenes. Todos ellos se esfuerzan día y noche por arrebatar cualquier atisbo de avance en materia antirracista, feminista y antifascista. No lo conseguirán.


Como recalca la secretaria General de CNT a nivel estatal, Nieves Román, “desde la CNT entendemos que la vivienda es un derecho y no una mercancía”. “No podemos aceptar que las necesidades básicas de la ciudadanía estén subordinadas al beneficio económico de grandes propietarios, fondos de inversión, empresas inmobiliarias o intereses especulativos”, añade.


Las experiencias de organización de inquilinas, vecinas y trabajadoras demuestran que, frente a los problemas que sufrimos individualmente, la respuesta está en la solidaridad, el apoyo mutuo y la acción colectiva. En cada plaza, en cada grito, en cada pancarta a favor de una vida mejor para la mayoría florece un mundo nuevo.


Román subraya que la lucha por la vivienda es también una lucha por los derechos de las trabajadoras. Desde la CNT pensamos que todo está relacionado: la precariedad laboral, la degradación de los servicios públicos, el encarecimiento de la vida y la destrucción del medio ambiente, entre otros motivos, generan malestar entre una población que ya no aguanta más.


La huelga general es el momento de que la clase trabajadora demuestre de lo que es capaz, todo aquello que produce con sus manos, que sin ella todo se para. Nuestra fuerza está en el apoyo mutuo, en la autogestión, en la acción directa, y el 11 de noviembre lo volveremos a demostrar.


Desde la CNT hacemos un llamamiento a la clase trabajadora en su conjunto para que, organizada, se levante contra los ataques, en muchas ocasiones mortales, del capital. Contra el fascismo, el casero, los fondos buitre, el empresariado, la progresía tibia que besa el liberalismo más atroz, los sindicatos vendidos, las promesas vacías predicadas desde los púlpitos políticos, vamos a la huelga general.


Contra el patrón y el capital, a la huelga general.


La entrada

CNT convoca huelga general el próximo 11 de noviembre contra los intereses especulativos que golpean a la clase trabajadora

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Sue Bull
title: Unionists discuss defending the CFMEU against Victorian Labor’s assault
content:
A public meeting organised by the Defend the Unions – Defend the CFMEU (DUDC) on October 14 drew 100 unionists and solidarity activists who discussed the federal and Victorian Labor’s attacks on unions and called for a fightback to defend the Construction Forestry Mining and Employees Union (CFMEU).

Leaders, activists and veterans from the Building Industry Group unions, the Maritime Union of Australia, which hosted the event, the Retail and Fast Food Workers Union (RAFFWU) and a number of other unions attended.

It was billed as a chance for militant unionists to assess the challenges for workers ahead of the Victorian elections and Victorian Labor’s decision to appoint a royal commission aimed at destroying the CFMEU.

A panel of speakers from the CFMEU and RAFFWU said while the challenges workers face may seem insurmountable, sticking together, showing leadership and rebuilding solidarity could help all build the fight back.

Loukas Kakogiannis, Secretary of RAFFWU, outlined how the union would have been disbanded if Labor had not recently withdrawn its union-busting bill, after massive pressure. RAFFWU, local Trades Halls, other unions and progressive political parties defeated the bill through a campaign of “solidarity”, he said.

Nigel Davies, former interim CFMEU Branch Executive Officer, spoke about the human cost of federal Labor’s two-year attack on the CFMEU, including the high-profile arrests of CFMEU organisers. Davies was sacked in May by the CFMEU Administrator, after four months in office. He described the dawn raids by police with guns drawn, on homes where small children were still asleep, saying it was “nothing more than a witch hunt” and largely for minor offences.

Davies also criticised the CFMEU Administration’s narrow criteria for CFMEU members to receive legal support if they were called before the royal commission.

Craig Johnston, a former Australian Manufacturing Workers Union leader, now a rank-and-file CFMEU member, described the history of Labor’s attacks on militant unions since the 1980s. He said it could have been avoided if the Australian Council of Trade Unions had defended militants unions instead of colluding with it.

Johnston said that if the Coalition and One Nation wins in November, all unions would be attacked. “We can beat them if we stick together,” he said. He outlined some actions that militant unionists could take to rebuild solidarity and a fightback.

“We have to stop shit canning each other”, Johnston said, because that creates disunity. He talked up the need to take collective action, such as visiting other unions’ picket lines and supporting social movements. He said by “helping each other out”, solidarity is rebuilt.

The discussion illustrated the anger and frustration many CFMEU members and veterans feel especially when other building unions, which are not under attack, have done little to build a solidarity campaign. The meeting welcomed the solidarity shown by RAFFWU and other non-construction unions,

Tim Gooden from DUDC said that although CFMEU members are demoralised, as the state’s attack was designed to do, the lack of leadership in response to the attack has been more damaging.

But, Gooden said, “we’ve got to work with what we’ve got … the minute someone decides to lead, the ranks will follow.”

The possibility of the Coalition winning the Victorian elections poses some big challenges for workers and their unions, not the least being a decline in safety standards. Anecdotal evidence shows that falls from heights are already on the rise in Victoria and NSW since the CFMEU was taken into administration.

[Sue Bull is a member of Defend the Unions – Defend the CFMEU. She is running for the Socialist Alliance in the Western Region in the Legislative Council.]

author: labor4pal
title: Two days ago, Ver.di issued a statement in support of the October 30th international strike by port workers.The statement is pathetic—blatantly shameful—and fails to even mention Gaza or the ongoing genocide against my people (Mo Anker)
content:
A post shared by Mo.Anker (@mo.anker)

Two days ago, Ver.di issued a statement in support of the October 30th international strike by port workers. The statement is pathetic—blatantly shameful—and fails to even mention Gaza or the ongoing genocide against my people. The world is being turned upside down; school strikes are spreading across Europe, with Palestine at the forefront. For three years, my people in Gaza and the West Bank have been subjected to ethnic cleansing—backed by clear and robust German support. Yet, Ver.di still dares not utter the word “Gaza,” nor does it take a strong, courageous, and just stance toward my Palestinian people, who are being exterminated by German-made weapons. Germany is the most blood-stained nation in modern history; it seems Ver.di—one of Germany’s largest labor unions—has learned nothing from that history. For over a year and a half, I have sought the solidarity of my colleagues and my union, only to be met with nothing but racism and discrimination.

The call issued by Ver.di is brazen and racist; it actively contributes to the ongoing genocide and the daily killing of Palestinians—facilitated by German weapons, policies, and support. As a member of Ver.di and a Palestinian directly affected by this genocide, I call upon all honorable people across the globe—all free workers of the world, my international colleagues, and my friends—do not trust Ver.di. Challenge them, demand a change in their conduct, and insist that they stop devaluing Palestinian lives and finally acknowledge the catastrophe my people are enduring. Freedom for Palestine. Shame upon those who remain silent or fail to act. Victory to the free workers of the world.

title: Sevda Karaca’dan Antep’teki taciz davası için dayanışma çağrısı: “İşçiler, kadınlar, kadın işçiler yalnız değildir!”
content:
Emek Partisi (EMEP) Gaziantep Milletvekili Sevda Karaca, Aslansoy Tekstil’in sahibi Ahmet Aslansoy’un yargılandığı davanın salı günü görülecek duruşması öncesinde dayanışma çağrısı yaptı. Karaca, “Herkesi bu davaya sahip çıkmaya, kadın işçiyle dayanışmaya ve Salı günü saat 11.00’de Antep Adliyesine çağırıyoruz” dedi.

Sevda Karaca, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, davayı “İşçi bir kadının, sırtını hem paraya hem de siyasete yaslamış kerli ferli bir patrona karşı cesaretini ortaya koyduğu bir davanın duruşması” sözleriyle tanımladı.

Aslansoy Tekstil’in sahibi Ahmet Aslansoy’un fabrikada çaycı olarak çalışan bir kadın işçiyi sistematik biçimde taciz ettiğini geçen yıl duyurduklarını belirten Karaca, şunları söyledi:

“Parayla, tehditle, güçle susturulmak istenen kadın, onurunu ve hakkını savunmak için adli makamlara başvurmuş, ancak sessizlikle karşı karşıya bırakılmıştı. Ancak yılmamış, BİRTEK-SEN’den ve bizden destek istemişti.”

Karaca, olayın duyurulmasının ardından soruşturma dosyasının yeniden ele alındığını ifade ederek şu açıklamayı yaptı:

“Bizim olayı duyurmamız üzerine, 1 yıl boyunca hiçbir işlem yapılmadan bekletilen soruşturma dosyası raflardan indirilmek zorunda kalmıştı. Ahmet Aslansoy’un bütün gücüne rağmen suçun açık delilleri iddianame hazırlattı ve dava açıldı.”

Duruşma sürecine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde de bulunan Karaca, “Ahmet Aslansoy ilk iki celse türlü bahanelerle duruşmadan kaçtı. Üçüncü celse mecbur kalıp katıldığı duruşmada suçunu inkar etti. Mağdur kadına ve avukatına suç duyurularında bulundu” ifadelerini kullandı.

Karaca, Aslansoy’un hukuk profesörlerinden aldığı görüşlerle suçsuz olduğunu ispatlamaya çalıştığını ifade etti.

“Ahmet Aslansoy’un parasına, iktidar partisine, HSK üyeliği yapmış hukuk profesörlerine, yargıda etkisine karşı işçi kadının elindeki tek güç sınıf ve kadın dayanışması” diyen Karaca, açıklamasını şu sözlerle tamamladı:

“Herkesi bu davaya sahip çıkmaya, kadın işçiyle dayanışmaya ve Salı günü saat 11.00’de Antep Adliyesine çağırıyoruz. İşçiler, kadınlar, kadın işçiler yalnız değildir!”

Salı günü Antep Adliyesinde çok önemli bir davanın duruşması görülecek. İşçi bir kadının, sırtını hem paraya hem de siyasete yaslamış kerli ferli bir patrona karşı cesaretini ortaya koyduğu bir davanın duruşması. Aslansoy Tekstil’in sahibi, AKP Gaziantep milletvekili Derya Bakbak'ın babası Ahmet Aslansoy’un fabrikasında çaycı olarak çalışan bir kadın işçiyi sistematik bir şekilde taciz ettiği olayı geçen sene duyurmuştuk. Parayla, tehditle, güçle susturulmak istenen kadın, onurunu ve hakkını savunmak için adli makamlara başvurmuş, ancak sessizlikle karşı karşıya bırakılmıştı. Ancak yılmamış, BİRTEK-SEN’den ve bizden destek istemişti. Bizim olayı duyurmamız üzerine, 1 yıl boyunca hiçbir işlem yapılmadan bekletilen soruşturma dosyası raflardan indirilmek zorunda kalmıştı. Ahmet Aslansoy’un bütün gücüne rağmen suçun açık delilleri iddianame hazırlattı ve dava açıldı. Ahmet Aslansoy ilk iki celse türlü bahanelerle duruşmadan kaçtı. Üçüncü celse mecbur kalıp katıldığı duruşmada suçunu inkar etti. Mağdur kadına ve avukatına suç duyurularında bulundu. Şimdi de hukuk profesörlerinden aldığı yanlı görüşlerle suçsuz olduğunu ispat etmeye çalışıyor. Ahmet Aslansoy’un parasına, iktidar partisine, HSK üyeliği yapmış hukuk profesörlerine, yargıda etkisine karşı işçi kadının elindeki tek güç sınıf ve kadın dayanışması. Herkesi bu davaya sahip çıkmaya, kadın işçiyle dayanışmaya ve Salı günü saat 11.00’de Antep Adliyesine çağırıyoruz. İşçiler, kadınlar, kadın işçiler yalnız değildir!

title: Fransa: Öğrenci isyanı toplumsallaşıyor, 800 bin insan Cumartesi sokaktaydı
content:
Fransa'da eylül ortasında başlayan lise protestoları, 17 Ekim Cumartesi günü Paris'ten Akdeniz kıyısında Marsilya'ya, Orta Batı'da Limoges'da kitlesel yürüyüşlere dönüştü. İçişleri Bakanlığı ülke çapında 110 gösteri düzenlendiğini açıkladı. Gösterilerin çoğu barışçıl geçerken bazı kentlerde yağma, kundaklama ve polislerle çatışmalar yaşandı.


İsyanın sınıfsal coğrafyası


Hareketin ilk merkezlerinden biri Seine-Saint-Denis. Burası, Paris'in kuzeydoğusunda işçi sınıfı nüfusunun yoğunlaştığı yoksul bir ilçe. İsyan, Saint-Denis, Aubervilliers ve Sevran'daki liselerde öğrenciler öğretmen eksikliği, bakımsız binalar, kalabalık sınıflar ve eğitimde bölgesel eşitsizlikler nedeniyle dersleri boykotuyla  başladı. Paul-Éluard ve Le Corbusier liseleri öne çıktı. Öğretmenler ve veliler de eylemlere katıldı.


Öğrencilerin itirazı yalnızca okul binalarıyla sınırlı değildi: Yoksul mahallelerde eğitime ayrılan kaynaklar ve yükseköğretime erişim koşulları da hareketin gündemine girdi.


Piketty: “Macronizmin alacakaranlığı”


"21. Yüzyılda Kapital"in yazarı iktisatçı Thomas Piketty, 17 Ekim'de

Le Monde

'da yayımlanan yazısında öğrenci hareketini şöyle değerlendirdi:


“Bugünkü lise ve üniversite öğrencileri hareketi, Macronizmin alacakaranlığına işaret ediyor.”


Piketty'nin aktardığı hesaplamaya göre 2017-2026 döneminde yükseköğretim bütçesi nominal olarak artsa da enflasyon ve öğrenci sayısındaki yükseliş nedeniyle öğrenci başına reel kaynak yaklaşık yüzde 20 azaldı.


Piketty, araştırmacı Asma Benhenda'nın verilerine dayanarak eğitimdeki bölgesel eşitsizliğe dikkat çekti:


"Paris ve varlıklı Hauts-de-Seine'deki öğretmenlerin yaklaşık yüzde 10'u sözleşmeli ya da mesleğe yeni başlamış öğretmenlerden oluşurken, yoksul Seine-Saint-Denis ve Val-de-Marne'da bu oran yüzde 50'ye ulaşıyor.”


Kaynak yetersizliği savunmasına “Fransa hiç bu kadar zengin olmamıştı” diyr karşılık veren Piketty sonucu bir cümleyle özetledi: 


“Sorun yalnızca bir bölüşüm sorunu.”


Sendikalar öğrencilerle buluştu


Öğrencilerle ilk örgütlü dayanışmayı eğitim emekçileri sendikaları kurdu. Eğitim, Öğretim ve Araştırma Sendikaları Federasyonu (FSU), Genel Emek Konfederasyonu (CGT), İşçi Gücü (FO), Fransız Demokratik Emek Konfederasyonu (CFDT), Ulusal Özerk Sendikalar Birliği (UNSA) ve SUD-Solidaires'in eğitim örgütleri ekim başında öğretmen açığına, eğitim bütçesine ve okul koşullarına ilişkin ortak eylem çağrılarında yer aldı.


17 Ekim'de katılım eğitim sektörünü aştı. CGT ve sendikal birlik Solidaires, üyelerini öğrenci ve emekçi gösterilerine çağırdı. CGT ücret ve emekli aylıklarının artırılmasını, hayat pahalılığıyla mücadeleyi ve kamu hizmetlerinin korunmasını öne çıkardı. Genel Sekreter Sophie Binet, kaynakların büyük servetlerden ve şirket kârlarından sağlanmasını savundu. Solidaires işyerlerinde grevlerin örgütlenmesini istedi.


Köylü Konfederasyonu (Confédération paysanne), gelir güvencesi, gıdaya erişim ve iklim adaleti talepleriyle katıldı. Akaryakıt fiyatları ve geçim sıkıntısına karşı harekete geçen Sarı Yelekliler de yürüyüşlere katıldı. Öğrenci örgütleri USL, UNEF ve Öğrenci Birliği çağrıları destekledi.


Ancak 17 Ekim'e bütün konfederasyonlar ortak genel grevle katılmadı. Eylem tatil günü yapıldı ve  CFDT ve FO ülke çapındaki ağırlıklarını 5 Kasım eylemine koyacaklarını açıkladılar. 


Gösterilerin yoğunlaştığı merkezler ve şiddet olayları


Paris'te Cumhuriyet Meydanı çevresi başlıca buluşma noktasıydı. Lyon, Nantes, Rennes, Marsilya, Lille, Toulouse, Bordeaux, Strasbourg ve Montpellier'de yürüyüşler düzenlendi. Boyun Eğmeyen Fransa (LFI) lideri Jean-Luc Mélenchon Paris'te gösteriye katıldı; komünistler ve Yeşiller de çeşitli kentlerde gösterilerde yer aldı.


Paris'te bazı mağazalar yağmalandı, araçlar ateşe verildi. Limoges'da belediye binasında yangın çıktı; Marsilya ve Lille'de belediye binaları zarar gördü. Lyon'da bir turizm bürosu kundaklandı; Bordeaux ve başka merkezlerde mağazalara saldırılar bildirildi.


Bununla birlikte, şiddet olayları yüz binlerce göstericinin katıldığı eylemlerin belkemiğini oluşturmuyor. İçişleri Bakanlığı yaklaşık 400 gözaltı açıkladı; bu sayı, yağma ve kundaklamaya karışanları ifade etmiyor. Önceki günlerde polisin gözaltına aldığı protestocu sayısı bundan birkaç kat yüksekti.

author: winter oak
title: When is a “fascist” not a fascist?
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


Troy Southgate (1965-)

 is someone whose name I have been hearing, on and off, for thirty-odd years now, particularly at the time when my political path crossed with that of the late Richard Hunt, who was being shunted out of the anarchist scene at the same time that I was wandering into it.


Southgate was one of the “far right” nationalists who took an interest in Hunt’s green anarchist philosophy – he contributed to his review

Alternative Green

 and ended up editing it.


He got in touch with me after I published my August 2026

article

 about Hunt’s thinking, [1] pointing out his friendship with the neglected thinker and suggesting that today his and my outlooks are closer than one might have imagined.


I have to admit that I have been long been put off by Southgate’s use of the term “national-anarchism” – he founded the National-Anarchist Movement in the UK.


For me the term is an oxymoron, national identities (rather than tribal or communal ones) having been manufactured to encourage emotional attachment to the “national” states – always anarchists’ enemies – which were, in fact, the first phase of the centuries-long programme of global centralisation.


But I learned from an

audio interview

 of Southgate (

pictured

) by Luke Dodson and Adam Ormes that there was a pragmatic reason behind this label – as a convert to anarchism, thanks to Hunt, he wanted to bring other nationalists along with him. It was a bridge between two different ideological positions. [2]


Although I believe that rooted and cohesive communities are the best defence against predatory centralisation, and recognise the value of kinship ties, I am a bit wary of the position on racial separatism adopted by Southgate’s group, despite the fact that it is by no means racist, purist or dogmatic.


The

National-Anarchist Manifesto


states

: “The ‘national’ component of the term National-Anarchism centres on the fact that some of us are racial separatists. Needless to say, whilst we wish to form Anarchist communities that are ethnically organic we also oppose negative and counter-productive attitudes that encourage racial hatred or mindless violence…


“The National-Anarchist Movement (N-AM) is not a racial separatist organisation

per se

 and neither do we believe that it is essential for everyone to accept this principle. We adhere to the principle of ‘live and let live’ and, if people wish to establish multi-racial communities whilst retaining the ‘National-Anarchist’ label, then they should be permitted to do so.


“In other words, we believe that supporters of both mono-racialism and mixed tribal communities can work together for the wider promulgation of National-Anarchism in general. The most important thing of all, however, is for each of our communities to be established with a unifying vision; be it racial, cultural or spiritual. Separatism for some, mixed tribes for others”. [3]


I would suggest that if the “national” component refers to racial separatism and yet you do not have to be a racial separatist to be a national-anarchist, then perhaps the name is not a good fit for the ideology!


Moreover, if the idea is simply for people to be free to gather in communities with a certain unifying affinity, under the supposition that ethnic identity might be that affinity for some, why even bother to

name

 “racial separatism” as a possibility? Why not just leave it at the “live and let live” principle and allow human nature to take its course when the time comes for people to seek out their tribe?


The notion that folk should be free to form a community

with whomsoever they wish

 (

including

 on an ethnic basis) is already embraced by anarchism as a whole – by authentic anarchism, in any case – so that awkward “national-” prefix could then safely be ditched!


Southgate seems to have been picked out as a particular bogeyman by the system and has a

profile

 on

Wikipedia

 in which we are told that “he has been affiliated with far-right and fascist groups, such as National Front and International Third Position…


“In 1998, Southgate and other ENM [English Nationalist Movement] members founded the National Revolutionary Faction. In 2001, Southgate and the NRF were the subject of a

Sunday Telegraph

 article, in which the NRF was accused of being a neo-Nazi organisation infiltrating animal rights groups to spread fascism”. [4]


But is he

really

 a “fascist” or a …

author: Unknown
title: Danny Evans - ‘Ultra-left’ anarchists and anti-fascism in the Second Republic
content:
Author

: Danny Evans

Title

: ‘Ultra-left’ anarchists and anti-fascism in the Second Republic

Date

: 2016

Source

:

International Journal of Iberian Studies

, 29: 3, pp. 241–56, doi: 10.1386/ijis.29.3.241_1


ABSTRACT


 This article investigates the anarchist understanding of fascism during the Second Republic, and particularly during the abstention campaign of 1933, when the practice of radicals in the National Confederation of Labour (CNT) has been described as ‘ultra-left’ in view of its sectarianism and insistence on the need for an insurrectionary response to the threat of the right. The article explores the comparison made to the German Communist Party (KPD) during the so-called ‘Third Period’, and the lessons that anarchists in Spain attempted to draw from the rise of Hitler.


INTRODUCTION


 The Spanish general election of November 1933 resulted in the formation of a centre-right government presided over by Alejandro Lerroux with the support of the Spanish Confederation of Autonomous Right Wing Groups (CEDA). Thus began the so-called ‘bienio negro’ of the Second Republic, characterized by the reversal of the reforms of the previous two years and the repression of left-wing and labour organizations. The elections had been preceded by a campaign orchestrated by the anarcho-syndicalist union, the National Confederation of Labour (CNT) which called on Spanish workers to abstain from voting. Following the elections, that same organization initiated a short-lived and disastrous uprising, which left over a hundred dead. This marked the beginning of a period of repression in which thousands of CNT activists were jailed and the day to day functioning of the organization was jeopardized.


 Understandably, the historiography has not been kind to the CNT in this period. Its actions have been considered a consequence of ‘impatience and revolutionary mysticism’ (Gómez Casas 1973: 172), its propaganda dismissed as ‘the radical discourse of a minority’ of anarchists within the organization (Casanova 2005: 46). Thus the abstention campaign and the rising of late 1933 have generally been considered to be consequent upon the internal dynamics of the CNT, and the culmination of the process of radicalization within the organization during the first bienio of the Second Republic (1931–1933). This radicalization had already produced two uprisings, in January 1932 and January 1933, and the December revolt has been considered the closing act of a ‘cycle of insurrections’. In contrast to the Asturian insurrection of October 1934, the anarchist revolt of late 1933 is not normally considered a response to the increasing perception of an international and domestic fascist threat. On the contrary, the CNT’s insistence on pursuing a lonely insurrectionist tactic has been taken as evidence of ultra-left indifference among radicals as to the specific danger posed by fascism. According to Chris Ealham, anarchist radicals in this period ‘downplayed the danger of the far Right’, and acted in a sectarian manner that undermined attempts at anti-fascist unity:


 Playing an ultra-leftist, divisive role that had much in common with the German Communist Party (KPD) prior to Hitler’s electoral triumph, the radical anarchists argued that there was no difference between the various electoral options, even suggesting that fascism was already in power […] like the KPD, the CNT and the FAI [the Iberian Anarchist Federation, a federation of anarchist affinity groups] blocked united anti-fascist action, directing their fury against what they regarded as the ‘fascism’ of their enemies, be they treintista [moderate syndicalist], socialist, republican or bloquista [dissident communist], all of whom were regarded as variants of authoritarianism. (2010: 134)


 Using this suggestive comparison as a starting point, in this article I examine the roots of the commonalities between the approaches of the KPD and the CNT, specifically their sectarianism and revolutionary maximalism, while also fleshing out the differences that marked the anarchist approach to fascism in theory and in practice.


 The ‘anti-fascist epic’ (Southworth 1996: 310) was finally won in 1945 by an alliance of imperial, Communist and democratic forces. This alliance contrasted with the ‘divisions and ineffectiveness’ of those who had opposed Hitler in Germany, identified as a contributing factor in his accession to power (Bullock 1973: 253). As such, the ‘object lesson’ of the rise …

author: Unknown
title: Franco Cavalli: The left’s weakness fuels the far right’s rise
content:
The rise of far-right and racist movements across Europe is deepening concerns about the continent's political future. The growing strength of Alternative for Germany (AfD), the increasing political influence of the far right in France and the policies of Giorgia Meloni's government in Italy have reignited debates about Europe's future. The economic crisis, the so-called “migration crisis”, growing inequalities and social discontent fuelled by neoliberal policies are among the key factors driving the rise of the far right.


What dynamics lie behind the rise of the far right in Europe? Why have left-wing movements been unable to offer a strong alternative? What is the relationship between the crisis of capitalism and fascist tendencies? We put these questions to Swiss politician and physician Franco Cavalli. Cavalli spoke to ANF about developments in Europe, drawing particular attention to the dangers posed by Germany's rearmament policies and the rise of the AfD. He said the left had largely embraced neoliberal policies over the past three decades, arguing that the rise of the far right was driven not only by the economic crisis but also by the ideological and political weakness of the left.


How do you assess the rise of the far right in Europe? Is it possible to describe what we are witnessing today as the threat of a new form of fascism?


Both yes and no. I think we need to be careful about calling too many things fascism, because some of them may not correspond exactly to the real fascism we knew a century ago. However, it is also clear that there are many similarities between what is happening today and what happened a hundred years ago.


The situation may vary somewhat from country to country. However, if we define fascism as an ideology based on racism, one that gives absolute priority to the national population and seeks to establish an authoritarian state, then we have to acknowledge that there are many similarities, at least in terms of its fundamental principles.


We have seen this in Italy, for example. Meloni used genuinely fascist rhetoric when she was still only the leader of her party. Now that she is in government, she has considerably softened her language. Beyond that, however, particularly when we look at Germany, Spain and, to some extent, France, we have to recognise that there are strong tendencies in Europe that closely resemble the fascism of the past. These tendencies are also present in France, despite the existence of a very strong popular movement on the left.


A heavily armed Germany frightens me more than Russia


What frightens me most, of course, is Germany. Germany has decided to invest enormous sums in its military and has declared that it wants to have the most powerful army in Europe.


Therefore, if the AfD comes to power tomorrow and takes control of a Germany with a very powerful army, that would naturally be extremely dangerous. It would be far more dangerous than what is currently described as the Russian threat.


I am much more afraid of a Germany armed to the teeth than of Russia, which is actually quite weak today and has no interest whatsoever in attacking the West.


Fascism emerges from the middle class with the support of big capital


As for the reasons behind this, I think we are essentially dealing with the consequences of an economic crisis that has hit the middle class particularly hard. We know that fascism almost always emerges from the middle class with the support of big capital.


Today, the middle class is experiencing a crisis as it becomes increasingly proletarianised, and it refuses to accept this situation.


The European left, on the other hand, has weakened considerably over the past thirty years, since the collapse of the Soviet Union. It no longer has a model to rely on. It has also largely internalised neoliberal counter-reforms.


As a result, the left has moved towards the centre. In fact, something similar happened to a certain extent a hundred years ago. When the left can no longer respond to the problems of the proletariat or the increasingly proletarianised middle class, these people turn to the far right. The far right then offers proposals that appear to be solutions but are not solutions at all.


I therefore believe that the two main factors explaining the rise of the far right in Europe are the economic crisis and the weakness of the left. When these two factors come together, the far right grows stronger.

Νίκη στη νεολαία της Γαλλίας – Σάββατο 17/10,11.30,Σύνταγμα (πορεία προς τη γαλλική πρεσβεία)


ΚΑΤΩ Η ΧΟΥΝΤΑ των «Μακρόν» και «Μητσοτάκηδων»


της ΕΕ των Πλουσίων, της Φτώχειας, του Πολέμου, της Καταστολής


Εδώ και πάνω από δέκα μέρες, οι κινητοποιήσεις των μαθητών στη Γαλλία συγκλονίζουν και εμπνέουν εργαζόμενους και φτωχούς σε όλη την Ευρώπη. Το κίνημα ξέσπασε αυθόρμητα σε ένα παρισινό προάστιο, για να κατακλύσει σύντομα όλη τη χώρα. Αυτή τη φορά -σε αντίθεση με την επαναστατική έκρηξη του Γαλλικού Μάη του 1968- την πρωτοβουλία είχαν τα

σχολεία εργατικών και λαϊκών προαστίων

. Όπου στοιβάζονται σε άθλιες συνθήκες και ζουν μια αφόρητη κατάσταση φτώχειας και στέρησης, ταπείνωσης και καταστολής μεγάλες μάζες της νεολαίας, μαζί και μετανάστες.


Η κατάσταση στα σχολεία της Γαλλίας θυμίζει τα αίσχη που ζούμε και στη χώρα μας οι μαθητές, εκπαιδευτικοί, γονείς: Αύξηση του αριθμού των μαθητών και λιγότεροι εκπαιδευτικοί, με αποτέλεσμα τάξεις των 30-35 μαθητών ή και παραπάνω. Κτήρια που καταρρέουν, με ποντίκια και κατσαρίδες να σουλατσάρουν από τη βρώμα και εγκατάλειψη. Σχολικό ωράριο από τα πιο βαριά στην Ευρώπη. Σύστημα εισαγωγής στα πανεπιστήμια που εξοντώνει τους μαθητές με άγχος και κούραση –

όπως εδώ η Τράπεζα Θεμάτων, η Ελάχιστη Βάση Εισαγωγής, το Νέο Λύκειο, οι συγχωνεύσεις, τα «Ωνάσεια»

… Όλα αυτά ενώ οι πλούσιοι (και) στη Γαλλία απολαμβάνουν τα πιο προκλητικά κέρδη και φοροαπαλλαγές, απαιτώντας πάλι εργαζόμενοι και φτωχοί να πληρώσουν για το τεράστιο δημόσιο χρέος με σκληρά «μνημονιακά» μέτρα.


Η οργή των μαθητών φουντώνει όχι μόνο από τα προβλήματα αλλά και από την απαξιωτική, αλαζονική συμπεριφορά εκπροσώπων της κυβέρνησης Μακρόν και του κατεστημένου. Ενώ η καταστολή των CRS (τα γαλλικά ΜΑΤ), διαβόητων για τη σκληρότητά τους, με πλαστικές σφαίρες, κρότου-λάμψης, δακρυγόνα στο ψαχνό, έχει αφήσει σοβαρά τραυματισμένους και χιλιάδες συλληφθέντες. Όμως η νεολαία δεν κάμπτεται,

σηκώνει το κεφάλι, απαντά με τη δική της λαϊκή αντιβία στους μηχανισμούς καταστολής

. Έχει παλλαϊκή υποστήριξη από εκπαιδευτικούς και γονείς, που σχηματίζουν ανθρώπινες αλυσίδες για να προστατέψουν τους νέους, ενώ σε κοινές μέρες δράσης συμμετέχουν φοιτητές και εργαζόμενοι.


Οι κινητοποιήσεις έχουν εξαπλωθεί και σε άλλες χώρες, π.χ. στο Βέλγιο, αλλά και στη

Γερμανία

, στην οποία η νεολαία παλεύει ενάντια στη στρατιωτικοποίηση και την επαναφορά μιας σκληρής υποχρεωτικής στρατιωτικής θητείας, ώστε να ικανοποιηθούν τα καταστροφικά σχέδια επαναξεπλισμού και πολέμου του γερμανικού ιμπεριαλισμού στην Ουκρανία και αλλού. Επίσης, στην

Ισπανία

, με το μεγάλο κίνημα που απαιτεί έμπρακτες λύσεις ενάντια στους κερδοσκόπους και τα funds, που λυμαίνονται τη λαϊκή ανάγκη για στέγη, ωθώντας τα νοίκια στον Θεό και τον λαϊκό κόσμο στην απελπισία.


Τον δρόμο δείχνει η Γαλλία – ΚΑΤΑΛΗΨΕΙΣ, ΔΙΑΔΗΛΩΣΕΙΣ, ΓΕΝΙΚΗ ΑΠΕΡΓΙΑ


Ενότητα, Αγώνας, Οργάνωση – Με μια Αριστερά Επαναστατική


Όλες αυτές οι κινητοποιήσεις και ειδικά η πιθανότητα να συγκλίνουν σε κοινούς αγώνες έχουν ανησυχήσει σοβαρά τις ευρωπαϊκές ελίτ. Στη χώρα μας, πρέπει να πάρουμε νέα πνοή από το παράδειγμα της γαλλικής νεολαίας,

μια γενιά που χάνει μερικά μαθήματα για να δώσει στους «από πάνω» ένα μεγάλο μάθημα, για να απαιτήσει μέλλον και ζωή με αξιοπρέπεια, αντί για τη χωματερή της φτώχειας και του ταξικού αποκλεισμού, αντί για τα πολεμικά φέρετρα που της ετοιμάζουν

. Η οργή και το μίσος για την κυβέρνηση Μητσοτάκη πρέπει να βρει αγωνιστική έκφραση, μέσα σε αυτές τις ευνοϊκές συνθήκες, σπάζοντας την προεκλογική σιγή «νεκροταφείου» του επίσημου πολιτικού σκηνικού, της φαρσοκωμωδίας κυβέρνησης και «αντιπολίτευσης», των μισερών, «συμβολικών» και συμβιβασμένων κινήσεων των ρεφορμιστών και της συνδικαλιστικής γραφειοκρατίας.

title: Demandez le programme ! Créer la brèche : construire et penser des perspectives révolutionnaires et antifascistes
content:
À la suite de la mort du néo-nazi Deranque, nous nous sommes retrouvé·es à quelques-un·es pour tenter de dépasser collectivement l'état de sidération face à la répression et la réaction de la classe politique et médiatique.


Nous constatons la place importante qu'occupe le milieu autonome à Lyon mais il nous semble nécessaire de le structurer afin de développer sa pleine puissance.


De ce fait, nous pensons qu'il faut s'organiser de manière collective et dans une perspective révolutionnaire. Notre volonté serait de dépasser l'agenda politique institutionnel, de proposer des espaces d'organisation laissant place à nos désaccords et à nos ambitions révolutionnaires tout en étant capables d'être à la hauteur des coups portés contre notre camp.


Pour cela, nous proposons un moment de discussion le week-end du 23, 24 et 25 octobre afin d'échanger ensemble pour penser les années à venir. Ces discussions suivront trois axes après un premier temps consacré au bilan de nos luttes et expériences révolutionnaires de ces dernières années :


Attaque

 : Les formes d'organisation possibles, leurs limites et leurs réussites


Défense

 : les possibilités de résistance et de solidarité concrètes


Propagande

 : Forces et limites de nos outils de diffusion des idées


Assemblée Antifasciste Autonome


Vendredi 23 octobre : Accueil


Rendez-vous à partir de 19h à l'Amicale du futur (31 rue Sébastien Gryphe, Lyon 7

e

) pour la soirée d'accueil du week-end. Tout le matériel des discussions seront mis à disposition à cette occasion.


Samedi 24 et dimanche 25 octobre


Rendez-vous à l'Ile Égalité (4 rue de l'Égalité à Villeurbanne, métro Cusset) pour les journées de discussion. Les discussions du matin démarrent à 9h et celles de l'après-midi à 14h. Nous vous invitons à rester en fin de journée pour un temps convivial. Il y aura une cantine et une buvette à prix libre (pas de

CB

, que du cash).


Samedi matin : Bilan de ces dix dernières années


Pour démarrer le week-end et lancer les discussions, un premier temps est organisé pour revenir sur la séquence politique de 2014 à aujourd'hui afin de prendre du recul sur les réussites et les échecs de l'autonomie lyonnaise.


Samedi après-midi : Défense/Solidarités


On le constate tous les jours : c'est la merde. À l'international, les capitalistes nous précipitent dans une fuite en avant guerrière, impérialiste et écocide. L'Europe et l'Occident transformés en bunker ont globalement fait le pari du fascisme pour tenter de garder leur place historique en tête du classement mondial, à coup de guerres impérialistes pour l'énergie et les minerais, de répression dans les anciens territoires colonisés, en érigeant des murs et en massacrant les migrant.e.s aux frontières. Au national, les gouvernements se succèdent et se ressemblent tant et si bien que la chanson demeure toujours la même : austérité et renforcement autoritaire de l'état, surveillance de masse et répression à gogo, mesures antisociales profitant au patronat et décrets liberticides, racistes et islamophobes tandis que les médias mainstream fabriquent de toutes pièces des ennemis intérieur à abattre. État d'urgence, état policier... À Lyon, ces dernières années, les choses se sont corsées, entre les vagues de dissolution de collectifs et les expulsions de squats de logement et d'organisation, le milieu autonome s'est trouvé amputé de lieux d'organisations stratégiques et de forces d'appel larges. La peur de la répression, qui isole les personnes face au triptique police/justice/prison, mais aussi l'abattement des défaites politiques d'après les retraites et les révoltes pour Nahel ont favorisé le sentiment d'inertie et ont laissé un goût amer.


C'est pourquoi nous sommes tombé.e.s d'accord sur l'idée qu'il fallait nous renforcer, nous, nos outils, nos espaces, nos stratégies. Renforcer notre camp social en mettant en place des mesures d'autodéfense révolutionnaires et en faisant vivre concrètement la solidarité entre nous. D'abord, nous protéger de la répression, et tout particulièrement de la possibilité de la prison. À l'intérieur de laquelle nous souhaitons parler du soutien aux prisonnier.e.s en prison et en

author: Ella Gutteridge
title: Hundreds protest far-right conference in Brisbane
content:
High-profile racists and far-right leaders descended on the Brisbane showgrounds over the weekend of 10 and 11 October for the Conservative Political Action Conference.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson headlined the event. She was joined by Liberal leader Angus Taylor, far-right podcaster Karl Stefanovic, and one of Britain’s least successful politicians, former Prime Minister Liz Truss.

Inside, it was a carnival of reaction. The ABC reported that

Hanson was greeted with

rapturous applause

 as she harangued the Coalition for signing up to net-zero and creating an eSafety commissioner, which she pledged to abolish on the grounds of free speech.

The leader of the National Party, Matt Canavan, cosplayed as a blue-collar worker as he took to the stage to extol the virtues of Australian manufacturing. Despite earlier criticisms, Hanson said that she’d be willing to work with the Coalition to “

throw out this wretched and corrupt Labor government

”.

Outside, hundreds of irreverent high schoolers, trade union activists and community members rallied, waving homemade signs, chanting and drumming. The crowd was a sea of keffiyehs, rainbow flags and signs, with many commenting on Hanson’s close relationship with Australian billionaire Gina Rinehart (“Pauline works for Gina!”).

“Migrants are welcome, racists are not!” was a popular chant, echoing across the showgrounds while conferencegoers streamed out for their lunch break. One Nation recently unveiled

its policy to cut Australia’s immigration intake

 by 750,000 people over three years, including plans to cut visas for the family members of skilled migrants and international students to zero.

“Pauline Hanson wants net zero immigration, but my parents are immigrants, my friends are immigrants, and without them this country would be nothing and fuck Pauline!”, Sam, a high school student, told

Red Flag

.  

The rally heard from Dave Pullen, an Indigenous elder from Inala who ran against Hanson in Ipswich in 1996. Draped in an Indigenous flag, Pullen opened with an acknowledgement of country and of Hanson’s long record of racism towards Indigenous people.

National convenor of the Socialist Party and teacher unionist Rebecca Barrigos highlighted the importance of posing an alternative socialist vision to One Nation and the broader right:

“Today’s rally isn’t just about sending a signal to those inside the conference; it’s about saying we know what you’re doing. They’re fighting for a more competitive, more brutal, more pro-billionaire, anti-worker vision of society, and to that we say, fuck your vision of society! We have an alternative vision.”

There is a long way to go to realise that vision.

Hanson is currently the preferred prime minister to Anthony Albanese

 and is polling at 36 percent in Queensland. While the right has momentum, it still faces opposition. People who oppose One Nation’s vision for the world should rally to our side and put up a fight.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Cancels Livestream of Firing Squad Execution After Fierce Backlash
content:
Polling released before the announcement found only 18 percent of Americans support the livestreaming idea.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump has cancelled a plan to livestream the firing squad execution of former soldier Nidal Malik Hasan after widespread backlash from the public, politicians, military members, and faith leaders.

Trump made the announcement on Truth Social.

“I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device,” he said. Studies have repeatedly found no evidence that the death penalty acts as a deterrent to crime.

“He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed,” Trump added. “That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!”

On Thursday, shortly before Trump announced his decision, polling by The Washington Post, ABC News, and Ipsos found that the idea of livestreaming an execution is extremely unpopular among the public. According to the poll, 80 percent of Americans say they oppose it, while only 18 percent said they are in support. The idea is even overwhelmingly unpopular among the respondents who said they overall support the firing squad execution of Hasan, with 69 percent opposition to and 30 percent approval of the livestream among that group.

The only group that saw majority support of the livestream was among MAGA Republican men, among whom 57 percent backed the idea.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, who often speaks of violence as a virtue, initially announced the livestream last week during an interview with far right commentator Jack Posobiec.

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it. That it’s public. Because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said.

But the idea was faced with immediate opposition, and in recent days, Trump had reportedly been gathering opinions from allies as to whether he should make the killing publicly watchable.

After Hegseth’s announcement, both Democrats and Republicans in Congress condemned the livestream idea. Vice President J.D. Vance, perhaps seeing the backlash, said that he would not personally watch it. The military’s archbishop put out a statement disapproving of the idea, saying that it would harm the reputation of the U.S. military.

Many other religious leaders condemned the idea. Pope Leo put out a statement, meanwhile, calling for the abolition of the death penalty altogether.

“The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person,” said the pope. “The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption.”

Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Arizona) introduced a bill on Thursday that seeks to ban the public broadcasting of any military executions.

The Trump administration has reveled in imagery of state-perpetrated violence. Pentagon officials have repeatedly published footage of its deadly strikes on boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific Ocean, which have been likened to snuff films. His administration has gone produced propaganda videos with video game footage spliced between clips of alleged war crimes, making light of killing.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your …

title: How will we build an understanding of democratic integration?
content:
Integration represents a transitional process for achieving peace and reconciliation. Knowing that every grain of these lands, stones, trees, and flowers belongs to us, that this is our country, we will work hard to make our country more beautiful.


As freedom fighters, we will carry out pioneering work in every sphere, from the children and mothers of this country to its nature, production, technology, and all aspects of life. Until now, we have defended our honour, will, existence, and identity with weapons in this country. Now, too, we will protect and develop everything, from its economy and ecology to its water and air.


We will bring this country to a leading position in the Middle East as well. We will raise, educate, and develop the consciousness of simple and humble people on the basis of truth and beauty. In short, we dreamed of a moral and political society. We see the practical steps towards realizing this dream and the foundations of the democratic society paradigm as very strong. This paradigm has inspired the world. If we are to build society in our country on the basis of this paradigm, we must place truth, beauty, simplicity, politics, morality, and aesthetics at the centre of our efforts.


Because we love this country. We rebelled against what was wrong, against mistakes, outdated mindsets, and hearts that had grown numb. We went up into the free mountains, fought, and struggled. At times, we fought fiercely. Why? Because we rebelled against backwardness and ugliness; we struggled to build what is beautiful, what is right, and what is moral. We learned politics and brought it into practice so that we could speak beautifully.


Love requires effort. If your spiritual world is not vast, you cannot make sacrifices or give yourself wholeheartedly. The freedom fighters gave of themselves and shared what they had; dedicating themselves to this cause, they filled every moment and every hour with hard work. We will also take the lead in the construction efforts during the integration period at this level, working with dedication and committing ourselves to our society.


We have paid a tremendous price to reach this stage. We have laid the most beautiful and unassuming daughters and sons of our country to rest in the earth. We went hungry, thirsty, and sleepless; we grew tired, yet we lived with love. Because this was the path we had chosen, and we knew why. We believed that bright days would follow these dark ones. But those days would not come on their own. Through struggle, by carving our way forward with our fingernails, we made it to where we are today.


We did not get here easily. We arrived through great acts of heroism, sacrifice, hard work, and sharing. We did not merely sweat; blood and sweat became intertwined. The flower of the tree of freedom was watered with blood and sweat; this is how it grew, matured, and bore fruit. Reaching this day has required tremendous effort.


Because we love our country, we chose the most difficult struggle and went up into the free mountains. Now we will continue the struggle in cities, towns, villages, and neighbourhoods. We received the best education in those mountains, experienced and learned the finest forms of communal life and comradeship. Now we will share these experiences with our people, our society, and all the people of our country. We will achieve this by entering a communal world of thought together.


We are entering the process of democratic integration to live and to help others live. We will take the lead in the work of peace, truth, and reconciliation committees. Rather than pursuing positions of authority, we will lead society through civilian politics.


Women will lead democratic integration. We will reorganize ourselves to build a just, equal, peaceful, and free life. As women of the mountains, our hair has turned grey, but our hearts remain childlike. We retain a nature that seeks purity, simplicity, and beauty; that asks questions with curious eyes and continues its search. Yet we do not merely ask questions; we also build our own answers. We have a fighting spirit.


As women of the mountains, we will advocate for gender equality to be placed at the centre of peace negotiations. As women at the negotiating table, we will bring attention to gender-based violence and human rights violations, the experiences of the thousands of villages that were evacuated, the impact of displacement on women and children, and the losses suffered by …

author: Equality Now
title: The Data Behind the Action: Exploring the SADC Dashboard that tracks progress on ending child marriage in Southern Africa
content:
19th October 2026


The Data Behind the Action: Exploring the SADC Dashboard that tracks progress on ending child marriage in Southern Africa


9 min read


News and Insights


End child marriage


Africa


Photo Credit: Cozar Photography


Every girl deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, and shape her own future. Across Southern Africa, governments, parliamentarians, civil society, and local communities are working together to strengthen laws, policies, and actions to end child marriage.


A decade after the adoption of the SADC Model Law on eradicating child marriage and protecting children already in marriage, the

Southern African Development Community Parliamentary Forum

 (SADC PF) and the Technical Working Group on the Implementation of the SADC Model Law on Child Marriage launch a Dashboard on core indicators tracking progress on ending child marriage and protecting girls who are already married. The Dashboard shows where action is happening, highlights what works, and points out where more effort is needed. By bringing key information together in one place, it helps advocates, policymakers, and communities monitor progress and hold everyone accountable.


On 27 November, as we mark the very first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, the dashboard will be one of the innovative accountability tools that will be on hand to help various players in the policy and advocacy field turn promises into real, ongoing action.


What is the dashboard and why was it created?


The SADC Dashboard is a regional platform for tracking how the

Model Law on Eradicating Child Marriage and Protecting Children Already in Marriage

 is being implemented. It also serves as a tool for accountability, knowledge sharing, and decision-making, all in one place.


The Dashboard was created to solve problems like fragmented data, unclear indicator definitions, and results that are hard to compare across countries. In the past, key information often did not reach those who needed it, making it difficult for parliamentarians, civil society, and young people to see where progress was happening or where more work was needed.


The SADC PF worked with members of the Technical Working Group, including Equality Now, Plan International, Hivos, Girls Not Brides, UNFPA, UNICEF, and CARE International Zambia to create a regional Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MERL) Framework. The Dashboard was then developed to put the MERL Framework into practice.


How does the Dashboard work?


The MERL Framework sets out key outcomes, indicators, data sources, responsibilities, and minimum standards for monitoring the Model Law. The Dashboard turns this framework into an easy-to-use digital platform.


Users can view a regional summary of progress, use filters to explore different pages and views, check information for each Member State, compare countries, and read indicator definitions and data sources.


What information does it provide?


The Dashboard brings together key indicators on child marriage and the protection of married girls across SADC Member States. It also includes indicator definitions and data sources on the same platform. This transparency lets users see what is being measured, where the numbers come from, and where data is missing.


What are the four pillars of the Model Law?


The Dashboard organises its indicators around four parts of the Model Law: prevention, protection, legal and policy frameworks, and monitoring and accountability. These cover both stopping new cases of child marriage and supporting girls who are already married.


Who can use the Dashboard?


The Dashboard is designed for a wide range of users, including parliamentarians, policymakers, program managers, researchers, civil society organisations, traditional and community leaders, and young people.


The goal is to make information about child marriage clear and useful for everyone, not just technical experts.


How can parliamentarians use it?


Parliaments are critical actors in law reform, budgeting, and oversight. The Dashboard helps MPs see how their country measures up to regional standards and to other countries. They can use it to:


Prepare for oversight questions and committee work


Inform legislation and policy formulation


Make the case for budget allocations where gaps are visible


Hold dialogue with ministries and national statistics offices on data and delivery

title: Adli kontrol değil tedavisiz infaz: Hülya Gerçek’in ev hapsi
content:
Erkek şiddeti, istismar, taciz, tecavüz… Kadına yönelik her türlü şiddet… O kadar çok bunları konuşuyoruz, erkeklik suçları o kadar çok gündemimizi işgal ediyor ki ne yazık ki kadınlarla ilgili başkaca konuları konuşmaya imkan kalmıyor. Mesela kadın mahpuslar hatta biraz daha detaylandırayım, kadın hasta mahpuslar ve hatta ev hapsindeki kadın hasta mahpuslar.


Zaman zaman tartışırız: "Ev hapsindeyken deprem olsa ev hapsindeki kişi ne yapacak?" ya da "Ev hapsindeki kişi işe gidemediği için işten çıkarılır mı?" Peki ev hapsindeki kişi ağır bir hastalıkla mücadele ediyorsa ne olacak?


Mesela Hülya Gerçek… Üçüncü evre meme kanseri. Bu, kanserin meme dışına çıkarak çevre dokulara, göğüs duvarına veya koltuk altındaki lenf bezlerine yayıldığı ancak uzak organlara (kemik, karaciğer vb.) metastaz yapmadığı lokal ileri evreye ulaştığını gösteriyor.


Gerçek, 4 Mayıs 2025’te "örgüte finans sağlamak" iddiasıyla gözaltına alınıyor, ardından ev hapsi ile serbest bırakılıyor. Hasta bir kadın için bu pek de serbest bırakılma sayılmaz elbette.


Bu arada “örgüte finans sağlamak” ne demek derseniz? Şöyle, Türkiye'de terörizmin finansmanının önlenmesine dair esaslar

6415 sayılı Terörizmin Finansmanının Önlenmesi Hakkında Kanun

 ve

TCK m. 220 / Terörle Mücadele Kanunu (TMK)

 kapsamında düzenleniyor. 


Yani Gerçek’in durumunda olduğu gibi cezaevindeki bir yakına par göndermek de bu suçla ilişkilendiriliyor, ya da cezaevindeki yazarlara da telif ödemesi yapmak bu suçla ilişkilendiliyor. Evet evet. Ocak 2026’da K

or Kitap

’ın yayınevi temsilcisine, tutuklu yazar ve editörler Tonguç Ok ile Necip Baysal’a telif ödemesi yaptığı gerekçesiyle konutu terk etmeme (

ev hapsi

) şeklinde adli kontrol tedbiri uygulandı.


Benzer durumda olan ağır bir hasta mahpus Hatice Yıldız da var. Yıldız, cezaevinde tutuklu bulunan öz kızına ve kızının ihtiyaçlarını karşılayabilmesi için aynı koğuşta kalan arkadaşına PTT (Devlet Posta Kurumu) üzerinden resmi kanallarla para yatırdığı için de suçlanabiliyor. 


Bu arada hem cezaevindeki Yıldız’ın hem de GErçek’in tedavileri yarım kalıyor, bakımları yapılmıyor, kimi zaman tek kalıyorlar. 


Gerçek’in durumunda ise başka bir şaşırtıcı detay daha var, kendisi ile aynı dosyada tutulu olan diğer kişiler hakkında önce adli kontroller kaldırılıyor, ardından 2 Nisan’da hepsi beraat ediyor. Buna rağmen Hülya Gerçek hakkında uygulanan ev hapsi kaldırılmıyor. Bu da insanın aklına Gerçek’e yönelik başka özel bir öfke mi va sorusunu akıllara getiriyor? Neden?


Anayasa’nın 17. maddesi yaşam hakkını ve kişinin maddi ve manevi varlığını koruma hakkını, 56. maddesi ise herkesin sağlık hizmetlerinden yararlanma hakkını güvence altına alıyor. Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi’nin 2. ve 3. maddeleri uyarınca devletin yaşamı koruma ve insanlık dışı ya da onur kırıcı muameleyi önleme yükümlülüğü bulunuyor.


Birleşmiş Milletler Ekonomik, Sosyal ve Kültürel Haklar Sözleşmesi’nin 12. maddesi ise herkesin ulaşılabilir en yüksek sağlık standardına sahip olma hakkını tanıyor. 


En yalın hali ile Anayasa, yasalar ve uluslararası düzenlemelere rağmen Hülya Gerçek hakkında uygulanan adli kontrol tedbirinin devam ettirilmesi; ölçülülük, gereklilik ve orantılılık ilkeleriyle bağdaşmıyor. 


DEM Parti Milletvekili Çiçek Otlu, Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek'in yanıtlaması talebi ile 7 Ekim'de Gerçek'le ilgli bir soru önergesi sundu.  "Aynı dosya kapsamında tutuklu bulunan şüpheliler tahliye edildi diğer şüpheliler yönünden uygulanan adli kontrol tedbirleri kaldırıldı. 2 Nisan'da görülen karar duruşmasında dosya kapsamındaki tüm sanıklar hakkında beraat kararı verildi. Buna rağmen Hülya Gerçek hakkında uygulanan ev hapsi tedbirinin sürdürülmesi, hukuki değil keyfi bir uygulama izlenimi yaratmakta, eşitlik ilkesine ve adil yargılanma hakkına aykırılık oluşturuyor" dedi. 


1412 hasta mahpus 


Geçen hafta ise bu kez HDK Eş Sözcüsü / DEM Parti Erzurum Milletvekili ve Anayasa Komisyonu Üyesi Meral Danış Beştaş, Gerçek’in durumunu Meclis gündemine taşıdı. “Ağır veya kronik hastalığı bulunan kişiler hakkında konutu terk etmeme yükümlülüğü kararı verilirken sağlık durumunun, tedavi gereksinimlerinin ve hastaneye erişim imkânlarının değerlendirilmesine ilişkin Bakanlığınızca belirlenmiş bir usul, kriter veya genelge bulunuyor mu?” diye sordu.

title: Conectivas: First Time in (Por primera vez en) CADF
content:
A table of our own: Conectivas First Time in CADF.    

 


 


For many years, we have seen organizations that serve people with disabilities occupy spaces like the Central American Donors Forum (CADF); this year, thanks to WEI’s support, we were able to attend in person, make our voices heard, and become visible in places where we are usually invisible.   

 


We were not there to hear people speak about us; we went there to speak ourselves, for the first time and in first person – as an organization led by women with disabilities.   

 


What did we achieve?

  

 


We facilitated a networking table on women and disability.  

 


We offered support to WEI’s lighting talk on women with disabilities fighting back anti rights movements.   

 


We networked with different actors about how we see – from a human rights perspective- the backlashes in rights we are seeing globally and how we want to be included in the resistance.  

 


They still see us as something apart.

  

 


Most of the donors we engaged in conversations agreed that the disability movement needs funding but struggled to see how to include us into what they are already doing.

Disability intersects with democracy, protection and gender equality.

Yes, we need specific resources and at the same time, inclusion is necessary in the actions already put in place.  

 


Our accessibility is not enough. We could get there and participate thanks to WEI’s support, but many other women are missing from the conversation.

A

rriving is not enough: we need conditions to remain and continue participating in those spaces

. To guarantee accessibility for women with disability the following spaces are also needed:   

 


Dedicated spaces for rest 

 


Physical and menstrual hygiene accommodations  

 


Spaces where we can isolate from noise and crowds 

 


To invest in the participation of the feminist disabled leaders is to invest in the movements:

it strengthens the local networks that already exist to access resources, but also to weave alliances that survive the forum’s duration.   

 


Thank you to Women Enabled International for the technical assistance they provided, it opened up space for us, instead of just occupying it.

This time we had a table of our own: what comes next is that this stops being the exception.

  

 


In solidarity,  

 


Conectivas

 · October 2026.

Por muchos años hemos visto cómo organizaciones que prestan servicios a personas con discapacidad ocupan espacios como el Foro Centroamericano de Donantes (CADF) y este año gracias al apoyo de WEI pudimos estar en persona, poner nuestra propia voz y hacernos visibles donde solemos ser invisibles.

Nos siguen viendo como un punto a parte.

 

 

 


La mayoría de donantes con quienes conversamos dicen que necesitarían recursos específicos para discapacidad, pero no ven cómo incluirnos en lo que ya hacen.

title: Students Say Cornell Banning Frat Parties and Adding Investigators Insufficient
content:
“Nowhere among these measures is the institutional change that students demand,” said Students for a Democratic Cornell.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Cornell University has suspended parties and social events at fraternity houses for the remainder of the academic year, and will work with state police and their sexual assault investigators on future cases.

The changes came in response to outrage over a gang rape at the university in 2024 that has brought national attention to the issue of sexual violence on college campuses and the failures of administrations to address the problem.

Cornell’s President Michael Kotlikoff announced these changes on Tuesday, after weeks of protest against the administration’s mishandling of the 2024 case that have escalated into calls for Kotlikoff’s resignation.

In 2024, a Cornell student, known by the pseudonym Jane Doe, reported that she had been drugged and raped by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity on campus. Her case was initially dismissed by the district attorney after university police “summarized” her complaint while omitting mentions of sexual violence and drugging. In mid-September, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the university, the Chi Phi Fraternity, and the 7 men. Weeks later, NBC reported on court documents and text messages revealing conversations rife with the language of rape culture among the fraternity brothers. Subsequent reporting on the university’s mishandling of Jane Doe’s case prompted protests at Cornell and the reopening of her case by the district attorney.

“I have spent the past weeks listening to students, faculty, staff, parents, alumni, and trustees, who have shared their feelings of deep connection and sympathy with Jane Doe, anger and frustration that this could happen at Cornell, and outrage at the broader prevalence of sexual violence against women in our society,” Kotlikoff wrote in his announcement Tuesday.

In addition to suspending fraternity parties and working with New York State police “trauma-informed criminal investigators,” Koltikoff promised more staffing to support students who come forward with complaints of sexual assault.

But students at Cornell have called these measures insufficient.

Students for a Democratic Cornell (SDC), which organized a protest on campus on October 5 that was attended by thousands of students and faculty members, said that the measures demonstrate a refusal “to make institutional change on sexual violence.”

In a press release shared with Truthout, SDC explained that “Nowhere among these measures is the institutional change that students demand; specifically, there is no mention of reforming Cornell’s corrupt judicial system or an independent investigation not led by the Board of Trustees.”

The group contends that these measures allow the university to skirt the blame for its part in mishandling the 2024 case as well as its role in creating a “campus-wide epidemic” of sexual violence at Cornell.

Saya Taylor, a member of SDC, explained that the group “will continue to push until all of our demands are met – not just a select few that allow the administration to place blame on other parties.”

While the SDC does not view limiting fraternity parties as a useful measure in combatting sexual violence, other groups disagree – as was clear in the chants and slogans calling for banning frats entirely during the October 5 protest.

Kaori Quan of Cornell’s Graduate Student Union (CGSU) told Truthout that the barring of fraternity parties for the remainder of the academic year does not go far enough. “Stopping frat parties for a year does not address the systemic issues on campus that perpetuate rape culture,” she said, “namely, the intertwined nature of donor money and Greek life.”

“Until Greek life is off our campus entirely, Cornell will continue to prioritize the money it brings in over the health and safety of both students and workers.”

Referring to Cornell’s plan to work more closely with state police and investigators, Quan added that “so long as there is money in protecting Greek life, the campus police and the investigators they work with will answer to university administrators, not the students they supposedly protect.”

“CGSU’s stance is that working more closely with state police will do more harm than good,” Quan also told Truthout.
