author: Darius Okolla
title: Art is Maandamano
content:
In the weeks leading up to the storming of the Kenyan parliament in June 2024, I noticed a unique element in the type of people who attended the protests; they polled much younger, more enthusiastic, and some wore fairly pricey clothing. Not exactly what we have come to expect of Kenya’s rank-and-file rioters.


The quest for justice expressed through protest had found resonance with the type of Kenyan who would often be considered apolitical and indifferent to politics. They are not the group most invested in the mechanics of dealing with teargas, running battles, and placards. Something had changed, we just didn’t fully appreciate it yet. Somehow this apathetic regime had finally managed to enrage a unique, previously indifferent cluster: the middle-class Gen Zs.


In the heated political climate of mid-2024, Kenya witnessed an unprecedented wave of protests led largely by its Generation Z. While the immediate trigger was the controversial Finance Bill, the movement was distinguished not just by its scale but by its form. This was a revolution articulated through art, creativity, and a masterful use of the public space, demonstrating a profound and sophisticated handling of artistic freedom as a tool for resistance, mobilization, and memory. Music, visual art, and digital creativity have become the lifeblood of the movement, giving voice to the voiceless and fuelling calls for change.


Art meets maandamano 


For Kenyan Gen Zs, the expression of artistic freedom became the primary language of dissent. The typical protest, characterized by marches and chants, was subsumed into a broader, more creative spectacle. The streets of Nairobi transformed into a dynamic, open-air gallery. Visual art and the national flag were reclaimed as symbols of resistance, becoming trendy and powerful identifiers for a disillusioned youth. 


Placards and banners carried in the 35 of the 48 counties that experienced protests were not mere cardboard and paint; they were vessels of sharp, poetic copywriting that defined the identity of the grievances against the regime. These creations provided clarity in the face of obfuscating political rhetoric, energizing the masses and forging a visual alliance both on the ground and online.


This artistic fluency did not emerge in a vacuum. It was cultivated in the weekend street photography and videography sessions that had revitalized Nairobi’s central business district over the preceding years leading up to 2024. 


Initially facing pushback from the state and vulnerable to crime, these weekend artistic gatherings on Uhuru Highway and Kenyatta Avenue in the heart of the city were later endorsed by the Nairobi County government. This provided a crucial, non-political arena where Gen Zs developed a deep,

tactical familiarity

with the city streets. 


When the protests erupted, this cohort did not see an alien urban landscape; they saw a territory they already owned spatially and creatively. The outcome of these continuous artistic activities by Gen Zs became undeniably visible as the same streets became the stage for a powerful subculture of protest art.


The ground zero of the state’s reaction to artistic freedom was the abduction of George Kibet, aka Kibet Bull.  Kibet was abducted by suspected security officials on 24 December 2024, shortly after meeting Busia Senator Okiya Omtatah at the latter’s office in Nairobi. The digital cartoonist Gideon Kibet, known for his viral caricatured silhouettes of President William Ruto, was released on January 6th after international outcry about the Kenya government’s reaction to the pro-governance protests.


Music served as the movement’s heartbeat. Understanding that a revolution must be musical to sustain energy and unity, protesters curated and created songs that crystallized their ideas. The phenomenon went beyond spontaneous chanting. On streaming platforms like Spotify, users created public “

Maandamano

” playlists, turning individual expression into a collective, curated audio-visual activism. This protest music was highly derivative and communal—a form of common intellectual property borrowed from gospel, traditional tunes, sports chants, and pop music. Songs like Gidi Gidi Maji Maji’s

Unbwoggable

 from a previous political era were resurrected, while new chants like

Yote Yawezekana Bila…

 targeted contemporary figures. This demonstrated a generational understanding of the power of music to convey emotions and uncomfortable truths that …

author: Kerry Smith
title: Australian-Indian community rallies for youth democracy protests
content:
The Indian community organised rallies in four cities on October 18 in solidarity with the youth-led democracy protests in India. They called on the Anthony Albanese government to condemn the repression of protesters.

The protest movement erupted in response to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) removing about 130 million people from the electoral roll. The SIR tightens the identity document requirements people need to vote, and to which many do not have access.

The protests, led by student organisations and the Cockroach Janata Party, are being supported by opposition parties, human rights organisations and unions. They are calling for the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the reinstatement of voting rights.

The protests have been severely repressed by police, who have arrested thousands of young people, including protest leaders.

About 200 people joined the protest in Burramattagal/Parramatta where speakers, including from community members, students and representatives from the Greens and Socialist Alliance addressed the crowd

One student, who had travelled from Canberra to join the solidarity rally in Gadigal Country/Sydney, said protesters are standing for “human rights, accountability, justice, voting rights, constitutional rights and democracy”.

Another spoke of the violence towards women protesters, including “physical brutality, sexual harassment and assault”. “Women protesters have described being pushed, beaten, dragged and subjected to inappropriate touching by police. These are serious allegations that demand independent investigation and accountability.”

Ishita Chakrabarty, from Hindus for Human Rights, which organised the rally, said minorities had been profiled and targeted by police. She called on Hindus from privileged castes to stand up for others.

“I am absolutely horrified with what has been happening in our country,” Chakrabarty said. “I’m guilt ridden at the fact that I am not able to stand alongside my fellow brothers and sisters protesting the brutal RSS [Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh] regime.

“But I am glad to be here with so many of you who are refusing to sit back when Gyanesh Kumar wiped 130 million voters off the electoral roll.

“We have seen lynchings, mass arrests, prolonged trials, prohibitions on what to eat, who to love, who to marry … the exclusionary SIR has been especially targeting Muslims, who live under the constant fear of deportation.”

Former NSW Greens Senator Lee Rhiannon said SIR’s intent is to create an electoral advantage for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), by targeting minority communities that are less likely to vote for the BJP.

“This is a huge attack on Indian democracy and provides more evidence of the democratic decline in India under Modi’s BJP.”

Isaac Nellist, Socialist Alliance candidate for Balmain, told the crowd that Socialist Alliance stands in solidarity with the Gen Z protesters who, he said, are fighting for democracy.

“The youth-led movement is a massive inspiration to those fighting for a better world … we have also seen huge youth-led uprisings in France, Nepal and Bangladesh and the willingness of young people to put themselves on the line shows the enormous discontent with the status quo.”

Nellist said Albanese must condemn the brutal repression of protesters. “Labor claims to supports human rights but has said nothing about the repression of protesters or people being removed from the voting rolls.”

The loudest cheer of the evening was for Neha Bora, the Jawaharlal Nehru University student and All India Students Association president who has become the face of the youth movement.

The rally ended with chants of azadi (freedom), inquilab zindabad (long live the revolution) and lal salam (red salute).

About 100 people joined the rally at Victorian Parliament in Naarm/Melbourne, where a range of speakers including artists, poets and activists addressed the crowd. They highlighted the importance of standing up for India’s hard-won democratic rights and celebrated its cultural, linguistic, religious and gender diversity.

The gathering was disrupted by far-right protesters, who had also also gathered at Parliament to spout racist chants against Indians.

About 60 people joined the rally in Magan-djin/Brisbane, held at the statue of Indian independence leader Mahatma Gandhi. Speakers condemned the stripping of voting rights and the draconian police crackdown on protesters …

title: Attack on martyrs’ cemetery in Aleppo sparks protests in Rojava
content:
An attack on the martyrs’ cemetery in the Sheikh Maqsoud (Şêxmeqsûd) neighborhood of Aleppo has sparked protests in several cities across Rojava. Unidentified individuals attacked the cemetery and desecrated graves, particularly that of YPG commander Şervan Heleb. The Councils of Martyrs’ Families condemned the attack in a joint statement and demanded an immediate investigation into the incident and the prosecution of those responsible.


The statement was read publicly in Qamişlo, Hesekê, Girkê Legê, Çilaxa, Amûdê, Tirbespiyê, Dêrik, and Dirbêsiyê, among other locations. Relatives of fallen fighters and representatives of civil society organizations and institutions participated in the gatherings. The statements were delivered in both Kurdish and Arabic.


‘A direct attack on the dignity of our people’


In their statement, the Councils of Martyrs’ Families described the attack on the cemetery in Sheikh Maqsoud as a deliberate violation of the memory of the martyrs.


“Attacking the resting places and images of the martyrs is not simply an attack on a physical structure. It is a direct attack on our sacred values and the dignity of our people,” the statement read.


The families emphasized that this was not an isolated incident. They recalled that graves and memorial portraits had previously been targeted at the martyrs’ cemetery in Shaddadi (Şedadê) and in other cities.


“The repeated attacks demonstrate that the protection of these memorial sites is not guaranteed.”


Calls for a transparent investigation


The Councils of Martyrs’ Families called on the institutions and officials responsible for the integration process to fulfill their duty to protect the cemeteries and prevent further attacks. They demanded an immediate, transparent investigation and the public prosecution of those responsible.


“This act is unacceptable under any circumstances,” the councils declared. They emphasized that the perpetrators must be identified and held accountable to prevent further attacks on martyrs’ cemeteries.


In conclusion, the families reaffirmed their determination to protect the resting places and memory of the martyrs: “The graves and memory of our martyrs are among our most sacred values. We will defend their legacy until the very end.”

title: Fransa’da kitlesel eylemlerin ardından gözaltılar 2 bini aştı
content:
Fransa’da lise öğrencilerinin eğitimde eşitlik talebiyle başlattığı protestoların yüz binlerce kişinin katıldığı bir toplumsal harekete dönüşmesinin ardından, bugün hükümetin güvenlik politikaları, polis müdahaleleri ve sendikaların talepleri ülkenin gündemindeki yerini korudu.


17 Ekim’de ülke genelinde düzenlenen 110 gösteriye katılım, sendikalara göre 800 bine, İçişleri Bakanlığı’na göre 550 bine ulaştı. Yürüyüşlerin büyük bölümü barışçıl geçerken Paris, Marsilya, Lyon, Toulouse ve Limoges başta olmak üzere çeşitli kentlerde çatışmalar, yağma ve kundaklama olayları yaşandı.


İçişleri Bakanı Laurent Nuñez’in bugün yaptığı açıklamaya göre, gözaltı sayısı 2 bini, yaralanan polis, jandarma ve itfaiye personelinin sayısı ise 600’ü aştı.


Fransa: Öğrenci isyanı toplumsallaşıyor, 800 bin insan Cumartesi sokaktaydı


Bugün  00:34


Gözaltı bilançosu büyüyor


17 Ekim akşamı yaklaşık 400 olarak açıklanan gözaltı sayısı, gece boyunca süren polis operasyonlarının ardından hızla yükseldi.


Paris Emniyet Müdürlüğü’ne göre yalnızca başkentte 855 kişi gözaltına alındı. Yetkililer bu sayının tek bir gösteri günü için olağanüstü yüksek olduğunu belirtti.


Nuñez, kamu binalarına yönelik saldırılarla mağaza yağmalarından “aşırı sol” olarak nitelendirdiği grupları sorumlu tuttu.


Hükümet cezaları ağırlaştırmak istiyor


Başbakan Sébastien Lecornu, gösterilerin ardından yaptığı açıklamalarda şiddet olaylarına karışanların daha ağır yaptırımlarla karşılaşacağını söyledi.


Hükümet, gösteriler sırasında ortaya çıkan maddi zararın sorumlularından tahsil edilmesini amaçlayan ve kamuoyunda “zarar veren öder” (casseurs-payeurs) adıyla bilinen yasa tasarısının görüşmelerini hızlandırıyor.


Senatonun resmî takvimine göre tasarı 27 ve 28 Ekim’de Genel Kurul gündemine gelecek. Düzenleme, kamusal alandaki şiddet ve tahribat nedeniyle ortaya çıkan zararların sorumlularından karşılanmasına ilişkin yeni hükümler öngörüyor.


Lecornu, Adalet Bakanı Didier Migaud’un yarın (19 Ekim) başsavcılarla bir araya gelerek gözaltılar ve soruşturmalar kapsamında uygulanacak adli politikaları değerlendireceğini de açıkladı.


Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron ise bu akşam Fransa saatiyle 20.00’da (TSİ 21.00) halka seslenecek. Élysée Sarayı, Macron’un konuşmasından önce hükümet üyeleriyle bir güvenlik toplantısı yapacağını duyurdu.


CGT: “Hükümet toplumsal taleplere yanıt vermeli”


Hükümetin güvenlik ve cezalandırma odaklı açıklamalarına karşı Genel Emek Konfederasyonu (CGT), 17 Ekim gösterilerinin geniş katılımını hatırlatarak toplumsal taleplerin gündeme alınmasını istedi.


CGT, yaklaşık 800 bin kişinin katıldığını belirttiği eylemlerde öğrencilerin eğitim koşullarının yanı sıra alım gücündeki düşüş, hayat pahalılığı, emekli aylıkları ve kamu hizmetlerine ayrılan kaynakların yetersizliğinin de protesto edildiğini vurguladı.


Halkın kitlesel ve barışçıl biçimde dile getirdiği taleplere ısrarla kulak tıkayan hükümet, bugün şiddetin tırmanmasından siyasi olarak sorumludur.

–CGT, 17 Ekim 2026


CGT, hükümete öğrenci ve çalışan sendikalarıyla müzakere çağrısı yaparken, gösterilere katılımı engelleyen polis müdahalelerine de karşı çıktı.


5 Kasım’da ülke çapında grev


Fransa’da sendikalar, hükümetin sertleşen güvenlik politikalarına karşın toplumsal taleplerini gündemde tutmayı sürdürüyor.


CGT’nin yanı sıra Fransız Demokratik Emek Konfederasyonu (CFDT), İşçi Gücü (FO), Birleşik Sendikalar Federasyonu (FSU), Ulusal Özerk Sendikalar Birliği (UNSA) ve Dayanışma Sendikaları Birliği (Solidaires), 5 Kasım'da kamu ve özel sektör çalışanlarının katılımıyla yeni grev ve gösteriler düzenlemeyi planlıyor.


Sendikalar, ücretlerin ve emekli aylıklarının artırılmasını, kamu hizmetlerine daha fazla kaynak ayrılmasını ve hükümetin 2027 bütçesindeki kemer sıkma politikalarından vazgeçmesini talep ediyor.


Lise öğrencileri açısından ise öğretmen açığının giderilmesi, kalabalık sınıfların azaltılması, okulların fiziki koşullarının iyileştirilmesi ve yükseköğretime erişimde eşitlik talepleri gündemdeki yerini koruyor.


Kaynaklar: AFP, Associated Press, CGT, Le Monde, Reuters

author: Shalina Chatlani
title: “No Kings” Shifts Focus to Midterms With Early Voting Day of Action
content:
Over 5 million ballots have been cast, according to an estimate, as Trump faces a historic low in approval ratings.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Organizers launched more than 2,500 No Kings events across all 50 states and the District of Columbia Saturday, this time focusing their efforts on the midterm elections.

From roadside rallies to letter-writing campaigns and protest songs, this round of demonstrations aimed to get people to the polls early.

In the bustling and diverse neighborhood of Jackson Heights, Queens, where Bangladeshi street vendors whip up fuska — crispy, potato-filled shells — and Mexican taquerías serve up al pastor and carne asada, volunteers gathered at a popular local restaurant called The Queensboro. The organizers are part of the Jackson Heights chapter of Indivisible, one of the many grassroots organizations that have made No Kings demonstrations happen.

Arianne Mayer, 49, cofounded the chapter about two years ago after President Donald Trump was elected to his second term. On this “No Kings: Vote Early Day of Action”, she hands out pens and paper to volunteers to write letters to voters in battleground states, encouraging them to get out and cast their ballots as early as possible.

“The practice of mobilization of bodies is really helpful, especially in New York City, where you’re trying to mobilize many thousands of people,” Mayer said. “When you see those thousands of marches, you understand people everywhere are not OK with this, but it’s nice to have a different approach for this event. ”

Mayer, like many people here, said she was deeply frustrated and “disgusted” by the presence of federal immigration agents targeting her neighbors. Many people also said the federal government is implementing increasingly authoritarian policies.

Since summer 2025, the No Kings movement has held multiple massive demonstrations across thousands of sites around the country, attracting millions of people to protest against what they consider to be an overreach of government under the Trump Administration.

This time around organizers shifted their focus, understanding that the midterm elections will determine which political party controls Congress. If it’s the Democrats, they could put up roadblocks to Trump’s agenda. Organizers are hoping the day of early voting could not only increase the pool of voters, but also ease the burden on poll workers on Nov. 3, Election Day.

Voting is in full swing across dozens of states, with over 5 million ballots cast, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab. Trump faces a historic low in approval ratings.

In Minnesota folk musician Emmett Doyle took to a stage in downtown Minneapolis to perform Lluís Llach’s “L’Estaca,” written in the 1960s in protest of Francisco Franco’s dictatorship in Spain.

Doyle is one of 15 defendants facing federal felony conspiracy charges stemming from protests against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s crackdown in Minnesota.

“When I was getting pulled out of my truck by federal agents a couple months ago, one of the first things I asked them was, ‘Hey, is this about the songs?’ And they told me, ‘No, it’s about resisting ICE,’” Doyle said to the crowd of about 1,000. “I told them, ‘Well, you’re going to have to arrest all of Minneapolis if you want to hit me for that.’”

Diane Komsky, 67, drove an hour to the No Kings protest in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, because of the “madness in the White House,” she said.

“I want to give peace a real chance for families in the United States,” she said.

Mark Lyons of Centennial, Colorado, said he hadn’t been involved in much political activism or organizing before last year. Saturday’s protest was his fourth No Kings event.

With the midterms approaching, Lyons is hopeful that Democrats will take control of Congress and “put all kinds of checks and balances” on the Trump administration.

“They’ve been stealing the country blind for the last two years,” he said. “There has to be accountability, and it can’t be business as usual.”

At an event in the nation’s capital, 25-year-old Octavia Clapp said using her right to vote especially matters as Trump attempts to wield authority over voting. The Trump administration has spent more than a year in court battles with dozens of states and voting rights groups seeking to force states to provide sensitive voter data and curb voting by mail.

title: La CPM denunció ” la decisión política de desplegar la violencia ilegítima del Estado contra la protesta”
content:
La Comisión Provincial por la Memoria (CPM) presentó una denuncia penal para que se investigue a los responsables políticos y quienes ejecutaron la represión contra la marcha en defensa de la Universidad Pública por los delitos de abuso de autoridad, estrago, detención ilegal, torturas o malos tratos, entre otros.


Compartimos el comunicado de la CPM:


REPRESION A LA 5ª MARCHA FEDERAL UNIVERSITARIA


Denuncian la decisión política de desplegar la violencia ilegítima del estado contra la protesta


Por primera vez en una marcha convocada en defensa de la Universidad pública, las fuerzas de seguridad federales (Policía Federal, Gendarmería Nacional, Prefectura Naval y Policía de Seguridad Aeroportuaria) junto a la Policía de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires desplegaron, de manera planificada, ilegitima e indiscriminada, un brutal operativo represivo en la zona del Congreso de la Nación. La represión se extendió durante más de 3 horas y dejó al menos 550 personas afectadas y heridas por mas de 120 granadas de gases lacrimógenos, químicos, disparos con postas de goma y agua a presión lanzada por los camiones hidrantes. Una vez más se registró el ataque dirigido contra trabajadores/as de prensa, equipos sanitarios que atendían a las víctimas y organismos de derechos humanos que monitoreaban el despliegue de las fuerzas de seguridad, entre ellos, integrantes la Comisión Provincial por la Memoria. Al menos seis personas fueron detenidas arbitrariamente, entre ellas dos adolescentes. El organismo de derechos humanos, en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Presión de la Tortura, pidió que se investigue a los responsables políticos y quienes ejecutaron la represión por los delitos de abuso de autoridad, estrago, detención ilegal, torturas o malos tratos, entre otros.


Los registros de la represión ocurrida el pasado jueves en el Congreso de la Nación y alrededores, evidencian una vez más el uso ilegal y desproporcionado de la fuerza pública y la utilización irregular de armas menos letales: lanzamiento de granadas de gas lacrimógeno y gases químicos de manera indiscriminada, ataques dirigidos contra personas que deben ser particularmente protegidas por las tareas que cumplen, disparos con postas de goma o químicas en dirección horizontal o apuntando al cuerpo de las personas.


“Las conductas de las fuerzas de seguridad en comando conjunto excedieron los límites de la normativa vigente en el uso de la fuerza. Tales conductas ostentan una coordinación que permite establecer que sus acciones fueron ordenadas y ejecutadas por superiores jerárquicos con conocimiento y voluntad del ejercicio de la coerción por fuera del marco normativo e incumpliendo con los compromisos internacionales suscriptos por la República Argentina de rango constitucional, y que fuera ya denunciada por organismos internacionales de forma reciente”, resumió la Comisión Provincial por la Memoria en la denuncia penal presentada en las últimas horas del viernes.


En su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura, y en el marco del monitoreo de la represión a la protesta social que el organismo viene realizando desde la aplicación del protocolo antipiquetes junto al Comité Nacional de Prevención de la Tortura y el Mecanismo local de CABA, la CPM solicitó que se investigue a los responsables directos y funcionales por los hechos represivos ocurridos el pasado jueves por los delitos de estrago, torturas y apremios, detención funcional ilegal, incumplimiento de deberes y abuso de autoridad.


Como ya denunció el organismo ante otros hechos represivos, el despliegue ilegítimo de la violencia, los movimientos coordinados de las fuerzas y la reiteración de las acciones, evidencian que la represión fue planificada y programada por los máximos funcionarios responsables de las fuerzas de seguridad y del Ministerio de Seguridad de Nación.


Además, la denuncia señala que el operativo represivo no sólo ocasionó lesiones y daños a quienes participaban de la movilización sino que generó un peligro para el resto de las personas que, en horario y día hábil, transitaban por la vía pública. Cabe recordar que, una vez que los efectivos de seguridad sobrepasaron el vallado del Congreso, el operativo se desplegó por distintas calles de la ciudad en dirección hacia la avenida 9 de julio y hasta la Plaza de Mayo.

title: İzmir halkından EÜ’deki köpeklerin toplatılmasına tepki
content:
İzmir - Ege Üniversitesi Hayvan Hakları Topluluğu ve İzmir Yaşam Hakkı Savunucuları, dün gece Ege Üniversitesi Hayvan Hakları Topluluğu tarafından öğrencilerin beslediği eğitim alanındaki köpeklerin polis zoruyla toplatılmasına tepki göstermek için Bornova’da yürüyüş ve basın açıklaması düzenledi. Bornova Cumhuriyet Meydanı’ndan Küçükpark Meydanı’na yürüyen İzmirliler burada basın açıklaması gerçekleştirdi. Basın metnini Melodi Zengin okudu.

Ege Üniversitesi’nde 2022 yılında rektörlük tarafından Hayvan Hakları Topluluğu’na tahsis edilen, yaklaşık 160 köpeğin padoklar içinde öğrenciler tarafından bakıldığı yaşam alanına gece 00.00 sıralarında Bornova Belediyesi ve çevik kuvvet eşliğinde baskın yapılarak köpeklere el konulduğunu belirten Zengin, “Buna karşı çıkan öğrenciler ve hak savunucuları polis tarafından darp edildi, biber gazı sıkıldı, alanda darptan dolayı yaralananlar oldu ve bu işkence gözükmesin diye alandaki tüm elektrik kesildi. Bu alan, kampüsteki köpeklerin öğrencilerin harçlıklarından artırdıkları paralarla tedavi ettirdikleri, besledikleri, ilgilendikleri; çoğu öğrencinin de mezun olduktan sonra alandan bir köpeği sahiplenip memleketine götürdüğü bir alandı” dedi.

AKP’li kayyım rektör Musa Alcı’nın yaklaşık 6 ay önce Cumhurbaşkanı kararnamesiyle Ege Üniversitesi’ne rektör olarak atandığını belirten Zengin, “İlk icraatı okula eylem yasağı koymak olduktan sonra ikinci icraatı da gece yarısı çevik kuvvet eşliğinde yaşam alanından köpek toplatmak oldu. Musa Alcı’nın şikayeti üzerine boşaltılan alanın özel yurt inşaatı için kullanılacağına dair söylemleri duymaktayız. Musa Alcı bu üniversiteye rektör olmadan önce AKP’ye secde ederken bu köpekler bu kampüsteydi” diye konuştu.

Köpeklerin çoğunun çipli olduğunu ve alanın topluluğa Ege Üniversitesi Rektörlüğü tarafından tahsis edildiğini vurgulayan Zengin, “Yasa dışı hiçbir şey yoktu. Buna rağmen öğrencilerin yıllardır emek vererek kurduğu yaşam alanı, gece yarısı baskınıyla dağıtıldı. Dün gece Ege Üniversitesi öğrencileri ve hak savunucuları olarak eşi benzeri görülmemiş bir direniş sergiledik. Yaptıkları işkence belgelenemesin diye bölgedeki tüm elektriği kestiler. Hayvanlara ve hak savunucularına işkence ettiler. Ege Üniversitesi KYK yurdunda kalan öğrenciler, yurtlarının içinden bize ışık tutarak bu işkencenin belgelenmesini sağladılar” ifadelerini kullandı.

Onca itiraza ve görüşme talebine rağmen öğrenciler ve hak savunucularının darbedilerek köpeklerin Ege Üniversitesi’nden çalındığını belirten Zengin, “Şu an akıbetlerini bilmiyoruz. Toplama araçlarının önlerine yattık, hesap sorduk. Gecenin birinde, polis şiddetine, darp edilmeye ve biber gazına rağmen yaşamdan yana tavrımızı koyduk ve bir adım geri atmadık. Bugün Bornova Hükümet Konağı’nın önünden Bornova Belediyesi’ne yürüdük. Çünkü açıkça gördük ki mesele hayvanların yaşam hakkı olduğunda en muhalifinden en sağcısına kadar aynı düzenin aktörleri el ele durabiliyor” dedi.

‘Yasayı uygulamayacağız’ sözünü veren Bornova Belediye Başkanı Ömer Eşki’nin belediyesinin, çevik kuvvet eşliğinde öğrencilere ve hak savunucularına yönelik şiddetin yaşandığı operasyonun parçası olduğunu belirten Zengin, şunları söyledi: “Ömer Eşki ise çıkıp tek bir açıklama dahi yapmadı. Hayvanların yaşam hakkını savunduğunu söyleyenlerle bu hakkı ortadan kaldıran politikaları uygulayanlar arasındaki fark, işte tam da burada ortaya çıkıyor. Sözlerinizin değil, eylemlerinizin hesabını vereceksiniz. İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, her geçen gün yeni bir oran paylaşarak köpeklerin toplatıldığını söylüyordu. Son açıklamasında İzmir’i de hedef gösterdi. Ardından İstanbul’da selden etkilenen kedilerle videolar paylaşarak hayvan sevgisinden bahsetti. Siz kimi kandırıyorsunuz? Önce kısırlaştır, aşıla, yerinde yaşat politikasını ortadan kaldırdınız; yerine katliam yasasını getirdiniz.”

Tüm karşı duruşlara rağmen nefret pompalayarak, halkın vergilerini trollere akıtarak Türkiye tarihinin en kanlı hayvan düşmanı yasalarından birini çıkaran AKP iktidarının ve bu yasayı uygulayan yerel yönetimlerin sorumlu olduğunu vurgulayan Zengin, “Hayvanlara eziyet ve işkence pahasına yürütülen bu politikaların, yasanın ötesine geçen uygulamalarla hayvanlara ve hayvanların yaşam hakkını savunanlara yöneltilen şiddetin hesabını soracağız. Bornova Belediyesi de bu sorumluluktan kaçamayacak. Emri verenlerden de uygulayanlardan da hesap soracağız” ifadelerini kullandı.

Dün gece yaşananların unutulmasına asla izin vermeyeceklerini söyleyen Zengin …

author: anred
title: Apuntes apurados tras la movilización frente al Congreso: “En algún momento hay que pegar el salto”
content:
El textual del título, “En algún momento hay que pegar el salto”, fue dicho por un estudiante de secundaria (16 o 17 años) que estaba en la marcha frente al Congreso (ver video adjunto). Más precisamente, estas fueron sus palabras, cuando la represión ya se había desatado: “Es lógico tener miedo, pero en algún momento hay que pegar el salto y empezar a combatir, hacer lo que haga falta”. Uno de sus compañeros agregó: “Somos hijos de trabajadores, es importante que peleemos por todos”. Como toda persona medianamente informada, los pibes sabían lo que iba a pasar: el gobierno ordenaría una represión para meter miedo, como parte de su apuesta estratégica que es quebrar la voluntad de lucha del pueblo, desmovilizar. Esta vez, sin embargo, la jornada tuvo su particularidad. Hay elementos auspiciosos, a pesar del fracaso parlamentario en el intento de voltear el DNU 12/70 y la prepotencia gubernamental. Estos son algunos puntos fuertes que no debemos dejar pasar. Por Pablo Solana | Reporte Ancora / Imagen Andres Manrique


1. Conflicto universitario I: no fueron solo marchas.

 La toma del Palacio Pizzurno el 7 de octubre sorprendió al gobierno y envalentonó a los estudiantes. Entraron por la fuerza, mantuvieron una sentada y forzaron a las autoridades a atender el reclamo, todo en medio de un esquema de seguridad desbordado por el efecto sorpresa y por la decisión del grupo que planificó la toma. Con ese antecedente, se llegó al día 15 con asambleas en decenas de universidades, tomas en unas cuantas y no solo de Buenos Aires, vigilias, sentadas y semaforazos en colegios en distintas ciudades. En una lucha encabezada por dirigentes del sector poco propensos a la confrontación, la acción directa por abajo gana espacio.


2. Conflicto universitario II: ya nadie está a salvo.

 Un análisis más o menos compartido hasta ahora decía que el gobierno sabía que no era el mismo costo si reprimía a desocupados o jubilados revoltosos, que si se metía con la comunidad universitaria; que había un factor de clase (media, pequeño burguesa) que de algún modo “protegía” las movilizaciones por la universidad pública. Bueno, eso ya no pasa. A diferencia de las cuatro anteriores, esta marcha fue enfrentada sin contemplación. ¿Cuánto falta para que se animen a reprimir, también, una marcha por el 24 de marzo?


3. La movilización se sostiene a pesar de los gases.

 Ya venía pasando en marchas anteriores, pero esta vez la consistencia de la movilización popular se plasmó en una imagen poco habitual. Además del activismo que resiste, de la “juventud revueltista” que se va forjando en cada enfrentamiento con la cana, en el Congreso esta vez convivió el acto de la Universidad con escenas de enfrentamientos en paralelo, a pocos metros, sobre Hirigoyen y sobre Rivadavia. Los dirigentes de la FUA terminaron el acto lagrimeando por los gases. Si hace un año el Frente de Sindicatos Unidos, Fresu, había instalado un palco casi sobre avenida de Mayo para distanciarse de los revoltosos, esta vez el escenario estuvo lejos de las vallas, pero ocupando el centro de la Plaza. Es saludable la decisión de ocupar el espacio público pese a la certeza represiva, más allá de las críticas a la dirigencia de las Universidades.


4. “Es importante que peleemos por todo”.

 La convocatoria universitaria fue central, pero también estuvo en agenda la defensa de la Ley de Tierras (desdibujada por el paso atrás de la Corte), la Emergencia en Discapacidad, y la posibilidad de voltear el DNU 70/12. Por fuera de las agrupaciones estudiantiles y las columnas universitarias, se vio una cantidad importante de manifestantes que estaban allí “por todo”. El antecedente de la Marcha de la Bronca no es circunstancial: aún no es masivo, pero crece un ánimo de confrontación política en las calles contra el gobierno, que no se ciñe a tal o cual “defensa” reivindicativa puntual.


5. “Empezar a combatir, hacer lo que haga falta”.

 Dicha por un pibe de colegio, la frase debe ser puesta en su contexto y en la perspectiva de largo plazo. Pero la claridad de esa sentencia no se limita al activismo estudiantil que se va radicalizando. El enfrentamiento a la represión es cada vez más organizado. La influencia de la revuelta chilena gana espacio: esta vez se vieron baldes apaga-gases y guantes para devolverlos, a ambos lados de la plaza; también aparecieron músicos trompetistas, no ya en las columnas, sino acompañando al activismo de la resistencia: dando ánimo a quienes combaten. Esa mística …

author: Daniel Hunter
title: How Vermont shut down ICE
content:
This article

How Vermont shut down ICE

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


After Operation Metro Surge, the Trump administration moved to rein in the Bovino-style spectacle with its made-for-TV arrests. In an attempt to avoid another public outcry, Immigration and Customs Enforcement has quietly settled into a new rhythm.


Arrests have still increased month after month, reaching

a record high

 of roughly 51,000 people taken into ICE custody in August. This is part of a new surge — carried out in hospitals, courthouses and airports — with an intent to stay off the nightly news. As

The


New York Times


reported

, this phase is “captured mostly by grainy security camera footage, through cracked blinds and from behind closed doors.” 


This phase is also backed by a dragnet of data. At airports, ICE has been

running name matches with TSA to detain people

 at check-in counters and gates. It has found a backdoor into the country’s license-plate cameras: Records show local and state police

ran more than 4,000 immigration-related searches

 on Flock’s camera network in a single year. (Yet another reason

Flock cameras should not exist

.)


Perhaps surprisingly, much of the tech infrastructure driving ICE’s new surge is headquartered in … Vermont. The town of Williston, outside Burlington, is home to both ICE’s

Law Enforcement Support Center

, which houses the agency’s national tip line, and ICE’s National Criminal Analysis and Targeting Center, or NCATC, its social-media surveillance hub. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


As ICE tries a new approach, this new phase of resisting ICE requires moving to more offense — and the people of Vermont are offering us some clear lessons. 


Vermont resistance


Resistance started with the fight over flights. Early in Trump’s second term, activists

documented

 ICE moving detainees onto commercial flights out of Burlington’s airport — more than 450 people as of mid-July 2025, by their count. They showed up in airports as witnesses and disruptors, sometimes aided by empowered flight attendants. They forced an ICE retreat: organizers say

ICE hasn’t moved detainees through the airport in more than a year

.


More recently they’ve gone after the hard infrastructure. Sit-ins at the White Cap Business Park in Williston, where the NCATC facility is located, have led to arrests for allegedly blocking the entrance to the ICE offices, including

11 people in February and 13 in July.


After those arrests came some unusual twists, which speak volumes about the courage it takes to refuse unjust orders and to continue protesting in the face of repression.


Complicity and noncooperation


Responses to authoritarianism are as old as a time — many of the same dynamics from Vermont show up in the ancient story of Pharaoh and Moses.


Undeniably the most powerful person in his land, Pharaoh was the ultimate authoritarian. His big trick was taking beautiful work and turning it evil. Take the work of midwives, whose job is to usher life into the world — he turned that work into ugliness by ordering the Hebrew midwives to kill every newborn boy. 


But we all have a choice. And famously, several of the midwives refused. Their act of noncooperation with an unjust order is the reason Moses lived.


We are living through a moment when institution after institution is being turned toward evil. Some, like the Department of Justice, were already a mixed bag. But now it is being turned against the very logic of due process it claims to serve, as we’ve seen recently with the

criminal indictment of whistleblower Cassidy Hutchinson

. Other institutions, like the Environmental Protection Agency and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, are being perverted, with

great resistance from insiders

 who cling to the key values that these agencies were founded on.


Previous Coverage


The movement to defend the Minneapolis 15


In Vermont, the local prosecutor, Chittenden County State’s Attorney Sarah George, faced her own choice. When asked to

bring charges

 against the protesters who held the sit-ins, she repeatedly declined, citing limited resources. That makes sense: No one was harmed, and the protesters have a strong necessity defense — the argument that they were preventing an even greater harm. Every minute that ICE isn’t taking part in abducting people is good for the country.


Then came a bizarre turn of …

author: labor4pal
title: Dezionizing the University of California
content:
Sean Malloy and Ethnic Studies Council at UC

In September 2025, I wrote a guest post for Chris Newfield’s blog that highlighted the complicity of UC leadership and the Academic Senate in federal attacks on the university under the guise of combating antisemitism. In a follow-up guest post in May 2026, I identified Zionism as the driving force behind many of the external and internal threats to the UC and its faculty, staff, and students. Building on those earlier writings, I want to explore at some length what it would mean to “dezionize” the University of California. Anti-Zionism is not new and has existed since the creation of the Zionist political movement. Given the stakes of the current moment, however, it is not enough to be simply anti-Zionist in orientation. It is past time that we consider the real, material steps that we must take to both sever the UC’s connections to Zionism and address the current and past harms created by those connections.

Dezionization entails not only ending the UC’s complicity in the genocidal actions of the Israeli state (which would include divestment and the end of formal research and teaching collaborations with Israeli-linked entities), but also confronting the role of Zionist organizations, donors, Regents, and administrators in repression targeted at members of the university community. Since 2023, students, faculty, and staff have been the subject of individual discipline and surveillance while entire university policies have been written or re-written to institutionalize compulsory Zionism and stifle those who would speak out on behalf of Palestinian life. Confronting and redressing these individual and structural harms is a crucial element of any meaningful dezionization effort. And while addressing the issues of post-10/7 complicity and repression are important immediate goals, dezionization also requires an honest accounting of the historical role of Zionism at the UC. Building on the flawed but necessary efforts of universities to acknowledge their historical connections to slavery and indigenous genocide and disposession, dezionization must also involve acknowledging and at least attempting to redress past harms resulting from the UC’s long entanglement with Zionism.

Thanks for reading Ethnic Studies Council @ UC! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.Subscribe

Dezionization does not require that individual staff, faculty, or students renounce their own personal beliefs. It does insist that the UC as an institution should neither advance nor be beholden to a political project that has fueled genocide in historic Palestine and repression on our own campuses.

Dezionization is neither an easy task nor will it solve all of the problems currently confronting the UC. Ultimately, however, the current status quo is both immoral and untenable and those who care about the university’s future are going to need to commit to a series of radical changes which include, but are not limited to, confronting the corrosive effects of Zionism. If pursued correctly, the process of dezionization will itself contribute to making the university more democratic, anti-racist, and accountable to all. And while I have focused on the UC in this essay because it is where I have worked and organized for 21 years, my goal in writing this is to spark conversation about how we might move forward with dezionization in all the institutions in which we are entangled, wherever those might be.

Before considering what dezionization might look like in practice, it is important to directly confront the question of what Zionism is — and what it is not. Contemporary defenders of Israel have mounted an aggressive campaign asserting that Zionism is an integral part of Jewish religious andethnic identity. In a 2022 complaint filed against the UC Berkeley law school with the Department of Education targeting several student organizations who refused to platform Zionist speakers, attorneys Gabriel Groisman and Arsen Ostrovsky asserted that “A rejection of Zionism. . . is an act of antisemitism and direct assault upon the very core ethnic and racial identity of Jewish students.” Kenneth Marcus, a former George W. title: Arnavutlukta halkın isyanı mahkemelere yöneldi, Başbakan Rama saldırılarını sertleştiriyor
content:
Arnavutluk'ta yolsuzluk, eğitim harcamaları ve hayat pahalılığına karşı büyüyen protestolar pazartesi günü de sürdü. Başkentte Eğitim Bakanlığı önünde başlayan öğrenci gösterisi, polisle çatışmaların ardından başka bölgelere yayıldı.


Bir grup gösterici İstinaf Mahkemesi'nin kapı ve pencerelerini kırarak binaya girdi. Kosova merkezli haber ajansı KOHA, göstericilerin birkaç dakika sonra binayı terk ettiğini duyurdu. İspanyol haber ajansı EFE ise Arnavutluk'un A2 CNN televizyonuna dayanarak binada yangın çıktığını bildirdi.


Polis, mahkemeye yönelik saldırıyla bağlantılı beş kişiyi gözaltına aldı, 15 kişiyi de aramaya başladı. Gözaltına alınanlar arasında 16 yaşında bir çocuk var.  


Akşam saatlerinde Başbakanlık çevresinde yeniden çatışmalar yaşandı. Göstericiler polise taş, havai fişek ve Molotof kokteyli attı. Polis, göz yaşartıcı gaz ve tazyikli suyla müdahale etti. Özel harekât birimi RENEA da Başbakanlık çevresinde konuşlandırıldı. 


Sağlık Bakanlığı: 310 kişi yaralandı


Sağlık Bakanlığı'nın 19 Ekim saat 21:00'de açıkladığı bilançoya göre, gösterilerin başladığı 13 Ekim'den bu yana 310 kişi yaralandı. Yaralıların 191'i polis, 88'i gösterici, 31'i ise olaylar sırasında bölgede bulunan kişiler.


Pazartesi günü yaralananlar arasında bir çocuk ve iki basın mensubu da var. Bakanlık, hastanelerde tedavisi süren kişilerin durumunu izlediğini bildirdi.


Yüksek Mahkeme ve Parlamento binalarında yangın


14 Ekim'de göstericiler Meclis Başkanlığı'nın idari binasına girmişti. KOHA'nın haberine göre binadan belgeler dışarı atıldı ve bazı bölümleri ateşe verildi. Aynı gün Eğitim Bakanlığı ve diğer kamu binaları da saldırıların hedefi oldu.


17 Ekim'de Yüksek Mahkeme'nin bulunduğu binanın bir bölümünde yangın çıktı. Ancak sosyal medyada ileri sürüldüğü gibi mahkemenin bütünüyle yok edildiğine ilişkin haberler doğrulanmadı.


Polisin müdahelelerde plastik mermi, gaz ve tazyikli su kullanması da tartışma konusu oldu. Reuters'ın haberine göre Polis Genel Müdürü Skender Hita, orantısız güç kullanımı iddiaları nedeniyle 7 polis memurunu görevden uzaklaştırdı. 


1000 akademisyen: “Rama istifa etsin, geçici hükümet kurulsun”


19 Ekim'de yaklaşık bin öğretim üyesi, öğrenci hareketini destekleyen ve Başbakan Edi Rama'nın istifasını isteyen beş maddelik ortak bir bildiri imzaladı.


Bildirinin ilk maddesinde şu çağrı yer aldı:


Başbakan Rama'yı öğrencilerin taleplerini dinlemeye ve ülkenin yatışmasının yolunu açmaya çağırıyoruz. İstifasını ve kurumsal istikrarı, durumun sakinleşmesini ve yurttaşların iradesine saygıyı güvence altına alacak bir geçici hükümet kurulmasını istiyoruz.


Akademisyenler, güvenlik güçlerinden öğrencilere yönelik şiddete son vermelerini istedi ve hukuka aykırı emirleri uygulamamalarını hatırlattı.


Bildirinin göstericilere yönelik çağrısında da şöyle denildi:


Hükümete şiddet uygulamak ve protestoları gayrimeşru göstermek için gerekçe vermemek amacıyla işletmeleri, kamu mallarını ve özel mülkiyeti koruyun.


İmzacılar arasında muhalefetteki Demokrat Parti'ye yakın akademisyenler, milletvekilleri ve eski siyasetçiler de var. Demokrat Parti lideri Sali Berişa'nın kızı Argita Berişa ve damadı Jamarbër Malltezi de bildiriye imza koydular.  


Protestolar Trump'ın damadı Kushner'in kıyı projesiyle başladı 


Günümüzdeki öğrenci hareketinin kaynağında, mayısta başlayan çevre protestoları var.


Donald Trump'ın damadı Jared Kushner'in desteklediği, Adriyatik kıyısındaki Vjosa-Narta sulak alanında planlanan lüks turizm yatırımı, çevre örgütleriyle hükümeti karşı karşıya getirdi.


Çevre koruma statüsündeki alanlarda yapılaşmanın önünü açan düzenlemelere karşı başlayan hareket, flamingoların yaşadığı doğal alanlara izafeten “Flamingo Devrimi” olarak adlandırıldı. 


Avrupa Parlamentosu, haziranda Arnavutluk hükümetinden doğayı koruma statüsünü zayıflatan düzenlemeleri geri çekmesini istedi.


Avrupa Parlamentosu Yeşiller grubundan Hollandalı milletvekili Tineke Strik, 19 Ekim'de The Guardian'a verdiği demeçte şöyle dedi:


Arnavutluk hükümeti Flamingo Devrimi'ni ciddiye alsaydı bugün burada olmazdık.


Strik, Rama hükümetini Avrupa Birliği'nin çevre standartları Tiran'ı da bağlayıcı hâle gelmeden turizm projesinin işlemlerini hızlandırmaya çalışmakla suçladı.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Police Violence Increases as 800k Protesters Take to the Streets in France
content:
French leaders condemned the uprising, while the left highlighted escalating police brutality against young protesters.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On Saturday, France saw its largest nationwide protests in years, as popular outrage over the rising cost of living converged with a month-long student movement against the country’s neglected public education system.

Nearly 800,000 people took to the streets in over 140 cities across France on Saturday, according to France’s major labor union, the CGT. The protests were made up of high school and university students who have blockaded their schools over the past month, demanding better education conditions, as well as labor unions, who mobilized workers in protest of public service cuts, and remnants of the 2018 “Yellow Vests” movement.

Mass protests during the day transformed into riots as evening fell, with multiple city halls and offices set ablaze or otherwise damaged. Police arrested some 2,400 protesters.

French leaders have placed blame on the protesters and the far left, including on the far left political party La France Insoumise (LFI), or France Unbowed. In a televised address Sunday, French President Emmanuel Macron said that the riots were caused by “groups from the far left, joined by a number of delinquents and criminals,” and spoke of police who were injured.

Macron attempted to differentiate between protesters with “legitimate grievances” and those who rioted, while stating that the cost-of-living crisis began because of the war in Iran and its effect on the cost of fuel — for which, he added, France is blameless, as it has not taken part in this war.

But while fuel prices have soared due to the U.S. and Israel’s war on Iran, there are much deeper grievances within France. The underlying causes of the unrest include racism and Islamophobia within France, as well as a decade of austerity policies under Macron alongside the rise of the far-right in the context of an upcoming election.

Marine Le Pen, head of the far-right National Rally party, also blamed “the extreme left” for the protests and riots, and specifically the leader of LFI, Jean-Luc Mélenchon. For his part, U.S. President Donald Trump once again blamed immigration, posting on his social media network Truth Social that France needs to “Close [its] Borders and take control.”

After state officials held crisis meetings on Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced that cities across France would impose partial curfews beginning on Monday night.

But while state media and right-wing leaders blamed the left, it is the police that have undertaken massive violence against protestors over the past month, including on Saturday.

In Paris on Saturday, police used tear gas and stun grenades against protesters even before the start of the demonstrations. John Mullen, an activist living in Paris, wrote that police “beat and injured thousands of protestors” as well as journalists and bystanders, and argued that police violence increased popular anger and led protesters to riot.

Manel ben Boubaker, a French teacher who joined the demonstrations in Paris, explained to Truthout that a “peaceful student-led march” faced “intense tear gas.” She described how police “effectively prevented [a protest] from taking place in and around Place de la République: people were blocked from entering, trapped inside, forced to retreat, and repeatedly tear-gassed in the surrounding streets. The violence was not confined to isolated clashes. It shaped people’s ability to gather, move through the square, and demonstrate at all.”

Left-wing LFI leader Mélenchon also blamed the police for inciting violence. Writing on X, he said that protesters were “calm and joyful everywhere when the police aren’t around.”

Last week, French lawyers and rights groups accused police of inflicting “war-like injuries” on youth protesters over the course of the past few weeks of student movement protests. On October 5, a 15-year-old had his hand blown off by a police stun grenade outside of a school protest, and during Saturday’s protests, a 17-year-old permanently lost vision in one eye after police fired a tear gas canister that hit her in the face.

Rayyan Seriket, a member of the French Student Union Federation, said in an interview on Democracy Now! Monday that Macron is blaming protesters for violence …

title: Özgür Çelik’ten ameliyata alınan tutuklu Belediye Başkanı Mutlu’nun durumuna tepki: Tarih bu zulmü unutmayacak
content:
Silivri Cezaevi’nde tutuklu bulunan Bayrampaşa Belediye Başkanı Hasan Mutlu, sol bacağındaki rahatsızlık nedeniyle sabah saatlerinde ameliyata alındı. Mutlu, geçirdiği ameliyatın ardından yeniden cezaevine götürüldü.

Eylül 2025'te de aynı rahatsızlık nedeniyle acil olarak ameliyata alınan Mutlu, sol bacağındaki rahatsızlık nedeniyle sabah saatlerinde hastanede ameliyat edildi. Eylül ayında ameliyatın ardından taburcu olan Mutlu, dört gün sonra 13 Eylül’de kontrol ve tedavi süreci tamamlanamadan gözaltına alınmış, ardından tutuklanmıştı. Cezaevinde ağrıları ve şikâyetleri artan Mutlu, 22 Ekim’de Silivri Devlet Hastanesi’ne götürülerek kontrol edilmişti.

Tutuklu Bayrampaşa Belediye Başkanı Hasan Mutlu ameliyata alındı

Yeni Parti İstanbul İl Başkanı Özgür Çelik, Mutlu’nun ameliyatının ardından X hesabından açıklama yaptı. Mutlu’nun daha önce de aynı nedenle ameliyat olduğunu hatırlatan Çelik, duruma tepki gösterdi.

"Silivri Zindanı'nda tutuklu bulunan Bayrampaşa'nın seçilmiş Belediye Başkanı Hasan Mutlu bugün sabah saatlerinde hastaneye götürülmüş ve sol bacağından ameliyat olmuştur.

Ameliyatın ardından yeniden cezaevine götürülen başkanımızın daha önce de bu nedenle ameliyat olduğu bilinmekte olduğu halde tutuklu yargılanmaya devam ediyor.

Onlarca dosyası olmasına rağmen halkımızın canına kast edenler, uyuşturucu tacirleri ve suçlular tutuksuz yargılanıp sokaklarda serbestçe dolaşırken Hasan Mutlu'ya ve yol arkadaşlarımıza sadece muhalif olduğu ve Bayrampaşa'yı kazandığı için yapılan zulmü herkes görüyor.

Bu işe sebep olanların, yetkisi olduğu halde kullanmayanların, yasaları bile isteye çiğneyenlerin aldıkları ah çoğalıyor, veballeri iki dünyada da taşıyamayacakları kadar büyüyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Andy Mannix
title: Election Officials Fear Trump Has Compromised Cybersecurity Agency
content:
Critics say the administration has undermined an agency key to protecting election infrastructure ahead of the midterms.

Critics say the administration has undermined an agency key to protecting election infrastructure ahead of the midterms.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A few months into President Donald Trump’s second term, political appointees at the Department of Homeland Security made an unusual request of its agency focused on cybersecurity: Secretly acquire a voting machine and hack it.

The appointees wanted the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to procure the machine, examine it and report back the findings so they could be given to the White House, according to two former administration officials with knowledge of the request.

The proposition was shocking to CISA’s career staffers, according to one of the former officials. CISA typically worked to thwart hackers. Moreover, the agency had been directed not to alert the voting machine company if it uncovered flaws, contrary to its standard practices. The request made the CISA employees fear they were being asked to take part in political interference.

“My thought was they could keep it in their back pocket to invalidate any [election] results they don’t like,” one of the former officials said. “This goes against everything CISA represents.”

The CISA employees repeatedly told the political appointees that their request was impossible, in part because the agents capable of pulling off such an operation had just been laid off by Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency initiative. The appointees eventually stopped pressing CISA.

Though not acted on, the request shows how the Trump administration has tried to use the agency for its own ends while draining it of resources for one of its critical missions: protecting the nation’s voting systems.

In Trump’s second term, his administration has laid off or pushed out more than 1,000 CISA employees, shrinking the agency by about one-third. The president’s 2027 budget proposal would reduce funding for the agency by another $700 million, which could necessitate 900 additional layoffs.

In response, Democratic lawmakers have called for an investigation into CISA’s ability to do its job and demanded answers as to why federal funds are not being used to support election security as directed by Congress.

Since Trump signed the CISA Act in 2018, the agency has worked with state authorities and voting machine vendors to help protect election infrastructure from cyberattacks. During Trump’s second term, though, CISA has abandoned much of this work. Several state election authorities said the agency provided them no assistance — and no explanation for its absence — during the most critical planning stages for the upcoming midterms.

“There is a difference between deprioritizing and being nonexistent,” said Ryan Macias, an election technology and cybersecurity expert who has worked as a consultant for CISA. In 2025 and through mid-September 2026 — when the bulk of preparations for the election typically would have been completed — “they were nonexistent. Literally nonexistent.”

While Trump has repeatedly warned that America’s elections are vulnerable to hacking, in some cases repeating disproven claims, experts said his administration is undermining the federal government’s role in helping secure them.

Though CISA re-emerged in September with a last-minute security plan for the election, some state officials told ProPublica they fear that what is left of the agency has been compromised by a conspiracy-obsessed presidential administration. In recent months, in reviving debunked theories about the 2020 election, the Trump administration has declassified troves of records, including sensitive material that state officials provided to CISA. Some state authorities said they no longer trusted the administration enough to share information with CISA, a key to the agency’s success in past elections.

“They’ve violated the entire premise of that information-sharing relationship,” said one former high-ranking federal cybersecurity official who now advises state governments on national security. “There’s no fucking way they’re ever going to give any information to CISA. And it’s unclear if they ever will in the future.”

A spokesperson for the White House declined an interview request but defended Trump’s handling of election security in an …

content:
L'État en pleine surenchère sécuritaire, après l'

adoption de la loi

RIPOST

 , envoie des drones et des armes de guerre contre les lycéen·nes. Pendant ce temps

la métropole

 s'en donne aussi à coeur joie côté sécurité (qui ne relève pourtant pas de sa compétence mais la compétence n'est pas spécialement leur fort), et nos municipalités continuent à déployer le parc de caméras de surveillance pour outiller la police.


Bref c'est la rentrée et 2027 sent le soufre

 

!


Le

collectif Technopolice Lyon

 s'est créé à l'image d'initiatives similaires dans d'autres villes (Paris, Marseille, Montpellier…) impulsées par l'association La Quadrature du Net afin de documenter et lutter localement contre la surveillance de l'espace urbain et de la population à des fins policières ou de contrôle social.


On vous invite à la Luttine à des temps d'échange, de partage et d'autoformation sur ces questions :


> mercredi 4 novembre, 19H : Tour d'horizon des outils de la Technopolice, Surveillance, Contrôle et Fichage, et répertoire des moyens de luttes. On revoit les bases et on met à jour nos connaissances sur des sujets divers comme les caméras, la

VSA

, qui gère quoi en matière de sécurité, surveillance des manifs ou des outils numériques... L'occasion de faire un point sur nos droits, les bonnes pratiques et les outils de lutte (veille, documenter, cartographier, visibiliser...)


> 2 décembre, 19H : focus sur un instrument pour documenter et surveiller la surveillance (et pas seulement

 

!) : la Demande d'Accès aux Documents Administratifs. Que trouve-t-on en «

 

open data

 

»

 

? Que demander, à qui et comment

 

? Quels sont nos droits et nos recours

 

? Comment exploiter les documents reçus

 

?

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Social media ban may exclude children instead of protecting them, advocates warn
content:
Child rights advocates have warned that a proposed social media ban could restrict children’s access to information, education, expression, and participation without addressing the perpetrators and platforms responsible for online abuse.


The warning followed the Senate’s approval of Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) Act, on third and final reading on October 8.


The Senate approved the measure by a vote of 16-1, with no abstentions, advancing a proposal sponsored by Sen. Robinhood Padilla that would restrict minors’ access to digital services classified as high-risk.


Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns argued that the government must protect children from online exploitation, grooming, bullying, and other forms of digital harm without treating their access to digital spaces as the problem.


“Banning children from social media does not make the internet safe. It impedes children’s right to participation while the perpetrators remain,” said Teacher Elle Buntag, Salinlahi secretary general.


The group warned that restricting children’s access would not, by itself, establish whether platforms would respond more effectively to abuse or whether authorities would investigate and prosecute offenders more consistently.


Instead, Salinlahi called on the government to strengthen investigations into online sexual abuse and exploitation, require platforms to detect and remove abusive content, improve reporting and rescue mechanisms, and provide survivors with psychosocial and legal support.


“If the government’s answer to online abuse is simply to remove children from the platform, then we are asking children to bear the burden of a problem created by perpetrators and enabled by weak systems,” Buntag said.


The group maintained that children have rights to information, expression, education, participation, and connection in digital spaces, and urged the government to protect these rights while making online environments safer.


“The state must not confuse restricting children’s access with protecting children. Protection means making the digital spaces they inhabit safe and holding those who exploit them accountable,” Salinlahi said.


Different approaches


The debate over the Senate measure centers partly on whether an under-18 restriction offers a proportionate response to online harm or whether lawmakers should adopt age-specific safeguards.


Sen. Risa Hontiveros, the sole senator who voted against the measure, argued for a more targeted approach that would allow older adolescents to use social media with adequate safety measures.


Hontiveros had proposed restricting access for children under 13 while allowing those aged 13 to 18 to use social media if platforms provided adequate safeguards.


The Child Rights Network Philippines’ explainer questioned the basis for setting the minimum age at 18, and urged lawmakers to examine the evidence behind a blanket restriction before limiting children’s digital rights.


Sen. Win Gatchalian, a co-author and co-sponsor of the Senate measure, argued that aligning the age threshold with the legal definition of a child under existing laws would make enforcement more consistent and easier for authorities, according to the network’s explainer.


Padilla, meanwhile, said lawmakers could amend the measure after assessing its effects, and cited other countries’ experiences with restrictions and subsequent policy reviews, the explainer said.


The Child Rights Network challenged the idea that ease of enforcement should determine the age threshold, arguing that lawmakers must also consider the measure’s effects on children’s rights and daily lives.


The debate therefore goes beyond whether authorities can enforce an age restriction and asks whether the restriction would protect children effectively without imposing unnecessary limits on their participation.


Beyond entertainment


Child rights advocates said children use social media for more than entertainment, including research, learning, creative work, communication, and maintaining relationships.


The Child Rights Network noted that children also use digital platforms to connect with friends and peers and to communicate with parents working overseas.


Salinlahi argued that the government must account for these uses when designing online safety policies, rather than assuming that removing children from platforms would resolve the …

author: April Holcombe
title: Chinese youth in a very shit time of their lives
content:
Certain quarters of the internet are filling with content lauding contemporary China as an advanced, anti-imperialist, even socialist society. Its unrivalled high-speed rail network and its continued use of Communist jargon have encouraged some disillusioned Western youth to declare themselves in “a very Chinese time of my life”.

State-of-the-art infrastructure and Communist iconography have obvious appeal to a section of people living in decaying, imperialist and increasingly far-right-controlled Western capitalism. But there is a big difference between Instagram China, a Potemkin country showcased by influencers at the invitation of the tourism bureau and marketed to disillusioned Western youth, and the real China, a nuclear superpower ruled by bureaucrat-businessmen.  

Young Chinese people on social media—students, workers and the unemployed—use a very different kind of language than influencers do. Theirs is the language of alienation, exploitation and oppression in a society every bit as capitalist as our own.

“Involution”: an obscure word for a common problem

Ever heard of “involution”? Me neither. This obscure academic term, translated into Chinese (内卷

neijuan

), has entered common parlance among young people trapped in the country’s hypercompetitive economy. Literally meaning “inwardly curling”, anthropologists repurposed the term to describe activities that increase in complexity but lead nowhere. Chinese youth decided it captured their social predicament: instructed to work ever harder to stay ahead of their peers, they end up doing much more without being any better off.

Neijuan

describes many things: the gruelling hours at Big Tech companies; the notoriously competitive university entrance examinations; the apps pushing food delivery workers to ride ever faster; and the impossible social media-influenced beauty standards. The second character is now used as a standalone verb, meaning “to work or try too hard”.

Many young people who reject the

neijuan

 rat race opt instead to “lie flat” (躺平

tang ping

), a vibe somewhere between “quiet quitting” and “bedrotting”. The Ministry of State Security finds it deeply disturbing that anyone would want to lie flat, claiming in a Douyin (like TikTok) video that “an unnamed overseas organisation heavily funds ‘lying flat’ influencers, mass producing short videos promoting ‘anti-involution equals anti-exploitation’”.

Successive surveys show scepticism and pessimism rising sharply. In 2014, 62 percent of 10,000 respondents agreed that “effort is always rewarded in our country”; only 28 percent agreed a decade later. One-fifth blamed “the unfair economic system” for poverty in 2014; more than one-third did a decade later. Two-thirds agreed their families’ lives would improve from 2014-19, but less than half thought so for 2023-28.

“Graduation means unemployment”

University degrees once guaranteed well-paid government or tech jobs, providing the Communist Party’s dictatorship with a large, stable base of middle-class support. But now, often, “graduation means unemployment” (毕业即失业

biye ji shiye

). The gradual slowdown in economic growth has intensified competition for entry-level positions (more than 600 people, for example, applied for one basic Beijing office job in November 2025). Stable employment has given way to job flux. “I have family members who, since the early 2000s, never lost their jobs”, labour researcher Kevin Lin told

Red Flag

. “Last year, my cousin was laid off for the first time. Then he struggled to find another job, got laid off again, and is on to his third job.”

Unemployment is roughly twice the official figure of 5.2 percent, according to estimates by economist Li Daokui. “There are roughly 24 million long-term discouraged unemployed people, which is highly unfavourable for social stability”, the Tsinghua University academic told the China Macroeconomic Forum in July. The youth unemployment rate, officially hitting 17.9 percent that same month, has not included students since it soared past 25 percent in 2024, and hides a vast pool of underemployed youth working as little as one hour per week.

For the first time, the Communist Party’s most recent five-year plan includes no job-creation target. On the other hand, the government has a very clear target of 70 percent AI adoption across key industries by next year, inciting fears of layoffs among many IT workers. “I still can’t shake the feeling that I’m getting closer to being …

author: Unknown
title: Hatimoğulları'ndan Halk TV'ye dayanışma ziyareti: "Basını sansürlemekten vazgeçin"
content:
DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tülay Hatimoğulları, Parti Sözcüsü Ayşegül Doğan ve beraberindeki heyet, kayyum atanan Halk TV’nin Ankara temsilciliğine destek ziyaretinde bulundu.

Ziyaret sonrası açıklama yapan Hatimoğulları, kayyum atamasını kınadığını vurgulayarak şöyle konuştu:

"Heyetimizle birlikte sabahleyin aldığımız haber üzerine hızla buraya geldik. İstanbul'daki gelişmeleri takip ediyoruz. Halk TV'ye bir şafak operasyonuyla yüzlerce polisin baskın yapması asla kabul edilebilir bir şey değil. Kayyum rejimi bu ülkede parça parça tesis edildi. Belediyeler üzerinden başladı ve artık Türkiye'de kayyum atanmayan hiçbir şey kalmadı. Ticari kurumlardan tutalım da üniversitelere kadar ve bundan şu anda en çok muzdarip olan, gerçekten Türkiye'deki basın yayın kuruluşlarıdır, organlarıdır. Bunu kabul etmek mümkün değil. Halk TV'ye yapılan bu saldırıyı bir kez daha burada sizlerin huzurunda kınıyoruz.

Bir televizyonu yüzlerce polisle basmak demek, Türkiye'yi çok karanlık bir dehlize doğru hızla sürüklemek demektir ve biz buna defaatle tanıklık ettik. Bundan önce TELE1'de oldu ve son zamanlarda birçok kanalda gerçekleşti. Bugün şayet televizyonun sahibiyle ilgili başlatılmak istenen bir soruşturma varsa bu soruşturma televizyon kanalı kapatılarak yapılmaz. Burada televizyon kanalının kendi yayın akışına devam etmesine hiçbir şekilde müdahale etmeksizin bir soruşturma açılacaksa o soruşturma açılır. Ortada bir suç varsa onun gereklilikleri yerine getirilir. Ama ne yazık ki Türkiye'de artık bir şeye bahane üretmek için, basını sansürlemek, ekranları karartmak, kalemleri ve tuşları susturmak için önceden hazırlanmış olan hikâyeleri ortaya atıp, gerekçeler oluşturup toplumu böyle ikna edeceğini sanıyor bu iktidar. Ama yanılıyor. Bugün Halk TV'nin Türkiye'de milyonlarca izleyicisi var. Dolayısıyla milyonlarca izleyiciyi bu anlamıyla bu iktidarın yanıltamayacağını, bu şekilde bir karartmanın üstünün örtülemeyeceğini bilmesi gerekiyor. Bugün Türkiye'de tepkiler çok büyük. Bugün insanların duygusal olarak da siyasi olarak da toplumsal olarak da tepkileri son derece büyük."

Hatimoğulları, günlerdir Türkiye'nin gündemini meşgul eden fon kriziyle ilgili TBMM'de komisyon görüşmelerinin başladığına işaret ederek, şöyle devam etti:

"Böylesi bir zamanda televizyon ekranlarının karartılması aynı zamanda bu yolsuzlukların, yüzyılın fon vurgununun üzerini örtmek anlamına da geliyor. Çünkü bu anlamıyla muhalif olan bütün basını susturmak, mevcut olan iktidarla ilgili tek bir negatif yorum yapılmasına izin vermemek demek, bu dünyada görülmemiş bir basın sansürüdür. Kendi işlenen suçların üzerini örtmek için yargı yoluna başvurarak Türkiye'deki çeşitli kurumların, iktidarın elindeki kurumların devreye sokulmasıyla bu operasyonların gerçekleşmesi asla kabul edilebilir değildir. Buradan bir kez daha diyoruz ki Halk TV ekranlarını karartamazsınız. Yurttaşın haber alma hakkına müdahale edemezsiniz. Basının özgürce haber yapma hakkını elinden alamazsınız. Burada yapılan bu operasyon, şafak operasyonu ve yayın akışına doğrudan müdahale asla kabul edilemez. Bu müdahale Türkiye'deki milyonlarca yurttaşın haber alma hakkına yapılmış bir müdahaledir. Biz Halk TV'yle ve bütün Halk TV ailesiyle dayanışma içindeyiz. Sonuna kadar basın özgürlüğü için mücadele edeceğiz.

İnsanların ya da kurumların sosyal medya erişim hesaplarının engellenmesi, bu susturmaya eklenen yeni halkalar. Neredeyse her gün yüzlerce X hesabının engellendiğine, sosyal medya erişim engelinin olduğuna tanıklık ediyoruz. Bunları biz asla kabul etmiyoruz. Türkiye böyle manzaraları askerî darbe dönemlerinde görmüştür. Bu kadar ekranın karartıldığını, Kenan Evren'le bütünleşmiş olan 'gazeteler makas makas' dediği, böyle formüle edilen anlayışa biz şimdi ne yazık ki en ağır şekliyle bir kez daha tanıklık ediyoruz. Halk TV ailesine bir kez daha geçmiş olsun dileklerimizi iletiyoruz. Dayanışma içinde olduğumuzu bir kez daha ifade ediyoruz ve iktidara buradan net olarak sesleniyoruz. Basını sansürlemekten artık vazgeçin. Türkiye'yi karanlık bir tabloya sürüklemekten artık vazgeçin. Basını özgür olmayan bir ülkede özgürlükten ve demokrasiden asla bahsedilemez. Dayanışma içinde olmaya devam edeceğiz.

Şimdi biz burada bu konuşmamızı gerçekleştirirken arkadaşlarım aktardı. Polis şimdi Halk TV'nin Ankara ofisinin kapısına gelmiş durumda. Kuvvetle muhtemel İstanbul'da yaptıkları aramanın, taramanın, hukuki olmayan, yeri olmayan aramanın, taramanın birini daha galiba burada gerçekleştirecekler …

author: dev
title: Du backlash écologique au backlash IA
content:
À quand une psychanalyse des nouveaux contes de fées ? Le vent serait-il en train de tourner ? Entre les Docteur Frankenstein de l'IA qui prennent peur de leur créature et les manifestations contre l'implantation de data centers un peu partout aux USA, mais aussi maintenant en France, l' 'IA mania', qui avait débuté comme un cyber-conte de fées, commence à virer au cauchemar.


Les fournaises estivales devenues habituelles (« il ne fait que 30°C… ça va ») entretiennent des torpeurs mentales qui convergent opportunément avec un aveuglement salutaire pour la santé mentale, sacrée cause nationale. Peut-on être assez inconscient pour se féliciter de la douce moiteur de cet été indien sans en voir ni les causes, ni les conséquences à bien trop court terme ? Comme l'a montré une anthropologue, Elise Boutié, à propos des méga-feux en Californie, les victimes de la catastrophe elles-mêmes (du moins les survivants, car il y a eu des morts) restent souvent dans le déni quant à l'origine climatique de ces incendies et les attribuent au simple hasard

 [

1

]

, un peu comme Emmanuel Macron avec son « Qui aurait pu prédire... ? » en 2022. C'est sans doute la même chose avec l'IA. "Qu'est-ce qui réveille ?" se demandait Lacan. Il semble en tout cas facile de continuer à ignorer le vase communicant entre la courbe des investissements dans l'IA et celle des investissements dans la transition écologique, désormais nettement inférieurs

 [

2

]

. On s'alarme du niveau d'endettement, mais quid de ses causes ? Une transition chasse l'autre : il n'y aura pas assez pour le numérique et pour l'environnement. Et il pourrait ne pas y avoir assez pour aucun des deux. Oui, mais : aux USA, 75 projets de

data centers

 ont été annulés rien qu'au premier trimestre, sous la pression des citoyens de toute sorte

 [

3

]

. Républicains comme démocrates,

rednecks

 ou cols blancs se révoltent contre ces gigantesques aspirateurs à eau et à énergie.


Et en France ? On part de loin : le problème, médiatiquement et politiquement construit, ce sont, semble-t-il, les éoliennes, approuvées sur le principe et en théorie, mais en fait très mal tolérées quand elles s'implantent dans le champ d'à côté. L'IA et le numérique, au contraire, c'est virtuel : comme disent les élèves, « mais comment ça peut émettre du CO2, un téléphone ? Où est le pot d'échappement ? » Si l'on ajoute la fable de la prétendue neutralité du nucléaire sur le plan environnemental, et de son coût prétendument faible, le piège se referme. Et pourtant un rapport récent à la Commission Européenne montre que non seulement le coût de l'énergie produite par les nouveaux EPR sera plus de 3,5 fois supérieur à celui des renouvelables, mais aussi que ces EPR2 bénéficient d'aides à l'investissement inédites (et de conditions particulièrement arrangeantes et coûteuses pour le budget de l'État)

 [

4

]

. A l'heure où l'EPR de Flamanville est à nouveau à l'arrêt, à peine un an après sa mise en service complète, il y a de quoi faire réfléchir au prix de l'électricité.


La France cherche à "rester dans la course" : "attirer les investisseurs", c'est-à-dire d'abord les data centers ("Choose France"), cela veut dire offrir aux GAFAM sur un plateau nos ressources en eau, notre électricité pas (trop) chère, en échange de... hum. Pas de transferts technologiques en tout cas. Quant à Mistral, il semble avoir renoncé à la compétition sur les LLM pour faire du business autrement, en contrats avec les Américains (... et avec Total). "Mistral AI veut être présent", dixit, "sur toute la chaîne de valeur, des data centers aux applications chez les entreprises, pour contrer la domination américaine" : c'est justement le contraire qui est en train de se passer. Et la France, sous l'influence de ses start-ups (théoriquement) souveraines a longuement renâclé avant de finir par signer un texte présenté à l'ONU pour renforcer les mesures de sécurité sur l'IA, sans engagement clair cependant.


Faisons confiance à la communication de la "marque France" : les éléments de langage nous livrent le bon message, mais sous forme inversée. Encore du Lacan !


La suspension de l'incrédulité


Le décalage entre les discours toujours lénifiants des medias mainstream, qui continuent à distiller des éléments de langage semi-publicitaires, et le réel (épuisement des ressources, émissions gigantesques de CO2, siphonnage d'emplois, voire autonomisation inquiétante des machines, inversement proportionnelle à la dépendance des …
