author: groundxero
title: Blackboxes and Such: New Delhi on the Eve of 10 October, and the Seeds of India’s Undeclared Neo-Emergency
content:
The administrative streets of central New Delhi have now become a terrifying labyrinth of surveillance and armed lockdown – except for the VIP residents who live there, and the exotic nightly businesses that entertain them.

Mouli Sharma

 report on New Delhi on the eve of October 10.


 


10 October 2026, New Delhi:

 At the stroke of the midnight hour on Saturday in the administrative district of India’s capital, a quiet terror overtook the once – illusorily – safe expanse.


 


Preparations for the coming morning’s protest call, for people to take the streets all over the capital, not just the “designated” protest site of Jantar Mantar that has now become a designated “detention” site with an indefinite application of the controversial Section 163 (which empowers district and other magistrates to issue ‘special prohibitory orders’ and temporarily suspend constitutional freedoms in a given region during ’emergencies’) that has since expanded to the India Gate region, the Kashmere Gate region, and then through 54 other localities over ten days of continued protests, began early in the morning a day prior.


 


First, the office of the Joint Commissioner of Police (Transport Range) at Jai Singh Road issued an unprecedented order for the indefinite suspension of Metro rail entry and exit ways (as well as a reduction of train frequencies) in an unprecedented 57 stations, due to ostensible (and unspecified) suspicions of “mob movement”.


 


“In view of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations in New Delhi District in 10.10.2026 and the likelihood of unruly mob movement towards sensitive locations, frequency of Metro trains passing through the following Metro stations may be reduced and their entry/exit gates may be closed from 9:00 PM on 09.10.2026, continuing on 10.10.2026 till the situation normalises,” said the notice issued to the Managing Director of the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), Vikas Kumar on Friday.


 


A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymlayla Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing the petitions challenging the curbs imposed in Delhi, and observed on the same day that the total shutdown of the services would affect the rights of citizens who are entitled to avail them. But these services nevertheless remained closed from 9PM onwards, at least within the New Delhi region.


 


Next was a network blackout. Internet services were suspended in a 4km radius extending from the Jantar Mantar protest site an hour after the transport lockdown. A “top secret” circular from the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police Special Cell, Manishi Chandra, instructing private service providers including Airtel, VI, Jio, along with MTNL Delhi to indefinitely suspend internet services in the region began circulation during the late evening of the 9th, and the over 50 kilometre square expanse was consequently turned into a complete blackbox.


 


***


 


Pushing 10 PM outside the barricading of the site nearest to the Kerala Bhawan, while the networks were still on, the police were bashful. The speakers hanging from trees announced that any violations of “the prohibitions under the order” issued under Section 163 of the BNSS would be punishable by law, but when asked what these prohibitions are, or if this order could be produced such that public could indeed heed its prohibitions, officers present at the scene stood clueless.


 


Come dawn, Vikas Meena, Harnit Singh Sudan and Bharat Bhushan pulled a few reporters to the side, reassuring them that no press would be detained or obstructed during the protests, provided that press themselves did not obstruct the detentions of common folk.


 


“We request that you stay far away and do your job,” Meena said. “If we are detaining someone, don’t try to stop us or come close to us or film what is happening. We have no problem with the press, but recently, journalists have started intervening in our processes and asking questions while we conduct our operations, which makes it difficult for us to distinguish them as press.”


 


When pushed on the precise details and prohibitions listed in the magisterial order, though, Meena repeats a familiar refrain: “Where is the order? It must be somewhere. You’ll have to ask the New Delhi DCP. I’m not from the district, so I don’t know.”


 


Ask at the station, though, over a hundred journalists have, but DCP Sachin Sharma has refused to respond in plain terms, and even …

author: Lana Harb
title: Lebanon’s ‘pilot zone’ experiment: The case of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah
content:
Ihsan Yaghi’s house in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah is scorched from the inside. Piles of rubble fill the rooms she and her husband walk through to see what remains. What was not demolished by nearby Israeli strikes has been blackened by fire, with soot covering the interior walls. But Yaghi refuses to leave.


“Despite everything, this is still my land, and we have a very strong attachment to this land that we can’t let go of,” Yaghi tells Mada Masr.


Yaghi’s is one of roughly 100 families that have, since July, returned to Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, one of around 70 villages in southern Lebanon still under Israeli occupation, its residents displaced, its homes destroyed, its fields unreachable. The question of what should be done for the south, how to rebuild and how to return people to their land under continued occupation, has become one of the most pressing political questions in Lebanon. The answer currently on offer from the Lebanese government and its international partners is the “pilot zone.”


On July 21, the United States announced

the official commencement

 of pilot zone operations in three villages in southern Lebanon: Froun, Srifa and Zawtar al-Gharbiyah. The model emerged from the framework agreement — a US-mediated trilateral framework signed by Lebanon and Israel on June 26, under which the Lebanese military is to restore sovereign authority over all Lebanese territory pending Hezbollah’s disarmament. The implementation of pilot zones was to mark the agreement’s first practical step. The idea was that the Lebanese military would deploy to select villages in coordination with a limited Israeli withdrawal, allowing residents to return while reconstruction and services would be concentrated there. Those villages would serve as templates, proof that return and rebuilding are possible, and the model could then be replicated elsewhere in the south.


Mada Masr spoke to residents, municipal officials and others involved with the project to assess whether this is indeed a workable model for the south.


Two months in, it is falling short on nearly every measure residents say matters. People are returning to villages without water, electricity, schools or livelihoods, the prefabricated homes promised as a temporary fix have arrived at a fraction of the numbers requested, and there is no guarantee of safety so long as Israeli forces remain in position nearby and have not withdrawn.


Children walking by destroyed houses in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, July 26. Photo by Ammar Ammar.


The model also treats villages as isolated units, when in reality they depend on one another for schools, shops, hospitals and work, activists say. While experts on the South’s history of war and reconstruction say the current process marks a fundamental shift from previous rounds of war, for those in the south adopting a more radical position on resistance, another pathway must be found.


***


The pilot zone is a new model for the south. Political historian Nassib Chams tells Mada Masr that it emerged from a major shift in Lebanese politics: direct talks with Israel.


Such talks were not the case during the 2000 Israeli withdrawal, after 20 years of occupation, or after the 2006 war. That shift, he says, is what allowed the pilot zone project to come into being, and it gives Israel agency and authority over the return of southern Lebanese.


“This is the first time in Lebanese history that we see many Lebanese expressing that they want peace with Israel. So, while Israel was always stronger militarily, it is the first time there is this much political support for Israel,” he notes.


He adds that the project remains loosely defined, with the government yet to give residents a clear account of what the pilot zones entail.


“We may not know what is in it. We don’t know the details of what is happening in the negotiations. So far, we have not seen an Israeli withdrawal or anything. Israeli military operations are still continuing,” he says. “Are the people supposed to test if their villages are still habitable? It is unclear what they are trying to achieve when it is not even contingent on a full Israeli withdrawal,” he says.


Israeli forces in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, September 24. Photo by Ammar Ammar.


A resident of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, speaking on condition of anonymity, tells Mada Masr that Froun and Srifa have no Israeli presence at all, while Zawtar al-Gharbiyah has a relatively limited presence of Israeli troops compared to its twin …

title: Die Schüler:innen und Studierende in Italien gegen Meloni, das rassistiche Schuldekret und die Lebenshaltungskosten: „Geld für Schulen, nicht für Krieg“
content:
„

Das neue Schuldekret ist eine Schande: von der Obergrenze von 30 % für ausländische Schüler*innen in den Klassen über das Verbot des Ganzkörperschleiers für Schülerinnen bis hin zu den extrem hohen Geldstrafen für Eltern ausländischer Schüler*innen, die kein Italienisch lernen – das Maß ist voll! Schluss mit Hass und staatlichem Rassismus. Die Regierung Meloni und Bildungsminister Valditara versuchen, uns von den wahren Problemen im Schulwesen abzulenken: von den baufälligen Gebäuden über das seit langem bestehende Problem der prekären Beschäftigungsverhältnisse bei Lehrkräften und dem Schulpersonal (ATA) bis hin zum Personalmangel an den Schulen aufgrund ständiger Kürzungen. (…) Es ist an der Zeit, sich ein Beispiel an Frankreich zu nehmen und auf die Straße zu gehen

..“ ital.

Aufruf vom 11.10.2026 der USB Scuola

Die Studentenproteste breiten sich auf Italien aus

In Europa ist nicht nur ein Schulstreit ausgebrochen. Es handelt sich nicht nur um jugendliche Unzufriedenheit. Es ist die Revolte einer Generation gegen ein System, das junge Menschen in überfüllte Klassenzimmer und prekäre Einrichtungen schickt, während es Milliarden für Krieg und Aufrüstung ausgibt.


Von den römischen Gymnasien bis hin zu den Schulen in Genua, Turin und Neapel ist die Besetzung zu einem politischen Zeichen geworden: Schluss mit der Finanzierung des Todes und Streichung der Mittel für das Leben.


Gestern wurde zu einem allgemeinen Studentenstreik aufgerufen. Am 30. Oktober beraten die Gruppen über eine gemeinsame Mobilisierung mit den Arbeitnehmern. Diese Perspektive ist es, die der Regierung wirklich Angst macht: nicht ein isolierter Protest, sondern ein Bündnis zwischen Studenten und Arbeitnehmern, zwischen Antiimperialisten, zwischen Menschen ohne Wohnung und ohne Zukunft.

Artikel vom 17.10.2026 auf mpr21

Tausende, laut Organisatoren rund 20, zogen durch die Straßen der Hauptstadt. Anschließend wurden Feuerwerkskörper und Flaschen auf die Sicherheitskräfte geworfen. title: KJK: Let us defend the revolution of humanity
content:

We call on all humanity, particularly the people of Rojava, their families and comrades, to uphold the values created by our fighters for a dignified life and freedom, and to participate in building a democratic and free society as a fulfilment of their commitment to the martyrs' memory.”

The disgraceful attacks carried out for days against the values of the Kurdish people, particularly in Hasakah, constitute a clear provocation and a policy aimed at removing Kurds from the region. It must be understood that those who seek to exploit the struggle of the people and women of Rojava, based on the perspective of coexistence and a Democratic Syria, and their approach of establishing democratic relations with the Syrian state for their own genocidal and liquidationist objectives will be defeated.

author: Cas Smith
title: Land Forces weapons expo protested in a time of genocide
content:
Around 2000 anti-war activists took to the streets on October 6, in a strong rebuke to the weapons’ manufacturers displaying their wares at the Land Forces International Land Defence Exposition and Western Australian Labor, which welcomed it.

The rally, one of the biggest in recent years, began at Yagan Square near Northbridge, before marching through the city to Elizabeth Quay, close to the Perth Convention Centre.

A “security area” had been set up around the expo venue, which included the Elizabeth Quay train station and several sections of surrounding streets.

A new law, the Land Forces (Special Powers) Act 2026, gave police the “ability to establish checkpoints, cordons, and roadblocks, while also searching people, bags, and vehicles, and issue lawful directions for a 10-day period”, until October 10.

Alongside this, several activists had been told they were banned from the security area, and could face fines of up to $36,000 and three years in prison if they challenged this.

The media coverage of these repressive security initiatives — to which WA Premier Roger Cook had allocated $11.5 million — may have encouraged people to come to the rally, which was hosted by WA Anti-War Collective, Stop AUKUS WA, Nuclear Free WA, Independent and Peaceful Australia Network (IPAN), Friends of Palestine WA (FOPWA), Students for Palestine WA, Right To Protest WA and Extinction Rebellion Western Australia.

It included several creative aspects, including a flash mob dance to the tune of the Temptations’ song “War” and a performance by Drummers for Climate Action.

Noongar Elders Uncle Headley Hayward and Uncle Herbert Bropho gave the Welcome to Country. Adrian Glamorgan (Independent and Peaceful Australia Network and Stop AUKUS WA), Danica Scott (Stop AUKUS WA and Freiends of Palestine WA), Greens MLC Sophie McNeill, Rojin Didari (Students for Palestine WA) and Berlin Guerrero (Migrante and International People’s Struggle) addressed the protest.

Sam Wainwright (Stop AUKUS WA), who MCed the rally, said Labor’s decision to roll out the red carpet for weapons manufacturers indicated his priorities.

“[Land Forces] comes in the context of a worldwide increase in military expenditure, including a 50% increase in military expenditure by Donald Trump. It comes in the context of the genocide in Gaza, and a climate emergency,” Wainwright said.

“It poses the question: What is the real response of our rulers to what are known as the ‘poly crises’ of capitalism. Is it not repression at home and war abroad?”

It was particularly horrific that weapons used in Gaza would be on display at the exhibition, Wainwright added.

“For the last three years, we have begged this federal government to stop sending arms to Israel and to cancel bilateral military ties, because it’s the one thing you’d do if you were serious about stopping the genocide.

“Labor won’t, because it has committed to making Australia one of the 10 major weapons exporters in the world. Roger Cook has said he wants to make weapons exports the number two industry in WA. The place of Israel in the military industrial complex means deepening bilateral military ties with that state.”

Elbit Systems and Rafael were among the Israeli weapons companies featured at Land Forces, alongside Lockheed Martin, which constructs the F-35 fighter jets used in much of the destruction of Gaza.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Army Suicide Reminds of Recurring Issues with Bullying and Hazing in the Military
content:
A RECENT CASE in which a female Army first lieutenant committed suicide is being investigated as a potential case of bullying. The first lieutenant in question, surnamed Wang, jumped to her death from a building at the Army’s 206th Brigade base in Hsinchu County on September 30th. An audio recording that was posted on Threads on October 12th shows a man berating Wang for failing to heed instructions, leading to the bullying allegations.

The Ministry of National Defense has vowed that the case is being investigated and that Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo is attentive to its developments. This would not be the only case in recent years in which a suicide in the military has been linked to bullying.

In November 2020, a similar case emerged of a corporal surnamed Liu stationed in the Eighth Army Command’s 203rd Brigade in Danei District, Tainan, who died by hanging. Liu, too, was reportedly bullied by his superiors and peers.

The most famous case of a death in the military thought to have resulted from bullying in the military would be the death of cadet Hung Chung-chiu in July 2013. Hung is thought to have been bullied by his superiors and peers shortly before his discharge from mandatory military service, as a form of hazing or as retribution against him before his service ended. The lack of government transparency in the wake of the death, with allegations of a cover-up, led to the Citizen 1985 movement, one of the major predecessor movements of the 2014 Sunflower Movement.

The government is likely sensitive to the optics of bullying in the military. The Hung Chung-chiu case, as well as the military’s perceived lack of transparency, is thought to be a major factor in public distrust in the military. This proves an important issue for the government at a time when it seeks to boost recruitment numbers, so as to counter rising Chinese threats.

At the same time, one notes that the military was an authoritarian institution during the many decades of the White Terror. In the course of the White Terror, the military served as the enforcer of the KMT state, and it conducted many of the political killings during the purges that took place then. Deaths due to bullying or hazing, as well as the cover-up of such deaths, were a common occurrence during the authoritarian era. In fact, incidents such as the Hung Chung-chiu case were relatively common during the authoritarian era and were mostly covered up, such that a single death in post-authoritarian Taiwan would garner such attention.

To this extent, one notes that cases of workplace bullying in government that have resulted in suicides have received greater scrutiny. Cases in point include the suicide of a civil servant surnamed Wu who worked in the Ministry of Labor in 2024. After the death of deputy trade representative Yen Huai-hsing in March at age 53, allegations that Yen was bullied by her superiors also emerged. Though such issues regarding workplace bullying have not always been put in the same frame as deaths in the military, insofar as both are, in some sense, public sector workers

author: Sharon Zhang
title: US Reportedly Considering Dropping “Mother of All Bombs” on Iran
content:
The US has only ever dropped a MOAB once before — on Afghanistan in 2017.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The Pentagon has reportedly drawn up plans to attack Iran with the “Mother of All Bombs” (MOAB), the largest conventional weapon ever developed by weight, after being ordered by President Donald Trump to develop strike plans for targets that include “a lot of energy infrastructure.”

Energy infrastructure is largely considered to be civilian in nature and thus protected under international law.

The GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, or MOAB, is the U.S.’s largest non-nuclear bomb. It is designed to explode a few feet before hitting the ground, creating a massive blast and shooting out plumes of fire, destroying everything within a 0.6 mile radius and causing damage within one mile. It is not an effective weapon against targets like Iran’s highly fortified nuclear infrastructure, experts said, because it does not penetrate deep below ground.

Legal experts have previously raised concerns about disproportionate harm to civilians in the U.S.’s use of 2,000-pound bombs on Iran. The MOAB, by contrast, weighs 21,000 pounds, and has a much larger blast radius.

The MOAB options were first reported by CNN and confirmed by CBS. The MOAB was first tested in 2003, as the George W. Bush administration developed its strategy of “shock and awe” in Iraq; as CNN notes, at the time, the Pentagon said it hoped that the mere existence of the MOAB was enough to cause “psychological” damage to the enemy.

The bomb has only been used once before in combat, by Trump. In 2017, the U.S. dropped a MOAB east of Kabul, in Nangarhar, Afghanistan, a province with a population of 1.5 million people. The Pentagon claimed that more than 94 ISIS members were killed in the attack. No civilian deaths were reported; some reports said that the area had long been evacuated. But some local reports suggested that civilians were harmed, and critics afterward noted that the U.S. had previously never considered using the bomb in Iraq because of civilian damage concerns. It caused a mushroom cloud visible from 20 miles away.

.@USFOR_A releases GBU-43 #MOAB strike video against #ISIS-K cave complex, #Nangarhar, #Afghanistan #DefeatDaeshhttps://t.co/MuhU7JXuNn pic.twitter.com/qBqptpuzbE

It is unclear what the timing of such an attack on Iran would be. Trump has said that he won’t relaunch strikes against Iran before the midterms, but reports have also said that his administration has drawn up plans to do just that. CNN said advisers privately wonder if Trump’s pledges are definitive.

CNN additionally found that the Trump administration and military planners have spent recent weeks looking for “an off-ramp that gives Trump a ‘symbolic’ win — at minimum — he can try to sell to the American people without preventing a potential diplomatic breakthrough, starting with an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.” This includes plans that could amount to strikes for a “fireworks show,” after which Trump would declare victory.

“The Trump administration’s threats to commit war crimes in Iran cannot be normalized,” said Ryan Costello, policy director for the National Iranian American Council, in response to the MOAB report. “President Trump acts on many of his threats, necessitating more urgent action to bring this illegal war of choice to a definitive end.”

The Trump administration has already been under fire for killing civilians in Iran, with several attacks having been described as war crimes by UN experts. This includes the February 28 strike on an elementary school in Minab, Iran, which killed 160 people, including 123 children.

Pentagon officials said in May that their report on the Minab attack, which is the single worst strike on civilians by the U.S. in the 21st century, was nearing conclusion. But Bloomberg reported on Thursday that the Pentagon is planning to withhold the report at least until after the midterm elections next month, and potentially even longer.

The attempt to withhold information about the U.S.’s conduct in the deeply unpopular war has incensed critics.

Defense Secretary Pete “Hegseth eliminated staff who prevent civilian casualties, called the rules of engagement safeguarding civilians ‘stupid,’ & now he’s covering up the report on the Minab school strike that killed over 120 children,” said Sen. Chris …

author: By Elvis Takahashi Mantello, Contributor
title: Marco Rubio’s Visit to Athens Raises Questions About Western Democracy
content:
Athens, Greece – U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Athens to talk about democracy and to deepen political ties with the right-wing Greek government. However, his visit also stirred public outcry, with demonstrators showing anxiety about Greece’s growing militarization and the potential to get entangled in foreign conflicts.


Rubio arrived last Tuesday evening for the sixth round of the U.S.-Greece Strategic Dialogue. By the next day, he stood on Pnyx Hill, the Acropolis behind him, and delivered a speech that invoked ancient Greece to defend Trump’s “America First” approach. He called on Europeans to “awaken from their long slumber.” His nationalist speech called for dominance in supply chains and future technologies.

CNN

 and the

Washington Post

 viewed the speech as a campaign ad for his potential candidacy in the 2028 U.S. elections.


Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis described Greek-U.S. relations as being “

at the highest level ever

,” while Rubio referred to Greece as “such a strong partner.” The leaders announced that Greece agreed to spend up to

$4 billion on a U.S. arms deal

 along with a joint counterterrorism program.


Yet, the streets of Greece during Rubio’s visit told a different story.


Rubio’s Arrival and the Protests


During Rubio’s arrival,

hundreds of demonstrators

 took to the streets of Athens in opposition to his visit.


Among them was Omar Almaani, a Palestinian living in Norway, who drove a van to Greece covered with images of Palestinian suffering and statistical figures.


He called the project “Witness on Wheels” to raise public awareness. “All these numbers are not just aesthetics,” he said. “They are human beings. Every one of them has their own life, their own smile, their own history.”


Almaani said he lost friends, acquaintances, and family members in Gaza. Despite such circumstances, he urged that protests in solidarity with Palestine continue.


“Whatever is gonna happen, it will not stop us; it will not scare us,” he said. “We will stay for the truth, we will stay for humanity.”


Giannis Sifakakis of the Stop the War Coalition spoke at the same protest. “We are here today because we are fighting for Palestine and against U.S. imperialism,” he said. “The Greek government is going deeper into the war on the side of Trump and Netanyahu.”


On the evening of Wednesday, October 7, despite the

24-hour public gathering ban in Athens

, a crowd of pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered in front of the Israeli Embassy. They organized to mark

three years of genocide in Gaza

.


Protesters gather in front of the Israeli Embassy on October 7, 2026, in Athens, Greece. Photo contributed by Elvis Takahashi Mantello.


Greg, a Greek demonstrator, said he was there for two main reasons, “one, to honor the Palestinian resistance and two, to shout against the genocidal settler colonial regime of Israel.”


Konstantina Kartsioti, an organizer for the Anti-Imperialist Movement, linked the protest with Rubio’s visit, stating, “the collaboration of the Greek state with the Zionist entity and U.S. imperialism.”


“We are telling Palestinians they have the right to resist and the right to return,” she said. “We hope to join the resistance from Greece to Gaza, from Gaza to the West Bank, to Jenin, to Nablus … We unite, and we are telling [people] we must fight and win.”


Why Greece Matters to Rubio


The Strategic Dialogue covered energy, defense, trade, technology and investment. Discussions also centered on U.S. companies such as

ExxonMobil and Chevron, the Vertical Corridor and electricity interconnections

 linking Greece with regional allies.


Greece’s ambition is to strengthen its role as a

regional energy hub

, distributing American liquified natural gas (LNG) to its European markets. The U.S., on the other hand, eyes

Souda Bay and Alexandroupoli

, which are both military logistics bases that project power across the Eastern Mediterranean, Eastern Europe, and the Middle East.


These discussions highlight the impact of Rubio’s visit by demonstrating how Greece serves as the perfect “model NATO ally,” combining strong self-defense investments with a dominance in strategic energy and logistics networks that support American interests.


The Contradiction


Rubio’s openly American-centric speech on Pnyx Hill talked about the ideals of protecting democracy and its future based on ideological goals.

title: Fermiamo la propaganda di guerra, inceppiamo la macchina bellica, disertiamo gli eserciti
content:
La propaganda militarista continua a crescere ogni giorno sia a livello nazionale che internazionale.


Il messaggio delle istituzioni veicolato dai media è sempre più chiaro: dobbiamo prepararci alla guerra per difendere la nazione. L’aumento delle spese militari e delle missioni all’estero, il rafforzamento del potere del complesso militare-industriale, la capillarità della penetrazione dell’esercito nelle scuole e nelle università, la sempre maggior presenza dei soldati nelle strade delle città sono tutti segnali chiari della direzione in cui si sta andando.


In questo quadro si inserisce la questione della reintroduzione della leva militare in vari paesi europei. Se in Germania questo processo è già in fase avanzata, nel nostro paese, per ora, il modello scelto è quello di un rafforzamento dell’arruolamento, aumentando la propaganda soprattutto negli istituti scolastici, preparando così il terreno per il futuro ad un’eventuale reintroduzione della leva militare.


In questo scenario è di vitale importanza continuare a praticare l’antimilitarismo in tutti gli ambiti sociali e in tutte le occasioni possibili.


Sosteniamo lo sciopero internazionale contro la guerra indetto dalla CIT Confederazione Internazionale dei lavoratori per il 30 ottobre e le manifestazioni del 31 ottobre.


Indichiamo nel 4 novembre, giornata delle forze armate e dell’unità nazionale, una data significativa per sviluppare iniziative sui vari territori.


Appoggiamo le mobilitazioni che si stanno sviluppando a livello studentesco e territoriale contro il reclutamento per l’esercito e contro ogni ipotesi di reintroduzione della leva.

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.

author: webadmin
title: All Warning, No Action?
content:
As more hunts receive police warnings and notices, are they a route to meaningful action, or a substitute for it?


Many of you cannot have failed to notice that we are writing more and more about hunts being issued with Community Protection Warnings (CPWs) and, occasionally, the CPW’s big sister, the Community Protection Notice (CPN). The former of course precedes the latter.


What in the puck is this? The Puckeridge and Essex Hunts have had 3 CPWs and a CPN and they still ignore them. Image: East Herts Hunt Sabs.


The Community Protection Notice system, including the requirement to issue a warning first, was introduced in 2014 by David Cameron’s Conservative-led coalition government, under then Home Secretary Theresa May as part of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime & Policing Act 2014.


The irony that these measures are now being used, more and more, to regulate the conduct of fox hunts, an activity that has recently been publicly defended by Cameron, is not lost on us.


A CPW is not a criminal conviction. Ignoring one is not, in itself, a criminal offence, and there is no automatic penalty for failing to comply. If the behaviour continues, the police can escalate matters by issuing a CPN. Unlike a warning, a CPN imposes legally enforceable requirements, and breaching those requirements without reasonable excuse is a criminal offence.


Warning, Warning, Warning. No Action


Most recently, Kernow Hunt Sabs revealed that one of their local hunts, the Four Burrow Hunt, has received a Community Protection Warning. One important point is that Devon & Cornwall Police have not issued a press release on the conditions or areas affected, although details have been

published elsewhere

.


Masked terrier-men on Dartmoor having just been caught about to dig a fox out of a badger sett. Image: Plymouth and West Devon Hunt Saboteurs 2026.


The same police force has been busy issuing these warnings. Plymouth & West Devon Hunt Saboteurs also announced that one has been issued to the Dartmoor Hunt. Although Devon & Cornwall police confirmed its existence in response to a Freedom of Information request, they have not published details of the locations concerned or the conditions the hunt must comply with.


The Dartmoor Hunt killing a fox in March 2026. Image: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs


Earlier this year, the force also issued a warning to the North Cornwall Hunt. While its

press release

 did not name the hunt, referring instead to a ‘hunt group within their force area’, it did provide comprehensive details of the locations and conditions covered by the warning.


Yet their wider record on handling hunt-related offences leaves a lot to be desired, particularly in relation to the

Eggesford Hunt where previous investigations and prosecutions

 have raised serious questions. Answers are still needed.


A look at other police forces issuing CPWs and CPNs reveals a myriad of problems.


Albrighton & Woodland Hunt – Still Waiting After All These Years


In March 2024, Staffordshire Police issued the Albrighton and Woodland Hunt with a Community Protection Warning following repeated incidents involving uncontrolled hounds, trespass and the killing of wildlife.


Less than a year later, on 15 February 2025, hounds were photographed loose on the A458 near the Enville Estate, bringing traffic to a standstill.


Ambulances held up by hound carnage on the A458. Image: Locals Opposed to the Albrighton and Woodland Hunt.


The A458 incident is not the only incident involving the hunt while its CPW remained in place. In June 2026, Albrighton and Woodland Huntsman

Paul Larby and whipper-in Phillipa Ward

 were sentenced following their convictions for assaulting a female member of Shropshire Wildlife Monitors in 2024.


This was not even the first CPW for this hunt. Staffordshire Police had already issued one in February 2019. Five years later, following further incidents involving uncontrolled hounds, trespass, property damage and the killing of a fox and muntjac deer, the police’s response was…to issue another warning!


The current warning is in effect until March 2027.


Despite further documented incidents, including two assault convictions involving hunt staff, and a previous CPW, the hunt still remains subject to a warning rather than an enforceable Community Protection Notice.


Shropshire Hunts – Warnings Keep Coming


The Albrighton and Woodland is far from the only hunt in the region to have attracted police attention. The …

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: admin
title: Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps
content:
Am 2. November ist Friederike Schmitz zu Gast in Leipzig. Ihr Vortrag beschäftigt sich mit der Frage von Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps.

Plaque, Industriestraße 101, Leipzig

Orga: tierbefreier*innen Leipzig

Die Erderhitzung schreitet voran und wir müssen damit rechnen, dass Wetterextreme und Katastrophen unsere Gesellschaften massiv unter Druck setzen werden. Es ist daher realistisch, von Kollapsszenarien auszugehen – das bedeutet nicht zwingend ein einmaliges Ereignis, das plötzlich alles verändert. Es kann auch bedeuten, dass etablierte Systeme und Sicherheiten zunehmend instabil und unverlässlich werden.>

Die Kollapsbewegung fordert, dass wir uns gemeinsam darauf vorbereiten und solidarische Strukturen aufbauen, denn wer gegen Umweltzerstörung und Faschismus kämpft, kann sich auf den Staat nicht verlassen. Doch inwieweit sind nichtmenschliche Tiere dabei eingeschlossen? Und wie könnte es aussehen, wenn die Solidarität nicht an der Speziesgrenze haltmacht? Der Vortrag liefert einen Einstieg in diese Fragen und lädt zu Austausch und Diskussion ein.

Friederike Schmitz ist eine deutsche Philosophin und Publizistin mit dem Schwerpunkt Ethik und Politik der Mensch-Tier-Beziehung. Zu ihrem Schwerpunkt gehört die Klimagerechte Transformation von Landwirtschaft und Ernährung. In dem Podcast “Was zu retten ist?” thematisiert sie zusammen mit Annemarie Botzki (Campaignerin und Aktivistin) Klima, Kollaps und Ernährung.

author: L214
title: Végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires : l’état des lieux de L214
content:
Au lendemain de la rentrée scolaire 2026, L214 dresse l’état des lieux de la végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires dans 40 villes de France. Ce bilan, le premier depuis la prise de fonction des nouveaux élus à l’issue des élections municipales de mars 2026, révèle des situations contrastées : là où certaines villes se contentent du minimum imposé par la loi, d’autres font preuve de plus d’ambition, indépendamment de leur couleur politique.

La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires constitue un levier puissant et efficace à disposition des maires pour contribuer à réduire le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France. C’est pourquoi L214 propose trois mesures de végétalisation dans sa charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle à destination des maires : instaurer une option végétarienne quotidienne, deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires et un plat végétalien hebdomadaire.

Ce début d’année scolaire révèle de fortes disparités d’une ville à l’autre sur la mise en place de deux journées végétariennes par semaine. Sur les 40 villes de plus de 100 000 habitants étudiées par L214 :

14 villes proposent deux journées végétariennes par semaine ou plus,

12 villes proposent 5 à 7 journées végétariennes par mois,

14 villes se contentent d’une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum légal imposé par la loi EGalim.

Concernant la mise en place d’une option végétarienne quotidienne, le tableau est là aussi très contrasté : 11 villes proposent déjà cette option, alors que 24 villes proposent une option « sans viande » ou « sans porc » pouvant contenir du poisson, une alternative qui n’est donc pas végétarienne. Cinq villes ne proposent aucune alternative végétarienne quotidienne.

Certaines villes comme Bordeaux, Grenoble, Lyon, Montpellier et Paris font figure de bonnes élèves en cumulant d’ores et déjà une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires. D’autres villes vont même au-delà des mesures portées par L214, à l’image de Saint-Denis, qui propose 3 journées végétariennes chaque semaine dans ses cantines, ou de Montpellier, qui propose deux plats végétaliens chaque mois.

À l’inverse, Boulogne-Billancourt, Limoges et Le Mans notamment se limitent à une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum prévu par la loi.

→ Découvrir la charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle

Cet état des lieux montre que la volonté de végétaliser les menus dans les cantines scolaires n’est pas portée par un seul parti politique. Parmi les cinq villes qui cumulent une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires, Bordeaux est dirigée par une majorité du centre, Grenoble et Lyon par des majorités écologistes, et Montpellier et Paris par des majorités de gauche.

Plusieurs villes affiliées à droite renforcent elles aussi la végétalisation de leurs cantines. Aix-en-Provence propose désormais deux journées végétariennes une semaine sur deux, et Metz en propose 5 à 7 par mois.

Pour Erwin Goeller, chargé d’affaires publiques de L214 : « La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires est un choix politique concret à la portée de chaque maire. L’enjeu a été pris au sérieux par plusieurs municipalités, mais les efforts restent très disparates selon les villes. Nous appelons les nouveaux élus à se saisir pleinement de ce sujet pour contribuer, à leur échelle, à réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France ! »

title: NINE MICE LIBERATED FROM A LABORATORY.
content:
19th September, New Orleans USA.


[editor’s note: whilst we have received text relating to the action, and it references extensive footage of the inside of the laboratory, we have not seen any of the footage and cannot confirm the validity of the report. No news press articles have been found at the time of writing. Image is unrelated, historical rabbit liberation image.]


received anonymously via email:


“The Animal Liberation Front claims responsibility for the liberation of nine mice from the University of New Orleans earlier this month.


On September 19, 2026, nine female mice (including four so-called “breeding females”) were loaded up and spirited away from a miserable, windowless cinderblock room on the 2nd floor of UNO’s Psychology Building to begin a new life in safety and comfort. All nine are being lovingly looked after and tended to. None were released into the wild.


The lab chosen was that of Christopher Harshaw, who subjects mice and rats to experiments that purportedly aim to study autism, body temperature regulation and social behavior. This includes injecting them with drugs (including acetaminophen to induce neurodevelopment disorders), shutting them into small lighted cabinets overnight, and putting poisonous chemicals into their water like aniline (known to cause blood disorders and spleen tumors in rodents).


Moreover, Christopher Harshaw and his research assistant Anna are personally responsible for the killing of hundreds of animals per year, sometimes as many as 30-50 in a single day, as noted in Harshaw’s “Euthanasia Log” notebook, which on a previous visit was removed, had its pages photocopied (along with other documents related to animal research) and then put back. His death tally: 323 in 2023 (rats and mice), 575 in 2024 (rats and mice, including one wild mouse caught in a live trap and killed on the premises), and 363 in 2025 (all mice). His method: gassing them to death with co2.


Extensive video was also taken documenting the decrepit conditions of the lab as well as Roberto Refinetti’s animal room full of cages formerly housing squirrels (empty at the time of filming).


As should be clear: the purpose of this action wasn’t to vandalize, nor was it mere opportunism. This was a carefully planned and orchestrated live liberation of mice from Chris Harshaw’s lab. Its only purpose was getting the animals to safety as quickly as possible, therefore no equipment was damaged and no messages left at the scene. The whole operation, from entering the building to exiting with the animals, took ten minutes.


It should also be noted: This action was carried out using a minimum number of tools (none) and a minimum number of personnel (one).


This proves not only that lab raids can still be completed in 2026 but that one person, working alone, can successfully accomplish them.


To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on site it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.


And a word to all you would-be liberators out there: These facilities are not the fortresses you think they are. They are not impregnable. In fact the animal abusers in white coats have become so secure in their belief that no one is watching that they sometimes don’t even bother locking their doors! Use this negligence to your advantage. And while they sleep, go and do your work.


THE LAB RAID IS BACK.


Nine go free…


Another victory for the animals,


ALF”

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

The group has used a variety of civil disobedience and nonviolent direct action tactics, notably blockading McDonald's distribution centres in May 2021, blockading dairy industry sites in September 2022, disrupting the 2023 Grand National, rescuing lambs belonging to King Charles III in May 2023, and carrying out the UK’s largest undercover farm investigation in 2024.

title: Tote Rehe für Wortwitz verhöhnt: „Speziesismus des Monats“ an smile Versicherungen
content:
Speziesismus ist in unserer heutigen Gesellschaft noch weit verbreitet, aber ethisch nicht gerechtfertigt: Bei diesem Denkmuster unterscheiden wir Menschen andere 

fühlende Tiere

 nach ihrem vermeintlichen Wert und Nutzen für uns – wir stellen uns über andere Spezies: Wir diskriminieren sie, beuten sie milliardenfach aus, lassen sie leiden und töten sie. Wir von PETA Deutschland vergeben regelmäßig den „Speziesismus des Monats“ als Negativpreis für Unternehmen, Prominente und Behörden, die mit speziesistischen und tierfeindlichen Aussagen und Aktionen auffallen.


Eine Werbekampagne der Versicherungsfirma

smile

 mit Sitz in Österreich und der Schweiz nimmt Wildunfälle zum Anlass, einen Wortwitz auf Kosten von Rehen als Slogan zu verwenden: „Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“ Aus unserer Sicht werden Rehe damit zu bloßen Hindernissen degradiert und ihr Tod für eine Werbebotschaft bagatellisiert. Für diese speziesistische Darstellung verleihen wir smile Versicherungen den Negativpreis „Speziesismus des Monats“ im Oktober 2026. Denn Speziesismus ist die Diskriminierung von Lebewesen aufgrund ihrer Artzugehörigkeit.


„Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“: Negativpreis für smile Versicherungen

 


Wildunfälle

 können für Tiere und auch für Menschen tödlich enden oder schwere Verletzungen verursachen. Die Werbekampagne von smile macht aus diesem Leid einen Wortwitz: „Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“ Aus unserer Sicht wird der Tod von Rehen damit verharmlost und für Werbezwecke instrumentalisiert. Die Tiere werden in diesem Zusammenhang zweitrangig als Objekte hinter dem finanziellen Schaden dargestellt – und ihr Tod als nicht so schlimm, weil der finanzielle Schaden ausgeglichen wird. Dass es sich um fühlende Lebewesen handelt, die durch einen Unfall ein schweres Schicksal erleiden, wird ausgeblendet.  


Für diese Darstellung verleihen wir smile Versicherungen den Negativpreis „Speziesismus des Monats“. 


„Die Kampagne von smile verharmlost das Leid der unzähligen Rehe, die jedes Jahr im Straßenverkehr auf grausame Art ums Leben kommen. Ihren Tod als vermeintliche Pointe eines Witzes zu benutzen, ist geschmacklos und hinterlässt den Eindruck, dass sie von den Verantwortlichen als reine Objekte angesehen werden. Es ist bedauerlich, dass die Texter:innen der Werbekampagne keinen Slogan gefunden haben, der sich für Mensch und Tier einsetzt.“

Peter Höffken, Fachreferent bei PETA Deutschland 


In einer von PETA angefragten Stellungnahme erklärt das Unternehmen, dass sie mit dem Slogan „halb so Wild“ ausschließlich den finanziellen Schaden am Fahrzeug darstellen wollten, der durch eine Versicherung reguliert werden kann. Ausdrücklich nicht gemeint sei das Tier selbst oder das Unfallgeschehen. Man empfinde Wildunfälle ebenso als schreckliche Ereignisse. Die Werbekampagne sei nun beendet.    


Millionen Wildtiere sterben jährlich im Straßenverkehr

 


Unter den größeren Tierarten fallen in Deutschland

Rehe

 besonders

häufig Wildunfällen zum Opfer. Im Jagdjahr 2023/24 waren es über 204.000 Tiere. Hinzu kamen unter anderem mehr als 15.000 Wildschweine. [1, 2] 


Doch die erfassten größeren Wildtiere sind nur ein Teil der Opfer des Straßenverkehrs. Jedes Jahr sterben auch unzählige kleinere Wildtiere wie Igel, Marder, Kaninchen, Vögel oder Kröten auf deutschen Straßen. Allein bei

Igeln

 wird die Zahl der jährlich überfahrenen Tiere auf 500.000 bis eine Million geschätzt. [3] 


In der Schweiz sterben jedes Jahr Hundertausende Wildtiere im Straßenverkehr.

Unter den größeren Tierarten fallen auch dort Rehe am häufigsten Wildunfällen zum Opfer. Im Jahr 2025 waren es 7651 Tiere. [3] Auf Schweizer Straßen sterben jedes Jahr schätzungsweise Hunderttausende weitere Wildtiere bei Wildunfällen, beispielsweise über 6000 Füchse im vergangenen Jahr. Besonders häufig sind Kleintiere wie Igel, Marder, Kaninchen, Vögel oder Kröten betroffen, von denen viele statistisch nicht erfasst werden. 


Wildtiere brauchen sichere und unberührte Lebensräume

 


Inmitten von Kulturlandschaften, Straßen und dicht bebauten Siedlungsbereichen wird der

Lebensraum für Wildtiere

 immer knapper. Dort, wo einst Rast- und Nahrungsgebiete waren, gibt es heute vielerorts kaum noch Platz. Insbesondere die auf Profitmaximierung ausgerichtete industrielle Land- und Forstwirtschaft trägt zum Verlust von Lebensräumen bei. 


Tierarten, die versuchen, in Koexistenz mit Menschen zu leben, werden vertrieben,

gejagt

 oder zu sogenannten „Schädlingen“ degradiert.  …

title: ÖHD documents environmental destruction on Mount Gabar
content:
The Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) has investigated the ongoing ecological destruction in the Gabar Mountains in the Kurdish province of Şırnak. A delegation from the Ecology Commission of the ÖHD’s provincial executive board and its local branch documented the impact of large-scale deforestation and intensive oil extraction on the ground. The findings of the investigation are expected to be published in a report in the coming days.


ÖHD lawyer Hülya Yıldırım regards the activities on Mount Gabar not as an isolated case of environmental destruction, but as part of the war and security policies pursued in Kurdistan for decades. She noted that forests are also being cleared in the neighboring mountainous regions of Besta and Cudi, while fires are destroying large areas of land and natural habitats are being damaged by mining operations and environmentally harmful industrial facilities.


“There are now oil wells and extraction facilities in virtually every corner of Mount Gabar. As a result, the mountain is literally being blasted apart. The Tigris River is being polluted by oil leaks and petroleum waste,” said Yıldırım, a member of the ÖHD Ecology Commission.


Oil extraction hinders return to destroyed villages


According to the delegation’s observations, the impact of oil extraction extends beyond the immediate destruction of the natural environment. The health of local residents and workers, as well as livelihoods dependent on agriculture and livestock farming, are also at risk.


The consequences are particularly severe for people who have been waiting for decades to return to their home villages. Numerous settlements in the region were burned down and forcibly depopulated during the dirty war against the PKK in the 1990s. According to the ÖHD, current oil extraction and development activities are creating additional obstacles to the resettlement of these villages.


Yıldırım also criticized the fact that the approval procedures for activities affecting the natural environment do not even comply with the requirements of existing legislation. She argued that these practices reflect a policy that views forests, mountains, soil, and waterways solely as resources to be exploited for economic gain.


“These areas, these mountains, this land, and this river are all regarded merely as resources. We will continue to oppose this mentality and the approval procedures that do not even comply with existing laws,” the lawyer stated.


‘This destruction is a policy of special warfare’


ÖHD lawyer Ayşe Şehriban Demirel, who participated in the field inspection, also placed the environmental destruction within the region’s political context. She argued that the activities on Mount Gabar should not be viewed solely from an economic perspective, but as an expression of a deliberate policy targeting the Kurdish population and their living environment.


“What is happening here is a policy of special warfare. This destruction causes us profound pain. We are working to put an end to this exploitation and ensure that those responsible are held accountable,” Demirel said.


The ÖHD plans to make the findings gathered during its investigation public in the coming days and expand its legal and public advocacy efforts against environmental destruction. The organization also intends to link resistance to the activities on Mount Gabar with efforts to protect the neighboring mountainous regions of Cudi and Besta.


“We will expose the ecological destruction on Mount Gabar and raise our voices against this exploitation and destruction of nature, particularly in Cudi and Besta as well,” Demirel announced.

author: Mohamed Sheikh Nor
title: Somali Man Speaks Out on Mogadishu Streets About El Niño Threats.
content:
Osman Yusuf Oskar‚ wearing a T-shirt with the letters “SUPER EL NINO‚” walks the streets of Mogadishu carrying a megaphone and signs to alert other Somalis of the risks of heavy rains during the upcoming rainy season․


His voice can be heard above the sounds of traffic and crowds, urging others to heed warnings that El Niño-related floods will threaten millions of people in Somalia, primarily children, according to

Save the Children warns of El Niño floods in Somalia

).


Osman Yusuf Oskar warning a citizen in Mogadishu


Oskar is not a government employee or a meteorologist․ His campaign effort is a solo project to educate others about El Niño‚ a weather phenomenon with which most Somalis are unfamiliar․


“I am not an official or officer at the disaster management center․ I am stepping into their role of volunteering to spread the word to my people‚ who don’t know much about the Super El Niño‚” Oskar said․


Street by street‚ Oskar shares his warning in public settings․ Some people respond to his efforts; others ignore him and go about their business․ Oskar’s signs and megaphone are tools to help laypeople understand technical weather information․


His campaign follows Somalia’s recovery from one of the worst droughts in recent decades․


“While other governments of nearby countries were preparing for this disaster‚ we seem to have had no warning and no preparation for this‚” Oskar said․


“The time for warning has gone‚ and other countries bordering that nation now are preparing․” He said․


“Here in Somalia‚ our politicians and other government officials are more focused on their own activities and are not communicating to the general public about climate-related issues‚ including the Super El Niño weather event‚” he said․


The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)  has warned that strengthening El Niño conditions and forecasts of exceptionally heavy Deyr rains could raise the risk of severe flooding across Somalia, with up to a 90 percent probability of above-normal rainfall in parts of central and southern Somalia

FAO warning that El Niño raises the risk of severe Deyr flooding in Somalia


For the past four years‚ drought has caused massive hardship in much of the country‚ including loss of livestock and crops and migration of rural residents to urban areas and internally displaced persons’ settlements․


In addition to years of drought‚ people in these areas are now at risk of flooding and other impacts from heavy rains related to El Niño conditions․


The October-December Deyr rains are forecast to be above average in Somalia‚ increasing flood risks near major rivers and other locations across the country․


In vulnerable communities affected by drought‚ flooding may lead to additional population displacement and destruction of homes and crops‚ as well as greater health risks and service disruptions․


From drought to other climate-related risks.


The threat of flooding follows several years of drought that have disrupted the ability of many Somali families to earn a living․


Farmers and herders have lost livestock and crops due to lack of water and grazing land․ Many households have relocated to find food‚ water‚ health services‚ and other humanitarian aid․


Extended drought has reduced communities’ resilience to other shocks․


That vulnerability was evident during my recent reporting trip to Kismayo‚ which included a fact-finding trip to Jubaland with a UNICEF delegation and the Swedish ambassador to Somalia․


The delegation visited internally displaced persons’ settlements and a stabilization center treating severely malnourished children․


Children treated at the center suffered from long-term health problems caused by food insecurity and lack of other health services․


This scenario describes a larger

humanitarian crisis in Somalia, compounded by drought and aid funding cuts

, which are placing additional pressure on vulnerable households already struggling with lost income and other hardships.


Sandra Lattouf‚ UNICEF Somalia Representative‚ told African Arguments that a long dry spell and decreased aid had left many families in Somalia without their crops and other means of support․


“Now kids have begun to die because of malnutrition and diseases‚ and we need and urge donors to save lives․”


Sandra Lattouf

 said some children had died of malnutrition and other complications from diseases․


The warning is issued amid budget challenges for other humanitarian groups․
