author: Chris Walker
title: Abdul El-Sayed Schools Heckler Who Questioned His Loyalty to the US
content:
The heckler asked El-Sayed if he disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, which the candidate has done in past remarks.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Michigan Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate Abdul El-Sayed responded to a heckler at a recent campaign event who appeared to question his loyalty to the country based solely on his religious beliefs.

El-Sayed, who is Muslim, spoke on Saturday at a campaign event in Caro, Michigan, a Republican-leaning area of the state. A heckler who identified himself as “Tommy” shouted toward the candidate, interrupting the forum by asking El-Sayed if he would “disavow the Muslim Brotherhood.”

El-Sayed has already repeatedly disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, and has fended off myriad attacks against him that have emanated from anti-Muslim voices. He responded to the outburst by questioning why Tommy would ask the question in the first place.

“Sure, yeah, absolutely,” El-Sayed said, according to a video that has now been shared by his campaign. “But I want to ask the question — why are you asking the question? … What are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?”

“Yes,” Tommy responded, rationalizing his action by saying he had not heard El-Sayed distance himself from the group before.

El-Sayed turned the question around on Tommy. “Have you disavowed them? I haven’t heard you disavow them yet,” the candidate pointed out.

“You’re asking the question because, implicitly, you assume that I’ll have dual loyalties, right? You assume that somehow I wouldn’t disavow, or that I’ll have some higher order of allegiance other than the Constitution,” El-Sayed continued. “Tommy, is that what you imply?”

The heckler responded, “Yes,” to which El-Sayed added: “Why would you think that about me?”

This is Tommy. Tommy had a question about my allegiances. Listen to the end to hear about his.

Tommy continued to claim it was because he hadn’t heard El-Sayed expressly disavow the organization. When El-Sayed said that he just did, and continued to press Tommy to actually answer the question, the heckler wouldn’t do so.

“Have you asked everybody in your life if they disavow them?” he said to Tommy, who responded that he hadn’t. El-Sayed asked once more why the question was really asked. Tommy again said it was because he hadn’t personally heard El-Sayed say he disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood.

“Everybody knows the answer, Tommy, answer the question,” El-Sayed pressed.

After it became clear that Tommy wouldn’t recognize his bias against Muslims as the basis of the question, El-Sayed redirected the conversation once again, pointing out that he would have to affirm an oath to the Constitution if he is sworn into office.

“I’m going to swear to the Constitution of the United States and that Constitution guarantees us all the right to practice whatever faith we want to or no faith at all,” El-Sayed said.

The Senate candidate also cited the example of President John F. Kennedy, who was attacked for his Catholic faith in the election of 1960. Kennedy famously said he was “not running to be a Catholic president but was running to be president and happened to be Catholic,” El-Sayed reminded Tommy. “I’m not running to be a Muslim senator. I’m running for the U.S. Senate and happen to be Muslim.”

I’m never going to tell you what faith you can or cannot practice. I want to protect your right to practice your faith as you choose as a Christian man. The only question though is that it seems like you don’t want to protect my right to practice as I choose.

He then asked Tommy whether he would disavow any violations of the separation between church and state. Tommy said he wouldn’t.

“I think it’s you who needs to understand the Constitution, not me,” El-Sayed countered.

Independent journalist Marisa Kabas has identified “Tommy” as Thomas Teepell, a former aide to Missouri GOP Sen. Josh Hawley, reporting that his presence at the event may be part of a larger operation of young Republicans in Michigan working to disrupt events in support of El-Sayed.

The polite but assertive back-and-forth between the candidate and heckler went viral on social media over the weekend, with many analysts praising El-Sayed for his nuanced arguments defending religious freedom and rejecting baseless attacks on his own faith that wrongly insinuate he isn’t qualified to run or has dual loyalties.

Despite El-Sayed’s citations of Kennedy’s arguments …

author: Lin Taylor
title: Israeli Firm Used Online Ads to Infect Millions With ‘Zero-Click’ Spyware
content:
Israeli adtech firm Discover-Tech used online ads to operate a global spy network targeting millions of people, including Al Jazeera journalists, a new report has revealed. 


Presenting as a legitimate company, Discover-Tech purchased malicious online ads to infect devices with spyware from

Candiru, an Israeli firm blacklisted by the US government. 


Discover-Tech ran a platform called Controlium to “automatically infect devices the moment an advertisement is rendered – a form of zero-click attack,”

 according to a

report by Citizen Lab

, a research group at the University of Toronto, and

cybersecurity firm Confiant

. 


The ads were displayed in over 70,000 mobile apps and more than 120,000 websites between March and June 2026, impacting millions of users globally, the report found.


“This is the first-ever public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads,” it said.


“Discover-Tech’s ads also covertly directed millions of devices to contact Candiru’s servers, likely for large-scale tracking and reconnaissance.” 


Broadcaster Al Jazeera said it reached out to Citizen Lab when it was targeted in 2024 and 2025.


“Al Jazeera worked voluntarily with Citizen Lab’s researchers, and… that cooperation helped verify and publicly document these attacks,” the network

said in a statement

. 


“The targeting of journalists is an attack on press freedom and on the public’s right to know. Those responsible must be held accountable.”


Israel raided the offices of the Qatari news network in the occupied West Bank city of Ramallah in 2024, ordering it to shut down its operations. At least 12 of the network’s journalists and media workers have been killed in Gaza since the start of Israel’s genocide in October 2023. In June this year, Al Jazeera condemned Israel’s “deliberate killing” of its cameraman, Ahmed Wishah.  


The report said Discover-Tech ads reached national security agencies, various ministries of defence, Nato and several international media networks, but did not find evidence linking the attacks to the Israeli government.


Novara Media approached Discover-Tech for comment.


The

Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has urged

 governments and authorities to investigate the attacks, particularly those targeting journalists. 


“The mass surveillance architecture supporting online advertising is being harnessed for other purposes and puts journalists at risk,” said Jonathan Rozen, CPJ’s deputy director of research. 


“Citizen Lab’s findings that Al Jazeera devices were infected with spyware delivered via targeted ads make these surveillance dangers even clearer.”


Since 2023, Israel has killed

 more than 240 journalists and media workers

, more than any other government, the press freedom group has said.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Plan Cóndor II: Trump prepara otra cumbre para coordinar la persecución de la izquierda
content:
Milei estuvo en diálogo con Marco Rubio, quien está organizando la conferencia junto con el gobierno alemán. El Presidente volvió a hablar esta semana de una “alianza” entre la izquierda radical y el terrorismo islámico.


Por Luciana Bertoia


El Departamento de Estado prepara una nueva cumbre para discutir cómo perseguir a los movimientos de izquierda a los que califican como “terroristas”. El encuentro se prevé para el mes próximo en Alemania, confirmaron voceros de la cartera que conduce Marco Rubio, ante una consulta formulada por Página/12. En su

 primera edición en Washington

, Javier Milei había enviado a dos funcionarios de alto rango: su canciller, Pablo Quirno, y el número dos de la Secretaría de Inteligencia de Estado (SIDE), José Lago Rodríguez.


El 16 de julio pasado, Marco Rubio encabezó la conferencia sobre el resurgimiento del terrorismo político en la que participaron enviados de más de 60 países.

El Departamento de Estado describió el encuentro como la conformación de una “coalición” contra la izquierda.

En la apertura del evento, el titular del Departamento de Estado comparó su cruzada con la coordinación que funcionó en los años 70 y puso como ejemplo de organizaciones a Montoneros y Tupamaros. La base del éxito de esta nueva empresa, sostuvo Rubio, sería una vieja receta: el trabajo mancomunado de las fuerzas de seguridad y el intercambio de inteligencia. O sea, lo que ya existió en el Plan Cóndor.


Argentina, a través de los emisarios de Milei, tuvo un rol importante en el encuentro de julio. Según trascendió, Quirno fue uno de los oradores. Sin embargo,

el canciller no dio a publicidad su discurso, a pesar del pedido expreso que hizo el diputado nacional Agustín Rossi, bajo el argumento de que estaba amparado por el secreto.

 Rossi encontró que no todos los países siguen esta lógica. La

canciller de Georgia, Maka Botchorishvili, publicó su intervención en la que le agradece a Marco Rubio por poner el asunto del terrorismo en la cima de la agenda.


La SIDE le respondió al Frente de Izquierda y sus Trabajadores (FIT), que tiene como referente a Myriam Bregman, que toda la información relativa a la cumbre estaba alcanzada por la clasificación de seguridad y que si se difundía esa información podría comprometerse el Sistema de Inteligencia Nacional (SIN). Según Cristian Auguadra, la única información pública era la que distribuía el propio Departamento de Estado.


La semana pasada, se conoció que el gobierno alemán había respondido a un pedido de informes que hizo Die Linke (La Izquierda) sobre la coordinación antiterrorista con Estados Unidos. Allí, las autoridades decían que estaban trabajando en un encuentro que se haría en otoño –o sea, antes del 21 de diciembre– en Alemania.


Página/12 remitió una consulta al Departamento de Estado. Voceros de ese organismo explicaron que la cumbre se hará en noviembre y que será coorganizada por Estados Unidos y Alemania. No precisaron cuál será la fecha, aunque es probable que sea después del 3 de noviembre, cuando en Estados Unidos se celebrarán las elecciones de medio término que serán una prueba de fuego para Donald Trump.


Milei pasó los últimos días en Estados Unidos. El jueves, mientras las fuerzas de seguridad reprimían la marcha en la que se pedía que el Gobierno cumpla con la Ley de Financiamiento de la Educación Universitaria (LFEU), Milei encabezó un acto en la embajada argentina en Washington en el que habló de una “alianza entre la izquierda radical y el terrorismo islamita”.


Al día siguiente, en los tribunales de Comodoro Py, aparecieron unas quince denuncias del Departamento de Investigaciones Antiterroristas de la Policía Federal Argentina (PFA). En un juzgado explicaron que se trataba de presentaciones que suelen hacerse en base a relevamientos que hace el Buró Federal de Investigaciones (FBI) en redes sociales. Según las fuentes judiciales, no estarían vinculadas a actividades de ciberpatrullaje por la marcha.


El FBI tiene un vínculo estrecho con el Gobierno. La versión oficial es que el Centro Nacional Antiterrorismo (CNA) se creó en coordinación con esa agencia estadounidense y es el primero de su tipo en la región. El 7 de octubre, el FBI compartió en sus redes sociales que había una delegación argentina para llevar adelante un intercambio estratégico sobre contraterrorismo. Una publicación anterior del FBI en Miami especificaba que la comitiva estaba integrada por diez funcionarios del Ministerio de Seguridad, la …

author: Hudson Hongo
title: EFF Launches Privacy Badger for Safari on macOS
content:
Free Tracker Blocker Used by Millions Will Protect Even More Users' Privacy

SAN FRANCISCO—Privacy Badger, the

award-winning

 tracker blocker made by the member-supported digital rights nonprofit

Electronic Frontier Foundation

 (EFF), is now available for Safari on macOS.  


Safari users can

download the free browser extension

 today and join the more than 4 million people using Privacy Badger to take a stand against data brokers and online surveillance. Users will need Safari version 26.5 or higher to use it.


Ranked as one of the best ad tracker blockers by

The Wirecutter

,

Consumer Reports

,

PC Mag

 and more, Privacy Badger is different from other blocking extensions. Created by EFF to stop companies from spying on you online, Privacy Badger

automatically learns

 to block hidden trackers on the web, along with additional privacy-protecting features. 


"Most websites contain invisible tracking code that lets companies collect, share, and profit from your personal data," said Lena Cohen, Staff Technologist at EFF. "Creepy ads are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the harms of online tracking: Once your information

enters the data broker ecosystem

, it’s nearly impossible to know who buys it or what they’re doing with it. Safari support has long been one of Privacy Badger’s most requested features and EFF is excited to be able to make this important tool available to Safari users to fight back for a better web." 


On Safari, Privacy Badger goes beyond the browser’s

built-in privacy features

 to provide additional protection against online tracking. In its default browsing mode, Safari limits the information that trackers can access, but it still allows them to load. Privacy Badger blocks online trackers from loading in the first place, preventing them from tracking you using

techniques

 that bypass Safari’s protections. 


With today's launch, Privacy Badger

is now available

 on all major desktop browsers. 


As the leading nonprofit defending online civil liberties, EFF is committed to fighting mass surveillance in the courts, through activism, and by making free, privacy-protecting tools like Privacy Badger. Now, even more people can join the movement against online tracking, by installing Privacy Badger themselves, telling their friends and family who use Safari about it, or

by supporting Privacy Badger today

. 


For more on Privacy Badger for Safari on macOS:


https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2026/10/announcing-privacy-badger-safari-macos


For more on the dangers of online tracking:


https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2025/03/online-tracking-out-control-privacy-badger-can-help-you-fight-back

 


For more on how Privacy Badger works:


https://privacybadger.org/

press@eff.org

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Man charged with murder following Oct. 6 altercation that left another man dead
content:
RCMP have charged a man with second-degree murder in connection with an altercation that happened Oct. 6 in Iqaluit.


Qaqasie Aningmiuq, 21, was arrested on Oct. 16, Nunavut RCMP said Monday in a news release issued by Sgt. George Henrie.


Police previously

identified

 the man who died as 38-year-old Robert Kipanik.


He was among two people transported to Qikiqtani General Hospital with life-threatening injuries on Oct. 6, after police responded to calls about an altercation at around 9:55 p.m. in the 300 block of the city.


The other person survived after being medevaced to Ottawa. Police have not identified them.


The RCMP’s Major Crime Unit is handling the investigation.


Aningmiuq remains in custody until his next court appearance, which is scheduled for Nov. 17.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: This Politician Posted a Quote About Palestinian Resistance. Now France Is Dragging Her Through the Courts
content:
For the last three years, Rima Hassan has watched in horror as thousands of people have been killed in her family’s homeland. The French jurist and La France Insoumise (LFI) MEP, who was born stateless in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria, is one of France’s most outspoken critics of both Israel’s genocide in Gaza and the complicity of Europe’s governments.


Now, she could be sent to prison over a post on social media.


In March, Hassan posted a quotation on X/Twitter attributed to Kōzō Okamoto, a member of the Japanese Red Army who took part in a 1972 attack on an Israeli airport in which 26 people were killed.


“I gave my youth to the Palestinian cause,” Okamoto’s quotation read. “As long as there is oppression, resistance will not only be a right, but a duty.”


Far-right National Rally politician

Matthias Renault

, interior minister

Laurent Nuñez

 and two French pro-Israel lobby groups reported Hassan to prosecutors for

apologie du terrorisme

(the glorification of terrorism) – a criminal offence.

Hassan denied the charges

 and said her main goal had been to share a quotation about the “philosophy of resistance”, and that she couldn’t be accused of glorifying terrorism for doing so.


Hassan’s trial began on 19 October. If found guilty, she could be sentenced to up to seven years in prison and fined €100,000 under French law. Her situation, she said, is the latest in a series

 of legal and political battles in France over solidarity with Palestine

.


“

People who stand in solidarity with Palestine are labelled as terrorists because it [this label] is the only instrument that allows them to silence concrete opposition and activism,” Hassan told Novara Media ahead of her trial.


This isn’t the first time the French state has brought the full force of its institutional machinery against Hassan.

22 legal proceedings

 have been initiated against her in the last two years in connection with her political views (six have been closed by prosecutors without questioning, 13 after questioning and three remain open). In September, a separate trial in relation to

two social media posts from 2025

 was adjourned.


Prior to the opening of the investigation

 into the post in March, police had

reportedly already been surveilling Hassan

, tracking her movements and monitoring her phone activity. In April, she was taken into custody for questioning in what she describes as a “deliberate attempt” to circumvent her parliamentary immunity. Details of her arrest, including the claim she was carrying drugs, were then

leaked to the press

 (the drug probe was subsequently dropped).


Hassan’s lawyer, Vincent Brengarth, has

long maintained his client’s innocence

, alleging the prosecutions are part of a “campaign of judicial harassment aimed at silencing her”. Five UN special rapporteurs have

raised similar concerns

, warning the French government that Hassan appeared to be facing “political and judicial harassment”.


Hassan told Novara Media she believed that the accusations against her were a “misuse of anti-terrorism laws”.


“The shift is very interesting,” she said, noting how she believes that we’re moving towards a situation in which the accusation of terrorism is directed at “all political opposition”.


Hassan’s case is perhaps the most high-profile of hundreds of cases of alleged

apologie du terrorisme

 offences in France.

In October 2023, police arrested trade union leader Jean-Paul Delescaut over a leaflet published following the 7 October attacks (Delescaut was convicted and sentenced, before being

acquitted on appeal

). In another case, the suspended sentence of a former deputy mayor, Mohamed Makni, for sharing a quotation which described the attacks as “resistance” was upheld by France’s highest court (Makni is now

challenging the ruling

 at the European Court of Human Rights). B

etween October 2023 and October 2025,

more than 350 people

 were convicted of the offence in total. While it’s unclear how many were in relation to Palestine, rulings surged after 7 October.


None of this may surprise anyone living in the UK. Since it was banned as a terrorist group in July 2025, those in the UK expressing support for Palestine Action, an organisation which targeted companies

 involved in supplying military equipment to Israel,

risk up to 14 years in prison. What’s followed, due to huge public opposition to the ban, has been

a 1,553% uptick in terrorism arrests

 – 94% of them in the …

author: Chris Walker
title: More Than $137 Million Has Been Spent on AI-Generated Midterm Ads
content:
The vast majority of ads emanate from GOP campaigns, depicting their Democratic opponents in fictionalized scenarios.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Millions of dollars have been spent on AI during this year’s midterm election campaign, oftentimes through candidates using the technology to depict their opponents in fictional situations, portraying them in negative ways to unsuspecting voters.

According to research from Wesleyan University, over 200 ads have used AI in this election cycle. The ads have totaled more than $137 million in campaign spending.

More than 80 percent of the ads have been produced by Republican candidates or political action committees (PACs) aligned with the GOP. One such ad, featuring Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul (who is running for re-election in New York), features her walking alongside New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The governor reminds Mamdani, “don’t say affordable” while the two refer to how they plan to govern the state moving forward.

No such statement from Hochul exists, and the video of them walking next to each other in such a way is entirely fictional. The ad doesn’t contain any disclaimer informing viewers that it’s generated by AI.

“It’s the year of the AI election,” Fred N. Davis III, founder of Strategic Perception, an advertising firm based in Hollywood, said to The New York Times. “It’s top of mind for everybody in my business and pretty much everybody in the political business.”

Some candidates who have become the victims of AI advertising are pushing back. Rebecca Cooke, a Democrat seeking to unseat Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R) in a contentious election in Western Wisconsin, sent a “cease and desist” order to him for posting a series of online AI ads he made against her. One of those ads featured fictionalized versions of Cooke and former President Joe Biden, with the former stating that she plans to “take advantage of as much corruption as possible” if Democrats win the elections.

“These defamatory, misleading videos undermine our democratic process and are the exact kind of mudslinging voters are tired of,” the letter said to Van Orden.

Wisconsin law forbids the use of deepfake videos in political messaging, but there is a loophole for federal candidates. The letter takes note of that state statute, telling the Republican lawmaker that he is “violating the spirit of the law.”

Van Orden has continued to produce AI videos. And though he has used Cooke’s image less often, he has now resorted to using an animated duck to refer to her, whose voice sounds eerily similar to the Democratic candidate’s.

For his own part, President Donald Trump has rejected calls for the government to regulate AI, instead touting a non-binding “self-policing” accord that he and several AI companies have signed onto. He has also sought to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” and has made the extraordinary claim that any criticism of the technology is akin to an act of treason.

American voters, meanwhile, would like to see more regulation of AI.

According to a Johns Hopkins University poll published this summer, most Americans back a “right to human” law, which would allow them to opt out of AI interactions if they so desire, including 79 percent who support that concept in health care settings, 76 percent who back it in legal proceedings, and 73 percent who say such a law should apply when AI is aiding in government services.

A recent CNN poll also found that most Americans believe the U.S. government is not doing enough to regulate AI, with 71 percent of respondents expressing that view. Support for regulation is also bipartisan — 85 percent of Democratic-leaning respondents support regulation, while 63 percent of Republican-leaning respondents do as well, the survey found.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our …

title: ᐃᓄᑐᖃᓄᑦ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᖓ ᐊᖅᑯᑎᒧᐊᕈᓐᓇᖅᐳᖅ 2027−ᒥ, ᓯᕗᓕᖅᑎ ᐅᖃᖅᐳᖅ
content:
For the English version of this story, please see

Elder van project could hit the streets in 2027, premier says

.


ᑕᓪᓕᒪᓂ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᐅᔪᓂ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ ᓂᐅᕕᖅᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᑐᓂ $1 ᒥᓕᐊᓐᓂ ᐃᓄᓕᒫᓄᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖏᓐᓂ ᓱᓕ ᐅᖅᑯᑎᒦᙱᓚᑦ ᐊᕐᕌᒍ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᐊᖅᑯᑎᒦᓐᓇᑎᒃ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᒥ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᑕᐃᒪᐃᑦᑐᒥ ᐱᔨᖅᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


ᑐᓂᓯᔪᓐᓇᙱᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓂᖓᓂ ᖃᖓ ᐱᔭᕇᖅᓯᒪᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓄᑦ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑎᑕᐅᓪᓚᕆᖕᓂᖓᓂ, ᓯᕗᓕᖅᑎ ᔮᓐ ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ “ᐱᔪᒪᓂᕆᕙᖓ” ᑕᑯᓂᕐᒥ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᒃᑲᓐᓂᕐᓂᖏᓐᓂ 2027−ᒥ — ᐊᕐᕌᒍᑦ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᖄᖏᖅᓯᒪᔪᓂ ᓂᐅᕕᖅᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ.


“ᓄᑖᙳᕆᐊᖅᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓ, ᒫᓐᓇᐅᔪᒥ, ᓱᓕ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᙱᑦᑐᖅ,” ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᖃᓘᑎᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᐱᖅᓱᖅᑕᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐅᒃᑐᐱᕆ 9−ᒥ. “ᑭᓯᐊᓂ, ᒐᕙᒪᕗᑦ ᒪᓕᒍᒪᐅᑎᖃᙱᓚᑦ ᐆᒧᖓ.”


ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᖅ ᓄᖅᑲᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ 2025−ᒥ, ᐃᓱᐊᓂ ᓯᕗᓂᐊᓂ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᓂᖏᓐᓂ, ᐱᔾᔪᑎᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᑕᖃᙱᓗᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᓂᖓᓄᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᔪᒃᓴᐅᑕᐅᔪᓂ.


ᑕᒪᓐᓇ ᐊᓯᔾᔨᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᐱᕐᙶᖅ 2026−ᒥ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᐅᖅᑏᑦ ᒫᓐᓇᐅᔪᒥ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᐅᕐᕕᖕᒥ ᐊᖏᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋ $1.25 ᒥᓕᐊᓐᓂ ᖄᒃᑲᓐᓂᐊᒍᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ, ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐸᓯᒥ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᖅ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᒥ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ, ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᖃᕐᓂᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᓯᕗᓂᒃᓴᒧᑦ ᐊᔪᙱᓐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ, ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᒻᒪᒃᓴᓂᕐᒥ ᓕᒥᑎᒃᑯᓐᓂᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᑐᒃᑐ ᑖᒃᓯᓂᑦ.


ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᖃᖅᐳᑦ ᐊᑐᓂ ᑕᓪᓕᒪᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᐅᔪᓂ: ᐃᖃᓗᐃᑦ, ᐃᖃᓗᒃᑑᑦᑎᐊᖅ, ᑲᖏᖅᖠᓂᖅ, ᓴᓪᓕᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐸᖕᓂᖅᑑᒥ. ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᓯᕗᓂᒃᓴᒧᑦ ᐊᔪᙱᓐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ, ᓇᖕᒥᓂᕆᔭᐅᔪᒥ ᑲᒻᐸᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᓂᐅᕕᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑕᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᓄᓇᕗᒻᒥ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᓐᓂ.


ᖁᑉᐸ ᒪᐃᒃ ᓇᖏᖅᐳᖅ ᓴᓂᓕᐊᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ ᐸᓯᖓᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᒥ ᐸᐃᕆᓃᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖏᑦ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ’ ᖃᒻᒪᖓᓂ ᐅᒃᑐᐱᕆ 9−ᒥ. (ᑎᐊᕆᓐ ᓕᐊᑦᔅ ᐊᔾᔨᖁᑎᖓ)


ᑭᒡᒐᖅᑐᐃᔨᐅᔪᓂ ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᒻᒪᒃᓴᓂᕐᒥ ᓕᒥᑎᑯᓐᓂᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑐᒃᑐ ᑖᒃᓯᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᓐᓂ ᐊᑐᐃᓪᓐᓇᐅᓚᐅᙱᓚᑦ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᓕᐅᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐆᒧᖓ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐊᖑᔪᒧᑦ.


ᐊᑐᐊᒐᒥ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᕗᖅ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᑉ ᑐᓄᐊᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ, ᐱᔭᕇᖅᑕᐅᒍᓂ, ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᐸᕐᓇᒃᐳᑦ ᑐᓂᓯᓂᕐᒥ ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑐᒃᓯᕋᐅᑎᓂ ᓯᕗᓂᐊᓂ ᐃᓱᐊᓂ 2026−ᒥ, ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᓱᓕ ᐃᓱᒪᒃᓴᖅᓯᐅᕈᑕᐅᓂᐊᖅᐳᖅ ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᖅ ᐃᓄᓕᒫᓅᖓᓂᐊᕈᓂ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ “ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᑎᒍᑦ,” ᐃᓚᒋᐊᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᒻᒪᒃᓴᓂᕐᒥ ᓕᒥᑎᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᓇᖕᒥᓂᖅ-ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᕿᓚᒻᒥᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᕿᑦᑐᒥ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᓂᐅᓚᐅᖅᑐᒥ ᐅᒃᑐᐱᕆ 2025−ᒥ. ᑲᒻᐸᓂᐅᔪᖅ ᑭᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ 200−ᐸᓗᖕᓄᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐱᓇᓱᐊᕈᓯᐅᑉ ᓄᙳᐊᓂᑕᒫᒥ.


ᖁᑉᐸ ᒪᐃᒃ, ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᖃᑕᐅᔪᖅ ᐸᐃᕆᔩᑦ ᑎᒍᒥᐊᖅᑎᒃᑯᑦ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᓄᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖏᓐᓂ, ᐊᑐᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᒻᒥ ᐱᖓᓱᐃᖅᓱᖅᖢᓂ ᐃᖏᕐᕋᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᒻᒪᖓᓄᑦ, ᓂᕿᑖᕐᕕᖕᒥ ᐊᔪᖅᓴᖅᑐᓄᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᓂᕿᓄᑦ ᓂᐅᕕᕐᕕᓄᑦ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᓄᑖᖅ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᒧᑦ ᐊᔭᐅᕐᕕᖓ ᐊᒃᓱᕈᕐᓇᒐᓚᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᓂᐅᕐᓗᖁᑎᖓᓄᑦ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ, ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑎᐅᔪᒥ ᐸᓯᒥ ᐊᔪᕐᓇᙱᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᒪᔪᕋᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᑎᑭᐅᑎᔪᓐᓇᓕᕋᒥ ᐊᒡᒐᒧᑦ ᑎᒍᒥᐊᕐᕕᓄᑦ ᐃᓄᐊᓂ ᐸᓯᒥ ᐃᑭᓇᓱᐊᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


“ᐱᐅᕐᔪᐊᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑕᐅᓂᖃᖅᖢᓂ,” ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖑᔪᖅ ᐃᒻᒥᓂᒃ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᕗᑦ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ, ᐃᓚᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᓄᑦ ᐸᓯᖓᓂ. ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᐸᓯᐅᑉ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᔭᐅᕐᕕᖓ ᓱᕋᒃᓯᒪᖕᒪᑦ ᐊᑯᓂᐊᓗᒃ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᖃᑕᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᐃᓂᐊᖅ ᖁᐊᒐᖅ.


”ᐅᑕᖅᑭᙳᓚᐅᖅᐳᒍᑦ ᓄᑖᒥ ᐸᓯᒥ ᑕᐃᒫᒃ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᖅᐸᕗᑦ” ᒪᐃᒃ ᐃᓚᒋᐊᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


“ᐅᔾᔨᕈᓱᒃᐳᖓ ᐊᑯᓂᐸᓘᓂᖓᓂ ᐅᑯᐊ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᑦ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᕐᒥ ᓂᐅᕕᖅᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪᓂᕆᐅᖕᓂᖃᒐᓚᒃᐳᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᑲᖅᓴᙱᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᓱᓕᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᓱᓕ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᙱᓐᓂᖏᓐᓂ,” ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ. “ᒪᓕᒃᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑕᑯᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᑐᐊᒐᕐᒥ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ, ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓇᔭᖅᑐᒥ ᑕᐃᔅᓱᒥᖓ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑕᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑕᑯᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᖏᕐᕋᓂᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᕗᓕᒫᒥ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓂᐊᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᑕᐃᒪᐃᑦᑐᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑑᓂᖓᓂ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ.”

title: Gewerkschaften, Sozialabbau und Widerstand: Fast 25 Jahre Theorie und Praxis
content:
Dossier


„…

Als die größte Klippe für wirksame einheitliche Proteste und den Widerstand gegen die Hartz-Gesetze hat sich die breite Akzeptanz des Leistungsprinzips und der Lohnabhängigkeit als einziger Quelle der Existenzsicherung erwiesen. Dies gilt für die Gewerkschaftsbürokratie gleichermaßen wie für die meisten der (noch?) beschäftigten wie erwerbslosen Lohnabhängigen selbst. (…) Durch diese Propaganda wurden auch die Gewerkschaftsspitzen ins Boot geholt, die ihre oberste Aufgabe schon immer darin gesehen haben, „Menschen in Arbeit zu bringen“. (…) Die Mischung aus der angeblichen Alternativlosigkeit der Lohnabhängigkeit und der Angst vor Hartz IV lässt die Belegschaften weitere Verzichte bei Lohn wie Arbeitsbedingungen hinnehmen, anstatt die erkämpften Standards zugunsten aller Lohnabhängigen hochzuhalten

…“  Bittere Bilanz im

Was ist bereits gewerkschaftlich an Protesten geplant?


Bundesweite Aktionskonferenz in Göttingen am Sonntag, den 11. Oktober 


„

Wie auf dem zweiten digitalen Ratschlag am 8. September beschlossen, will der Gewerkschaftsratschlag im Nachgang der bundesweiten Proteste am 21. und 26. September eine bundesweite Aktionskonferenz in Göttingen veranstalten. Wenn weitere Kürzungen und Verschlechterungen unserer Arbeits- und Lebensbedingungen verhindert werden soll, dann können die bundesweiten Aktionen im September nur der Auftakt für weitere Proteste sein. Ziel der Konferenz ist es daher, mit möglichst vielen gewerkschaftlich Aktiven aus unterschiedlichen Regionen und Branchen in den Austausch zu treten und gemeinsam an einer wirkungsvollen Strategie zu arbeiten. Im Zentrum stehen dabei die Fragen: Wie können wir (noch) mehr Menschen in Bewegung bringen? Und wie können wir wirkungsvoll den Druck auf die schwarz-rote Bundesregierung erhöhen? Gemeinsam sollen hierfür die konkreten nächsten Schritte verabredet werden. Was steht in den nächsten Wochen auf dem Spiel und wie schaffen wir es, möglichst vielen Kolleginnen und Kollegen den Ernst der Lage bewusst zu machen?

…“

„

Am 11. Oktober 2026 trafen sich über 200 Gewerkschafter:innen zu der Aktionskonferenz unter dem Titel „Sozialstaat verteidigen – Die Reichen zur Kasse!“ Die Teilnehmer:innen kamen aus verschiedenen Gewerkschaften und Branchen, wobei Mitglieder von ver.di und IG Metall am stärksten vertreten waren. Auffallend war allerdings, dass aus den Betrieben der Automobilindustrie, aus denen in den letzten Wochen kämpferische Aufrufe gekommen sind, kaum jemand den Weg nach Göttingen angetreten hatte.


Da der Aufruf zu dieser Konferenz ausschließlich an gewerkschaftliche Aktivist:innen gegangen ist, war es nicht weiter verwunderlich, dass aus anderen Spektren wie Sozialinitiativen oder Wohlfahrtsverbänden niemand anwesend war. Dementsprechend war die Tagung auf Themen, die für Gewerkschafter:innen unmittelbar relevant sind, wie Rente, Arbeitszeit, Befristungen etc. ausgerichtet. Die vorgesehenen Kürzungen bei Elterngeld, Wohngeld oder Unterhaltsgeld spielten so gut wie keine Rolle, obwohl diese die Beschäftigten auch treffen werden. (…)


Bei der anschließenden Diskussion saßen drei ehrenamtliche Kolleg:innen auf dem Podium: Isa Senff von ver.di, Betriebsrätin bei der Post und Mitglied im Gewerkschaftsrat, Claudia Salvoch, Betriebsrätin bei Lufthansa in Frankfurt a. author: Unknown
title: Koçyiğit: We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice
content:
The Turkish government plans to increase spending on defense and the arms industry by more than 60 percent in 2027. Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, deputy parliamentary group chair of the DEM Party, criticized these budget priorities in light of the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process. While billions are being allocated to the military and security apparatus, funding remains insufficient for social welfare, healthcare, and education, she underlined.


At a press conference in the Turkish Parliament in Ankara, Koçyiğit put the planned defense expenditure for 2027 at 3.454 trillion Turkish lira (nearly 62.1 billion euros). This represents an increase of 60.28 percent compared to the 2026 budget. The planned increase, she argued, contradicts political statements about a peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question.


“We would have liked to see a substantial portion of the budget actually allocated to improving the well-being of the population and covering healthcare and education costs,” the DEM Party politician stated.


‘We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice’


Koçyiğit called for the peace process not to be limited to political statements and negotiations. She stated that a departure from decades of conflict-driven policies must also be reflected in the state’s economic priorities.


“The peace process must also be reflected in economic policy. If there is genuine sincerity here, we want to see all the effects of peace. We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice. We want to feel it in every aspect of life,” Koçyiğit said.


According to the DEM Party, the planned military expenditure is part of a fundamentally misguided budget policy. Koçyiğit argued that the draft 2027 central government budget primarily serves the interests of capital, while the social needs of the population are pushed into the background.


According to the figures presented by Koçyiğit, government expenditure is expected to increase by 44.09 percent and revenue by 44.35 percent. At the same time, the budget deficit is projected to rise by 42.57 percent. She was particularly critical of the growing burden of interest payments.


Koçyiğit pointed out that the public funds earmarked for these payments could instead be used to support farmers, improve healthcare for low-income people, and safeguard the living conditions of pensioners and minimum-wage workers.


Floods hit low-income communities particularly hard


In addition to the budget debate, Koçyiğit addressed the recent devastating floods in Istanbul, which claimed six lives and caused significant economic damage. Low-income neighborhoods were particularly hard hit.


She emphasized that the consequences of such disasters cannot be attributed solely to extreme rainfall, but are also the result of inadequate preventive measures and poor urban planning. These shortcomings, she added, further exacerbate existing social inequalities, particularly in poorer neighborhoods.


Koçyiğit criticized the lack of adequate attention to public infrastructure and the protection of the population, saying: “The floods once again demonstrate how closely social inequality, political priorities, and the population’s vulnerability to natural disasters are interconnected.”

author: David Swanson
title: That Canada Can’t Name U.S. Interference Proves U.S. Interference
content:
By

Yves Engler

, October 19, 2026


The cowardice. As evidence of U.S. meddling in Alberta’s political process grows, the Carney government buckled to pressure to withdraw its sponsorship of a conference because a panel mentioned U.S. interference.


Last Saturday the front of the

Globe and Mail

 blared “Elephant in the room”. The long article revealed how Republican operatives are assisting Alberta separatists who “have gone to D.C. offering fresh water and oil in exchange for American support.” In addition to hosting Alberta separatists in Washington, the Trump administration has made statements supporting their cause and MAGA-aligned media outlets have promoted Alberta becoming part of the U.S.


The

Globe

 story prompted NDP MP Heather McPherson to request an emergency parliamentary debate “on reports of foreign interference in Alberta’s upcoming referendum.” For its part, Public Interest Alberta called for an inquiry into whether foreign interference had taken place.


A week earlier, media in Quebec published a slew of stories about possible US inference with the premier asking CSIS to investigate. The media cited a February essay from the Arlington, Virginia, based Defense Analyses and Research Corporation that called for the US to destabilize the Canadian federation by supporting sovereigntists in elections.


Amidst growing evidence of US interference in Canada, Ottawa buckled to Trump administration pressure and withdrew its sponsorship of a European disinformation conference. The reason is that Disinfo2026 featured a panel that discussed the US being a source of “foreign information manipulation and interference” and another that discussed US meddling in the arctic (most of the panels were about Russia and other official enemies.)


The

Guardian

 reported that the Trump administration “pressured multiple countries to withdraw their sponsorship” and Ottawa buckled. Photos of the publicity at the conference in Lithuania show the Canadian logo covered up.


The cowardice is stunning. It shouldn’t be at all controversial to say the US has interfered in dozens of countries. In Haiti, for instance, Washington has meddled in an open and aggressive way for over a century. The list of countries in the Americas where the US has interfered in the political process is the list of countries in the Americas.


Long before the rise of Donald Trump and the Alberta successionist push, US interference was a far bigger threat to Canadians than alleged Chinese, Iranian or Russian interference. Not happy with Prime Minister John Diefenbaker’s attitude during the Cuban Missile Crisis or his ambivalence towards nuclear weapons in Canada, President John F. Kennedy worked to precipitate the downfall of his minority Conservative government. Kennedy preferred Lester Pearson’s Liberals who criticized Diefenbaker on Cuba and were willing to accept nuclear-armed Bomarc missiles.


“In the fall of 1962,” notes Peter McFarlane in

Northern Shadows:


Canadians and Central America

, “the State Department began to leak insulting references about Diefenbaker to the U.S. and Canadian press.” Articles highly critical of the Canadian prime minister appeared in the

New York Times

,

Newsweek

and other major U.S. media outlets. On January 3 the outgoing commander of NATO, US General Lauris Norstad, made a surprise visit to Ottawa where he claimed Canada would not be fulfilling her commitments to the north Atlantic alliance if she did not acquire nuclear warheads. Diefenbaker believed the US general came to Canada “at the behest of President Kennedy” to set the table “for Pearson’s conversion to the United States nuclear policy.”


During the 1963 election campaign Kennedy’s top pollster, Lou Harris, helped Pearson get elected prime minister. Kennedy backed Harris’ move, though he opposed an earlier request for the pollster to help British Labour leader Harold Wilson, which Harris then declined. Washington may have aided Pearson’s campaign in other ways. Diefenbaker wondered if the CIA was active during the 1963 election while External Affairs Minister Howard Green said a US agent attended a couple of his campaign meetings in BC.


Canadians are hostile to Trump administration meddling. Recently

275,000 signed

 an official parliamentary petition urging the federal government to expel US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra due to his meddling in Canadian affairs, support for Alberta separatism and promotion of US annexation. If Mark Carney …

author: Cecília Melo
title: Sem educação, clima ou fome: O dito e não dito na propaganda eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro
content:
“A boca fala do que o coração está cheio”, diz o versículo 31 do capítulo 12 do livro bíblico de Mateus. E apesar de a fé ter entrado em cheio na campanha presidencial, a lição não parece ter sido colocada em prática pela propaganda eleitoral do candidato de extrema direita Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Educação, fome, moradia, mobilidade e clima foram termos que nenhum dos guias de exibição gratuita na TV mencionaram ao longo de sua corrida presidencial. A palavra “constituição”, inclusive, não foi sequer mencionada pelo candidato em 14 inserções gratuitas até o momento.  


Segundo especialistas ouvidos pela

Agência Pública

, até então, o foco do discurso de Flávio Bolsonaro esteve em provocar comoção nos eleitores, através do medo e projetar força pessoal, através da autopromoção. 


A palavra “Brasil”, por exemplo, é a mais usada pela campanha do ultradireitista, numa frequência mais de 18 vezes superior a termos como “proposta(s)”.

 Embora faça parte do seu slogan “O Brasil vai Vencer”, “Brasil” também é usado conjuntamente a “Brasileiro(s)” e “Soberania” para criar sentido de pertencimento nacional, unidade, identidade coletiva e à defesa da nação. É o que diz a professora e pesquisadora em semiótica da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN) Lilian Muneiro.


A responsabilidade pela elaboração do conteúdo dos guias – roteiro, cenário e edição, por exemplo – é integralmente do partido político.

 A legislação garante o espaço na programação de rádios e televisões, comerciais e públicas, para veiculação do guia ou propaganda eleitoral de candidatos a cargos estaduais, federais e presidência durante 70 minutos por dia, distribuídos entre os comerciais da emissora. 


O levantamento da

Pública

 identificou as palavras mais repetidas por Flávio Bolsonaro nos 14 vídeos de seu guia eleitoral até agora. As peças estão disponíveis no perfil do candidato no YouTube e foram exibidas em rede nacional de 28 de agosto a 14 de outubro. O levantamento também identificou palavras que o candidato não citou, mesmo sendo assuntos de preocupação mundial. 


Para a professora do Departamento de Letras da UFRN e pesquisadora em análise do discurso, Cellina Muniz, a escolha de palavras de Flávio Bolsonaro não deve ser interpretada como coincidência, pois para seu campo de estudos, as palavras que usamos não são só nossas, e carregam uma história.

A construção narrativa visa projetar uma imagem de si “historicamente associada a regimes tipicamente autoritários. Governos totalitários, de diferentes posicionamentos ideológicos, sempre se pautaram na idolatria da figura mítica de um ‘chefe’ que tenta se afirmar simultaneamente como combatente e como guardião”, avalia.


O dito…


O termo “medo” aparece duas vezes mais que “esperança” nos guias eleitorais de Flávio Bolsonaro. “Esse discurso tenta comover seu público e construir sua adesão por meio do apelo emocional com a criação de um ‘inimigo’ a ser combatido (as milícias, o petismo etc.)”, avalia a professora Cellina Muniz.


“O Brasil nunca teve tanto medo”, disse o candidato no programa exibido no dia 1º de setembro, se referindo a grupos de facções espalhados pelo Brasil.

 “Comando Vermelho”, “facções”, “PCC” “organizações narcoterroristas” e “milícias” não são termos dos mais recorrentes no guia eleitoral, mas aparecem duas vezes mais que as palavras “democracia” e “paz” na mensagem passada aos eleitores.


Apesar do apelo ao medo, alguns fatos conectam o candidato ao universo que critica. Ainda em setembro, a revista

piauí

 expôs que em 2023, o senador Flávio enviou emenda parlamentar para o Instituto de Formação Profissional José Carlos Procópio (Ifop), uma ONG sediada na Taquara, reduto miliciano na Zona Oeste do Rio. O pedido partiu de Robson Calixto Fonseca, o “Peixe”, preso e condenado por agir como braço operacional da organização criminosa dos irmãos Brazão, os mandantes do assassinato de Marielle Franco. Peixe é apontado como o elo entre os Brazão e os milicianos da região de Jacarepaguá.


Em sua análise, a pesquisadora de semiótica Lilian Muneiro comentou que os vocábulos sobre segurança produzem juntos um “eixo de sentido associado à vulnerabilidade, ao risco, à necessidade de proteção e ao restabelecimento da ordem.

 Nesse conjunto, também é possível observar a dimensão passional do discurso”, afirma.


As escolhas do que compõe o discurso repetido de Flávio Bolsonaro também ajuda a indicar suas prioridades narrativas. O candidato do PL falou mais em …

title: Warum wählen immer mehr ArbeiterInnen in Deutschland die AfD?
content:
Dossier


„

… Arbeiter gehören zu den Berufsgruppen, die die AfD besonders stark unterstützen. (…) In der Parteienforschung wird seit geraumer Zeit diskutiert, ob der besondere Erfolg der AfD diese zu einer neuen Arbeiterpartei macht. Weitgehend unstrittig ist, dass ihr Wahlprogramm nicht unbedingt als arbeiterfreundlich bezeichnet werden kann. Dass sie dennoch unter Arbeitern überdurchschnittlich erfolgreich ist, wird unter anderem darauf zurückgeführt, wie sie Unzufriedenheit und Protest aufgreift. Die Studie legt nahe, dass Unzufriedenheit im Arbeitsleben zu einer Hinwendung zu Parteien führt, die radikale Veränderungen versprechen, wie dies bei der AfD der Fall ist

…“

Beitrag von Bernd Müller vom 03. Dezember 2023 in Telepolis


 („Warum wählen immer mehr Arbeiter in Deutschland die AfD?“) über die WSI-Studie zu AfD-Wählern – siehe mehr zu dieser und zum Thema:


Warum die AfD keine Arbeiterpartei ist

Bei der Bundestagswahl 2025 gaben 38 Prozent der Arbeiterinnen und Arbeiter ihre Stimme der AfD. Wie kann das sein, wo diese doch eine Politik gegen die Interessen von Arbeitnehmern vertritt? Der Soziologe Klaus Dörre sucht im Gespräch mit Claus-Jürgen Göpfert [am 14.10.2026 in Frankfurt/M.] nach Antworten. Die Veranstaltung findet nicht im Club Voltaire, sondern im Haus am Dom statt. Der Club ist Mitveranstalter

Video von Club Voltaire Frankfurt vom 15.10.2026


 (1:23 Std.) samt Transkript bei youtube


[„Gewerkschaftsratschlag“ und „Megazoom“ der Initiative Arbeiter*innen gegen Faschismus ] Nicht alle stehen rechts 


„

Wenige Tage nach der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt, bei der sechs von zehn Arbeiter*innen die AfD wählten, trafen sich über 140 Gewerkschafterinnen, Betriebsrätinnen und Beschäftigte zum „Megazoom“ der Initiative Arbeiter*innen gegen Faschismus. Kolleg*innen aus völlig unterschiedlichen Branchen: Pflege, Logistik, Medien, Bildung und Wissenschaft.


Was als Idee einer Berliner Intensivpflegekraft begann, nimmt konkrete Formen an:

Vom 22. bis 24. Januar 2027 soll eine bundesweite Konferenz unter dem Motto „Verstehen, Vernetzen, Verabreden“ in Halle (Saale) stattfinden

 – also in Sachsen-Anhalt, wo die AfD die meisten Stimmen holte. Mobilisiert wird dabei ohne große finanzielle Mittel, über persönliche und kollegiale Netzwerke in den Betrieben – genau darin sehen die Organisatorinnen ihre größte Stärke.


Zwei Treffen innerhalb einer Woche


Bereits am 8. September, zwei Tage vor dem Megazoom, hatten sich 114 Kolleginnen zum mittlerweile zweiten „Gewerkschaftsratschlag“ getroffen. Unter dem Titel „Sozialstaat verteidigen – Die Reichen zur Kasse“ stand der Austausch zu den Sozialprotesten im Mittelpunkt, mit Berichten einer ver.di-Vertrauensperson und einer Betriebsrätin über die Mobilisierung aus den Betrieben. (…)


Diverse Branchen waren auch hier vertreten: Ein Sporttherapeut aus Berlin moderierte die Videokonferenz, eine Intensivpflegekraft, ein Kollege der Berliner Stadtreinigung, eine Betriebsrätin vom Lufthansa-Bodenpersonal präsentierten sich als Initiatoren. „Wir sind die, die dieses Land am Laufen halten“, brachte es der Kollege der Stadtreinigung auf den Punkt. „Wenn wir uns wehren, dann kann uns keiner aufhalten.“


Wissenschaftlichen Input bei den „Arbeiter:innen gegen Faschismus“, die mittlerweile mehr als 500 Kolleg:innen auf ihrem Informationskanal zählen, lieferte ein Kollege, der sich schon lange mit der AfD beschäftigt. Im Zentrum steht das „AfD-Paradox“: überdurchschnittliche Zustimmung unter Arbeiterinnen bei einem Programm gegen ihre Interessen – verschärft dadurch, dass viele das sogar wissen.


Die AfD bediene den Mythos der „hart arbeitenden Bevölkerung“, der Partei der „Leistungsträger“, und stigmatisiert zugleich Sozialleistungsempfängerinnen: 66 Prozent der AfD-Wählerinnen halten Bürgergeldbezug für ein „bequemes Leben auf Kosten der Gesellschaft“. Zudem steht die Partei der organisierten Arbeiterinnenbewegung offen feindselig gegenüber.


Als Angriffspunkt gegen die AfD böte sich ihre Kampagne gegen „kulturfremde Fachkräfte“ an, die sich gegen so viele Kolleg:innen richtet, ohne die die Betriebe in der Pflege und der Logistik stillstehen würden. Die Diagnose des Referenten: Die Legitimationskrise des Parteienstaats habe ihr Epizentrum in der Arbeiter:innenklasse. Die Antwort muss demokratische Selbstwirksamkeit am Arbeitsplatz sein: Solidarität …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Qikiqtarjuaq man forfeits right to jury trial after sleeping in
content:
A Qikiqtarjuaq man lost his right to a jury trial after he accidentally slept through a court date in early September.


Ronald Audlakiak faces four charges, alleged to have taken place between Nov. 30 and Dec. 5, 2024. They include sexual assault with a weapon, assault involving suffocation, assault and uttering threats.


His four-day jury trial was supposed to begin on the morning of Sept. 1 in Qikiqtarjuaq.


Sixty community members had gathered at Qikiqtarjuaq’s community hall anticipating the start of jury selection, Justice Mark Mossey said in a written decision dated Oct. 15.


When Audlakiak didn’t present himself at court, Mossey delayed the proceedings until the afternoon. He did not give a reason, in an effort to avoid prejudicing the jurors.


Audlakiak then arrived when court reconvened and jury selection proceeded in the afternoon.


The accused once again failed to show up the next morning, for Day 2 of his trial.


Mossey declared a mistrial, issued an arrest warrant and, an hour later, RCMP found him asleep in his mother’s home.


When court reconvened in the afternoon to determine next steps, Audlakiak said he did not want to give up his right to jury trial and requested a hearing to determine whether that right had been waived.


“Mr. Audlakiak took the stand and explained that he simply slept in that morning,” said Mossey in his decision. “His evidence was that he only woke up when the police came to his home to execute the warrant for his arrest. He testified that he had gone to bed relatively early for him, around midnight, but did not have an alarm.”


Audlakiak acknowledged that he could have asked his mother or two adult sisters to wake him up, but he did not.


As for the apparent non-appearance during jury selection, Audlakiak explained he did show up and was in court with the group of potential jurors.


“Mr. Audlakiak did not provide an explanation as to why he did not present himself to the court, or his lawyer,” Mossey wrote.


Audlakiak has a constitutional right to a trial by jury, explained Mossey in his decision. But an accused who fails to appear at their own trial without a reasonable excuse can be deemed to have waived that right.


Defence lawyer Alan Regel argued that the “vast majority” of Qikiqtarjuaq’s population has been impacted by colonialism, and denying Audlakiak the right to a jury by his peers could be seen as an extension of that.


“What message does it send to the community, if the allegations are serious enough that the Crown files a direct indictment, personally signed by the Attorney General of Canada, that he is exposed to a jail term as great as 34 years, he has no chance of a preliminary inquiry — and he loses his right to have a jury simply because he slept in,” Regel said.


Regel also pointed out Audlakiak has been unemployed for years and is not accustomed to keeping a regular schedule.


“The court needs to consider as well, that the concept of time of an Inuit person growing up in a remote northern community … may be different from that of the court,” Regal said.


Mossey sided with the Crown, which argued sleeping in is not a reasonable excuse for missing a jury trial.


He took into consideration the cost — financial and otherwise — of delivering “meaningful access to justice” to people in the communities.


Mossey pointed out that the approximately 10 per cent of Qikiqtarjuaq’s population of approximately 600 people who showed up for jury duty was taken out of the workforce, from child-care duties and from hunting.


“The level of disruption to the community is evident,” Mossey said, adding allowing for a new jury trial would “minimize the cost” of the community fulfilling its jury obligations.


Mossey said at best, Audlakiak took a “cavalier approach to his jury trial” and that he was “wilfully blind in making the mistake of not taking even the smallest of precautions to ensure that he would be awake in time for trial.”


Audlakiak’s trial is set to resume, before a judge alone, on Feb. 25.

content:

У меня такое впечатление – и по тому, что появляется в наших различных периодических изданиях в Италии и за границей, и по тому, что присылают нам товарищи и что в значительной части остаётся неопубликованным из-за нехватки места или потому, что набор и вёрстка решительно не поспевают, – у меня, говорю я, впечатление, что нам ещё не удалось добиться, чтобы все поняли цели, которые мы ставим перед этим изданием.

В самом деле, есть те, кто, истолковывая по-своему наше явное стремление к практичности и к осуществлению наших идей, полагает, что мы намерены «начать ревизионистский процесс ценностей теоретического анархизма», и, сообразно со своими склонностями и предпочтениями, боится или надеется, что мы хотим отказаться – на практике, если не в теории – от наших строго анархических воззрений.

В действительности мы не считаем, как некоторые заставили нас сказать, что существует «антиномия между теорией и практикой». Мы, напротив, считаем, что вообще теория верна лишь тогда, когда она подтверждается практикой, и что в нашем случае, если анархию нельзя осуществить сразу, то вовсе не из-за недостаточности теории, а потому, что не все являются анархистами, и анархисты ещё не обладают силой, чтобы завоевать хотя бы свою собственную свободу и заставить уважать её.

Словом, мы остаёмся твёрдыми в идеях, которые с самого возникновения были душой анархического движения, и нам решительно не от чего отрекаться. Говорим это не в качестве заслуги, ибо если бы мы считали, что в прошлом впали в ошибку, мы почли бы своим долгом признать это и исправиться; но говорим это потому, что это факт. И тот, кто знает пропагандистские писания, распространённые повсюду основателями этого Журнала, вряд ли смог бы найти хоть одно противоречие между тем, что мы говорим сейчас, и тем, что говорили более чем пятьдесят лет назад.

Итак, речь идёт не о «ревизии», а о развитии идей и их применении к текущим обстоятельствам.

Когда анархические идеи были новинкой, которая изумляла и ошеломляла, и можно было лишь вести пропаганду ввиду далёкого будущего, а сами попытки восстания и добровольно спровоцированные и принятые на себя судебные процессы служили лишь для привлечения общественного внимания в целях пропаганды, – тогда могло быть достаточно критики современного общества и изложения идеала, к которому стремились. Даже вопросы тактики в сущности были лишь вопросами о лучших средствах для распространения идей и подготовки индивидов и масс к желанным преобразованиям.

Но сегодня времена более зрелые, обстоятельства изменились, и всё заставляет думать, что в срок, который мог бы быть близким, но который уж точно не очень далёк, мы окажемся в возможности и в необходимости применить теории к реальным фактам и показать, что мы не только более правы, чем другие, в силу превосходства нашего идеала свободы, но и потому, что наши идеи и наши методы наиболее практичны для достижения максимума свободы и благосостояния, возможного при нынешнем состоянии цивилизации.

Сама свирепствующая и тревожная реакция держит страну в состоянии неустойчивого равновесия, которое оставляет открытым путь как для всех надежд, так и для всех катастроф. И анархисты могут в любой момент быть призваны показать свою ценность и оказать на события давление, которое поначалу может и не быть преобладающим, но будет тем больше, чем больше будет их число и их моральная и техническая способность.

Следовательно, необходимо воспользоваться этим переходным периодом, который может быть лишь периодом спокойной подготовки, чтобы собрать как можно больше моральных и материальных сил и быть готовыми ко всему, что может произойти.

Факт, который нельзя упускать из виду, таков: мы – относительно небольшое меньшинство и останемся таковым до того …

title: Face à l'expulsion imminente des 280 habitant-es de la place de Milan, rassemblement à 16h devant la Métropole !
content:
La Métropole de Lyon s'apprête à remetrte à la rue 280 personnes dont des femmes et des enfants qui occuement un bâtiment vide place de Milan depuis le 6 mars 2026. Pour cela, elle a demandé à la Préfecture le concours de la force publique. Quelques personnes se verront proposer un hébergement d'urgence. Toutes les autres seront mises dehors, exposé-es à la violence de la rue, et aux intemperies, et bientôt au froid.


Non-assistance à personnes en danger


Le fait de ne pas intervenir volontairement ou de ne pas alerter les secours face à une personne en péril est puni par la loi. Le code pénal prévoit même des sanctions.


Pourtant la Métropole estime qu'un lointain projet de démolition, peut justifier de tels actes. La Préfecture, elle, rencontrée récemment, propose aux personnes de quitter le territoire.


Ainsi les résidentes de l'immeuble, parce qu'étrangères, ne peuvent plus prétendre à l'égalité devant la loi commune à tous et toutes. Ainsi elles se voient refusé le droit à l'hébergement d'urgence pourtant inconditionnel dans la loi. Pour cette raison, la Métropole comme la Préfecture s'apprêtent à faire subir un traitement dégradant et cruel à des personnes et ne reculent pas devant l'ignoble.


Cette politique d'agressivité contre des personnes et à plus forte raison contre des femmes et des enfants est dégradante pour ceux qui décident de ces actes mais aussi pour l'agglomération au nom de laquelle elle agit.


L'absence d'empathie dont la métropole fait preuve est inquiétante pour toutes et tous.


Si l'expulsion a lieu, ce sera un campement de plus dans la ville alors que le bâtiment restera vide.


Il n'est pas trop tard

 

! Ne baissons pas les bras

 

! Beaucoup de voix se sont déjà élevées pour condamner cette violence à l'encontre des occupantes et pour leur témoigner leur soutien.


Nous appelons les citoyens, associations, organisations, élu.es pour qui le respect des autres, la dignité, la fraternité, et l'égalité des droits sont le socle de la vie commune à demander ensemble à la Métropole de Lyon l'abandon de la décision d'expulsion

title: Juicio Molinos: “Antes de su secuestro, a mi hermano le ofrecieron plata para que dejara la fábrica y abandonara el país”
content:
En la cuarta jornada del debate oral y público por crímenes de lesa humanidad cometidos en la planta de Avellaneda de la firma Molinos Río de La Plata, el extrabajador de la sección Expedición, Guido Almaraz –cuyo hermano Ricardo Avelino Almaraz fue secuestrado el 7 de julio de 1976 junto a su esposa Celia Arzamendia en su casa de Lanús Este- declaró acerca de las protestas y acciones de reclamo por derechos laborales que los obreros llevaron adelante en los años previos al golpe de estado y que desembocaron en el señalamiento, persecución y amenazas de quienes terminarían siendo secuestrados y desaparecidos por un grupo de tareas que operaba directamente en el interior de la fábrica. En este juicio sólo se contemplan tres de un total de 24 trabajadores de Molinos desaparecidos: Francisco Fernández, Santos Ojeda y Roberto José Rivolta Bonino.


El miércoles 14 se llevó a cabo una nueva jornada del juicio en el que se ventila la responsabilidad penal de quien fuera jefe de Personal de la planta de Molinos Avellaneda, Emilio Parodi, en torno al secuestro de tres trabajadores que hasta el día de hoy permanecen desaparecidos: Francisco Fernández, Santos Ojeda y Roberto José Rivolta Bonino.


Los hechos ocurrieron el 7 de julio de 1976 y además de esas víctimas hubo otras 21 cuyos casos se investigan en distintas causas. A instancias del Tribunal Oral Federal 2 de La Plata -con la presidencia del magistrado Pablo Wilk y las vocalías de Nelson Jarazo y Yesica Sircovich-, el juicio atraviesa la etapa de declaraciones testimoniales que, en general y desde distintas perspectivas, aluden a la hipótesis fiscal respecto a un operativo ilegal llevado a cabo por las fuerzas de seguridad cuyos miembros ingresaron armados y portando listas que contenían nombre de trabajadores.


Las personas secuestradas fueron obligadas a subir a un camión del Ejército argentino sin que, hasta el momento, se conozca su destino. En ese marco, el exgerente de Recursos Humanos y jefe de Personal de la planta de Molinos Avellaneda, Emilio Parodi, es quien habría señalado a los trabajadores que luego serían secuestrados y desaparecidos por el Ejército y la Policía Federal.


En este juicio Parodi está siendo juzgado como coautor funcional del delito de privación ilegal de la libertad de Francisco Fernández, Santos Ojeda y Roberto José Rivolta Bonino, en virtud del rol y actividades desplegadas e inherentes al ejercicio de tareas gerenciales o de dirección de la empresa al momento de los hechos.


De acuerdo a la acusación fiscal, esa conducta facilitó la ocurrencia de los hechos y consolidaron dicha situación a través del impedimento del acceso a la información por parte de los familiares de las víctimas y, más allá de la petición solicitada, los hechos que se investigan constituyen delitos de lesa humanidad y en consecuencia son imprescriptibles para el ordenamiento jurídico argentino.


Uno de los testimonios brindados en la jornada del miércoles 14 de octubre fue el de un extrabajador de la sección Expedición de la planta de Molinos situada en Avellaneda, Guido Almaraz, cuyo hermano Ricardo y su cuñada Celia Arzamendia fueron secuestrados aquel 7 de julio de 1976 de su casa de Lanús Este.


“Antes del secuestro de mi hermano, el ambiente era insostenible para los trabajadores de Molinos. Había señalamientos, persecuciones dentro y fuera de la planta, amenazas y una presencia constante de un grupo al que llamaban ´bomberos’ pero que entiendo que eran policías dentro de la fábrica”, contextualizó el testigo.


De acuerdo a su relato, Ricardo Almaraz junto a otros trabajadores habían impulsado desde varios años antes del golpe de Estado las reuniones para intercambiar experiencias y organizar un conjunto de reclamos relativos a las pésimas condiciones laborales y de seguridad que existían en la fábrica que en ese entonces pertenecía al grupo Bunge y Born.


Fue así como nació una primera junta interna y un intento de toma de la fábrica a mediados de 1974 que no pudo terminar con resultados favorables respecto a los objetivos de la acción. Sin embargo, en marzo de 1975 se realizó una toma exitosa que terminó con la aceptación de casi la totalidad de las reivindicaciones que exigieron los trabajadores a la gerencia de Molinos.


Se trataba de aspectos básicos dentro del plexo de derechos laborales para la época: que la jornada laboral regular fuera de 8 horas diarias y que el resto de tiempo se computara y abonara como horas extra; que el sábado después …

title: “Şahiya Hebûn û Azadî” events kicks off in Germany
content:
The opening of the “Şahiya Hebûn û Azadî” events, organized in Stuttgart and the nearby cities of Reutlingen and Tübingen, has taken place.


The event, which featured cultural programs and political assessments, addressed the peace and democratic society process currently on the agenda of the Kurdish people.


The program attracted a large audience and featured performances by artists Simar, Narinxan, and Çiwo Bakur.


Speaking at the event, politician Faysal Sarıyıldız drew attention to the current stage of the process and the steps that need to be taken in the period ahead.


Sarıyıldız emphasized the need to embrace the process, take part in the communes to be established, and strengthen social organization. He also highlighted the importance of expanding democratic organization and continuing political activities.


Following the speeches, artists Simar, Narinxan, and Kurdish rap artist Çiwo Bakur took to the stage. The program, which included musical performances and cultural activities, concluded amid strong interest from participants.


As part of “Şahiya Hebûn û Azadî,” various cultural events and commemorative programs will be held over the coming month in Stuttgart and surrounding cities. Different programs are planned for each weekend, with events also expected to continue in other cities across the region.

title: Families demand reconstruction of destroyed guerrilla cemeteries in Şırnak
content:
Following the process initiated by the Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, many cemeteries in Kurdistan that had been prohibited for years were visited for the first time. HPG and YJA Star guerrillas were buried there, but have been demolished. Gravestones had been rendered unrecognizable by excavators, damaged in aerial attacks, and, in some cases, buried in pits. In Şirnak (Şirnex), where such attacks have become systematic, families are calling for the cemeteries to be rebuilt and access routes reopened.


 


The Cuma Bilika and Binevş Edessa Martyrs’ Cemetery on Mount Cûdî was bombed and destroyed in 2015; its surrounding wall, mosque, and guesthouse were also damaged. The cemetery, which could not be visited for years on the grounds that it was in a military security zone, was visited on 2 August 2026, for the first time in 11 years. On 11 October it was discovered that the gravestones had been buried together in a pit. At the cemetery, the family of Cihan Zilan (Hatice Erbağa), who fell as a martyr in 2006, found the grave they had been searching for over the years.


The Martyr Binevş Cemetery in the village of Basret on Mount Gabar was also targeted in the attacks. It was learned that the cemetery, built between 2010 and 2014, had been damaged and that numerous gravestones bearing the names of those who had fallen as martyrs had been broken.


The Goristana Martyr Rojat and Martyr Zelal Cemetery in the Besta region was also damaged in an aerial attack in 2017. The region was then declared a military security zone for many years.


The Kato-Feraşin cemetery is still off limits


Nuri Salgucak, an executive of MEBYA-DER in Şirnak who has visited the cemeteries alongside families and has been working on the issue, spoke about their current condition. Stating that they wanted to rebuild the cemeteries, Salgucak said the attacks constituted crimes against humanity.


Providing information about the number of bodies buried in the cemeteries in Cûdî, Besta, Gabar, and Kato-Feraşin, Salgucak said: “There are four martyrs’ cemeteries: Cûdî, Besta, Gabar, and Kato-Feraşin. There are 98 bodies in Cûdî, 160 in Besta, and 71 in Gabar. We do not know how many bodies are in Feraşin. Access to the area is still prohibited because a police station has been built next to it. Therefore, neither we nor the families are allowed to visit the cemeteries.”


Salgucak said the attacks on cemeteries are unacceptable, adding that “the condition of the cemeteries is terrible; they have demolished all of them. During periods of conflict, they wanted to take revenge on the dead. They have looted everything. They have left nothing among the graves and completely demolished the surrounding areas. We do not know how to describe those images. This is an entirely inhumane policy. Attacks on cemeteries are unacceptable, both legally and morally. It makes a person ashamed of humanity. When families see the cemeteries, they repeatedly say that this is unacceptable and that the cemeteries must be protected. Such attacks do not happen anywhere else in the world.”


Remains have all been identified


Salgucak said: “There are no unclaimed remains in Şirnak. All the families have provided blood samples in connection with their relatives’ remains. Some remains have been identified. However, even though some families provided blood samples years ago, the state has not responded to this matter for a long time. The blood samples have not yielded results, and the families are being kept waiting. Apart from that, there is a mass grave in the city where bodies were buried in the 1990s. It is located in the Cumhuriyet neighborhood of Şirnak. We do not know how many people are buried in this grave.” 


The main demand is reconstruction


Nuri Salgucak said: “As an organization, we are carrying out work on this issue. First, we visit the cemeteries together with the families. We want to rebuild all of these cemeteries. How this proceeds will depend on the course of the ongoing process. The other cemeteries we visit are still officially off-limits, but we are taking the initiative and going there. As the images show, the cemeteries have been left in ruins. They have flattened the Besta Martyrs’ Cemetery with excavators. The situation in Cûdî is no different. This is clearly visible in the footage we have recorded.”

title: Arîn Student Association opens in Istanbul
content:
The Arîn Student Association opened in İskender Paşa neighbourhood in Istanbul's Fatih district, established through the initiative of university students. The association attracted considerable interest from students, young people and local residents within hours of opening.


The opening ceremony began with traditional clothing, slogans, applause and halay dances. Feleknaz Karabaş, a member of the Istanbul Peace Mothers' Assembly, was the first to speak. Karabaş said, “It is a source of pride to see you young people protecting your language and culture. Without you, we are incomplete. Language, culture and art are the foundations of a people's existence. Let us protect our existence.”


 


Students reject impositions and come together to build an alternative


Arîn Student Association member Melisa Çelik then read out a press statement. Çelik highlighted the lack of spaces where students can express themselves freely, saying: “Educational institutions, which should contribute to the qualitative development of society in cultural, scientific and social fields, are instead seeking to create obedient and passive masses serving the interests of those in power in particular and capitalist modernity in general. As students, we reject these impositions and have come together here today to develop an alternative.”


University students then performed a play titled Avare, receiving enthusiastic applause for their message: “Against assimilation, young people turn to Arîn!”


Halay dances and slogans continued outside the Arîn Student Association as members Merve Sultan Daş and Abdulmelik Çelik spoke to ANF about Arîn, which they described as a space where university students could “breathe”.


‘Arîn is an alternative academy’


Merve Sultan Daş began by saying that they were living through a time when coming together as a community was more necessary than ever. Daş said: “Students needed a place where they could express themselves democratically and breathe freely. That is why we decided to open Arîn.”


Abdulmelik Çelik then explained the story behind Arîn's name: “Several alternative names were initially proposed. A democratic process was then launched to choose the name. The main reason we chose ‘Arîn’ was its meanings, such as ‘spark’ and ‘before the fire’. Since this is a student association, we chose the name to harness the revolutionary fire of the youthful spirit.”


Merve Sultan Daş said: “We are actually in the process of building a democratic society,” stressing that developing educational spaces and focusing on culture and the arts were among the most important requirements of this process. Daş added, “That is why we aim to create an environment where students can come and develop their cultural and artistic skills, sing songs and spend time with their friends, learning and developing together. We want this to be an alternative to cafés, a place where they can express themselves freely.”


 


Abdulmelik Çelik described Arîn as an academy established as an alternative to universities. Merve Sultan Daş concluded by outlining the association's plans for workshops and inviting young people to take part: “We will have Kurdish, Zazaki and English language workshops. We will also focus on music, including the saz, a traditional long-necked string instrument, the erbane, a frame drum, and the piano. Our doors are always open, and our tea is always hot. We look forward to welcoming you.”


An International Youth Delegation from eight different countries, which had applied to the Ministry of Justice for a meeting with Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan, also joined Kurdish young people in halay dances at Arîn's opening ceremony.


Isabelle W., a member of the German Democratic Youth Union (YUNA) who was part of the delegation, spoke to ANF about the opening of the Arîn Student Association and the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


‘The process is an opportunity to build a communal society’


Isabelle W. spoke against the backdrop of music, halay dances and slogans echoing through the street. Isabelle W. said: “I think it's wonderful that Kurdish students, and indeed all young students, have a place where they can come to learn more about their own cultures, learn their mother tongues and spend time with organised people. We are here now, and there is so much happening in the street... It's really beautiful to see everyone embracing their own culture. Bijî berxwedana ciwanan! (Long live the resistance of the …

title: YBŞ spokesperson: We want genuine integration
content:
Hadi Elyas, spokesperson for the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ), spoke about the integration of security and administrative institutions in Shengal into the Iraqi state structure during the program “Hevpeyvîneke Taybet” (Special Interview), broadcast on Çira TV.


Referring to their meetings with Iraqi state officials, Hadi Elyas said: “Our talks with senior security and military officials began in February. The aim was to reach a sound and secure agreement on the integration of our forces, institutions, and community into the Iraqi state system. This is also a process that serves Iraq’s sovereignty. We take this matter very seriously. A formal and legitimate framework is also needed to resolve the other problems facing Shengal. Resolving this issue is a first step toward broader solutions.”


Emphasizing that the problems in Shengal cannot be reduced to security concerns alone, Hadi Elyas continued: “Although security is a very important issue, there are other fundamental matters that need to be addressed, such as the return of displaced people, compensation for citizens, the reconstruction of residential areas, and locating missing persons and those held captive by ISIS. If the security issue is addressed in a formal and systematic manner, it will provide a solid foundation for protecting the identity and achievements of the Yazidi people and guaranteeing their rights within the Iraqi state.”


Noting that discussions on integration came to the fore when Ali Zeydi’s government took office, the YBŞ spokesperson said: “As a force that emerged during a critical period, we were also part of this process. We have never considered ourselves separate from the state. Formal integration is not something that should remain merely on paper. It is a step that will strengthen our forces, our community, and the state itself. We want genuine integration that preserves the distinct characteristics of our community and our forces and prevents a tragedy similar to what happened in 2014 from occurring again.”


Hadi Elyas continued:


“We reached agreement on many points during the talks, particularly in meetings with the prime minister. We want the Êzdîxan Asayish (Yazidi local forces), YBŞ, and YJŞ (Shengal Women’s Units) to become part of the state system. Discussions also focused on protecting the rights of fighters who have resisted since 2014 and integrating them into the system in a way that allows them to continue serving the people of Shengal. Negotiations are still ongoing to achieve an effective outcome.”


Describing the length of the integration process as normal, Hadi Elyas said: “This process is not simply about transferring a military unit. We are dealing with a sensitive issue that will directly affect the future of Shengal, its people, and its forces. It involves aspects that are new to Iraq, such as the presence of women’s forces and the Êzdîxan Asayish. Comprehensive studies and discussions are being conducted on integration, geographical conditions, and the social situation to achieve a lasting and sustainable solution.”


Rejecting allegations that the YBŞ is opposed to the Iraqi state, the YBŞ spokesperson continued: “The Yazidi community and our forces have made sacrifices for Iraq’s sovereignty. At a time when the Iraqi flag was not flying in Anbar, Tikrit, or Mosul, our forces raised it in Shengal. This demonstrates our commitment to this country. Claims to the contrary are nothing more than propaganda. Our community has never considered itself separate from Iraq and has struggled to strengthen the sovereignty of the state.”


Hadi Elyas concluded his remarks with the following message to the Iraqi state:


“Our message to the Iraqi government is that we are serious about formal and systematic integration and want our forces to become part of the state’s security system.


Our message to our people is that this step will safeguard the future, security, and rights of our community.


Genuine stability can only be achieved through the recognition of Yazidi rights, justice, and the reconstruction of Shengal. We hope this process will produce results soon and serve both our community and the sovereignty of the Iraqi state.”
