author: Unknown
title: Ronda Tayfur: Jineolojî enables us to look at problems from different perspectives
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference, held in Haelen, the Netherlands, and titled “The Role of Jineolojî in Building a Democratic and Communal Life,” brought together participants from across Europe. Speaking to ANF, Ronda Tayfur discussed how she came to know Jineolojî, her experiences in the women’s freedom struggle, and the discussions held at the conference.


Tayfur, who works within the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Switzerland, emphasized that Jineolojî is not merely a theoretical field but offers a perspective that helps people approach the problems they encounter in everyday life from different angles.


I first encountered Jineolojî in 2014


Tayfur said she first encountered Jineolojî in 2014, while studying at university in Istanbul. The workshops and discussions she attended during that period helped her develop a new perspective. “I first encountered Jineolojî in 2014, when I was studying at university in Istanbul. It was something entirely new to me. That year was when I first engaged with Jineolojî, attended its workshops, and took part in discussions.


Because of the environment we lived in and the geography in which we grew up, we had always been interested in women’s freedom and gender consciousness. But Jineolojî encouraged us to look at things from a different perspective. That is what drew me to it.”


Tayfur said that since discovering Jineolojî, she has sought to apply its perspective not only in organized political work but throughout every aspect of her life.


“Since then, I have tried, and continue to try, to look at everything through the lens of Jineolojî, not only in my work or in the areas where I am active, but in every part of life. I also try to address the problems I encounter through this perspective. First and foremost, I would speak of the plurality of life. There is no single quest for freedom, just as there is no single way to solve problems. Solutions can also be found by looking at things through different windows.”


Variety of experiences at workshops


Tayfur also spoke about the workshops held as part of the European Jineolojî Conference, noting that she participated in the workshop on Democratic Society and the Democratic Family.


She described the methods used in the workshops as creative and productive, adding that bringing together women from different institutions and fields of work enriched the discussions. She said:  “We held workshops yesterday, and I took part in the Democratic Society and Democratic Family workshop. The working method was genuinely creative and also more productive. We could call this one of the distinctive aspects of Jineolojî. We discussed several issues. Having a workshop with broad participation, bringing together people from different backgrounds and institutions, had its advantages. We discussed these issues from a broad perspective, and everyone brought different viewpoints and opinions.”


Tayfur said that the concepts of the democratic family and democratic society have long been subjects of discussion within the women’s movement. She noted that the conference provided an opportunity to revisit these discussions through the perspective of Jineolojî.


 


Emphasizing the importance of strengthening the links between Jineolojî and the work of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Switzerland, she said: “The democratic family and democratic society have always been concepts we discuss. But now, through the lens of Jineolojî, we can ask what we have overlooked and what we need to complete or develop further. We can also better understand how to build relationships and work together with Jineolojî and the Kurdish Women’s Movement, of which I am a part and within which I carry out my work.”


The importance of sharing experiences


Tayfur said the conference had also included discussions on the legacy and influence of actually existing socialism. She described these discussions as important for connecting ideas to ongoing work and developing plans for the future. She added: “We also discussed the effects of actually existing socialism today. People do not remain confined to the present moment; they try to connect these discussions with the work they are doing and carrying out. At the very least, they try to develop a plan or program. For us, this is something productive and creative. No matter how much social work we carry out, when we come together like this, we realize that there are still patterns we have not broken and ideas that have not yet …

author: Unknown
title: Eskişehir’de İklim Adaleti Forumu: “İklim adaleti mücadelesi sınıfsal temelde ele alınmalı”
content:
Eskişehir Ekoloji Derneği tarafından Taşbaşı Kültür Merkezi’nde İklim Adaleti Forumu düzenlendi. İklim krizinin sınıfsal boyutunun, emisyon ticaret sisteminin, madencilik faaliyetlerinin ve uluslararası iklim politikalarının ele alındığı forumda, ekoloji mücadelesinin emek ve yaşam hakkı mücadelesiyle birleştirilmesi gerektiği vurgulandı.

Forumda avukat Mert Yedek ve avukat Onat Öncü’nün yanı sıra Eskişehir-Bilecik Tabip Odası Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Murat Erol, TMMOB Makina Mühendisleri Odası Eskişehir Şubesi adına Mustafa Haydar Tiftikçi, İYİP Odunpazarı İlçe Başkanı Gürol Yer, Çiftçi-Sen Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Hasan Cengiz Yazar, Emek Partisi Eskişehir İl Örgütü adına Şevval Duran, ziraat yüksek mühendisi Zevaiddin Özcan, Tüm Emeklilerin Sendikası Eskişehir Şubesi Yürütme Kurulu Üyesi Alim Yıldızkan, Eskişehir Gıda Topluluğundan Emin İrfan Akkaya, Türkiye Ormancılar Derneği Eskişehir Temsilcisi Deniz Hakan Durmuş, Eskişehir Barosu Kent ve Çevre Komisyonu Başkanı Ecir Ayaş ve akademisyen Ozan Devrim Yay söz aldı.

Avukat Mert Yedek, iklim krizinin sonuçlarının toplumun bütün kesimlerini aynı biçimde etkilemediğine dikkat çekerek iklim adaleti mücadelesinin sınıfsal bir perspektifle ele alınması gerektiğini söyledi. Aşırı yağışlar, sel ve taşkınlar gibi iklim krizinin sonuçlarından en fazla emekçilerin ve yoksulların etkilendiğini belirten Yedek, sermaye sahiplerinin ise sahip oldukları ekonomik olanaklarla kendilerini bu sonuçlardan kısmen koruyabildiğini ifade etti.

Yedek, “Bir avuç, yüzde 1’e tekabül edecek sermayedarlar bir şekilde buradan kendi birikimleri ve servet birikimleriyle birlikte kendilerine sürdürülebilir bir yaşamı var edebiliyorlar. Ama adalet kısmı burada açığa çıkıyor” sözleriyle iklim krizinin yarattığı eşitsizliğe dikkat çekti. Krizin sorumluluğunun ve sonuçlarının toplumun farklı kesimleri arasında eşit dağılmadığını vurgulayan Yedek, iklim adaleti tartışmasının yalnızca çevresel etkilerle sınırlı tutulamayacağını belirtti.

İklim krizi karşısında bireysel tüketim alışkanlıklarının değiştirilmesinin çözüm olarak sunulmasını da eleştiren Yedek, su tüketimini azaltmak, toplu taşıma kullanmak ve bireysel karbon ayak izini düşürmek gibi önerilerin büyük şirketlerin ve üretim faaliyetlerinin sorumluluğunu geri plana ittiğini söyledi. Bireysel önlemlerin öneminin, üretim ilişkileri ve sermayenin doğa üzerindeki etkisi tartışılmadan ele alınamayacağını belirten Yedek, iklim krizinin yapısal nedenlerine odaklanılması gerektiğini ifade etti.

Yeşil dönüşüm ve net sıfır emisyon hedefleri kapsamında gündeme getirilen emisyon ticaret sistemini de değerlendiren Yedek, karbon salımının alınıp satılabilen ekonomik bir değere dönüştürülmesine karşı çıktı. Karbon salımının piyasa mekanizmaları üzerinden düzenlenmesinin iklim krizini ortadan kaldırmaya yetmeyeceğini belirten Yedek, “Karbon devredilebilir, ücretlendirilebilir, ekonomik bir değer verilebilir ve tahsis edilebilen bir meta hâline getirildi” dedi.

Yedek, emisyonların ticarete konu edilmesinin iklim krizinin çözümünü piyasanın işleyişine bağladığını belirterek, “Bizim tartıştığımız bu makro iklim krizi dediğimiz ve herkesin yakıcı bir şekilde hissettiği durumu önleyebilmesi ne yazık ki mümkün değil” ifadelerini kullandı. İklim politikalarının şirketlerin kârlarını ve piyasa ilişkilerini korumak yerine emisyonların azaltılmasını ve ekolojik yıkımın önlenmesini esas alması gerektiğini vurguladı.

Yedek, yeşil dönüşüm politikalarının yalnızca yenilenebilir enerji yatırımları üzerinden değerlendirilmesine karşı çıkarak bu dönüşüm için gerekli görülen madenlerin hangi amaçlarla kullanıldığının da sorgulanması gerektiğini söyledi. Nadir toprak elementlerinin yalnızca enerji teknolojilerinde değil, savunma sanayisi ve silah teknolojilerinde de kullanıldığına dikkat çeken Yedek, bu kaynaklar üzerindeki rekabetin uluslararası güç mücadeleleriyle bağlantısına işaret etti.

Türkiye’de madencilik faaliyetleri ve acele kamulaştırma kararlarının yerel halkın yaşamı üzerindeki etkilerine değinen Yedek, Eskişehir’de nadir toprak elementlerinin çıkarılmasına yönelik girişimlerin de bölge halkının üretimini ve geleceğini doğrudan ilgilendirdiğini belirtti. Yıllardır işledikleri topraklardan geçimini sağlayan köylülerin, yaşamlarını etkileyecek kararların alınmasında yeterince söz sahibi olmadığını ifade etti.

Üreticilerin yaptıkları harcamalar, ektikleri ürünler ve gelecek dönem için kurdukları ekonomik planların bu süreçlerde belirsizliğe sürüklendiğini belirten …

author: Unknown
title: Jineolojî must connect with society’s needs, say women at Haelen conference
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference titled “The Role of Jineolojî in Building a Democratic and Communal Life,” is being held in Haelen. The third session focused on “Socializing Knowledge and Decolonizing Science.” Participants discussed collective learning, educational methods, knowledge production and the role of women’s knowledge in building a democratic society.


Presentations were given by Jineolojî Committee members Yasemin Anday and Nûjîn Derya, and Jînda Amed of the European Kurdish Women’s Movement (TJK-E). Topics included educational experiences, research, the social role of academies and strengthening local organization.


Education was the foundation for building a new human being


Reflecting on the Kurdish Freedom Movement’s educational experience and the development of Jineolojî from this legacy, Jînda Amed said education had been a central focus since the movement’s beginnings. Initiated with limited resources under the leadership of Haki Karer and Kemal Pir, educational activities gradually expanded and adopted new methods. Their aim was not only to transmit knowledge but also to shape people’s identities and personalities.


She said education emphasized ethics, morality, love for humanity and nature, women’s liberation and overcoming feudal influences. “Jineolojî, too, grew out of these values. It is their product,” she stated.


Amed stressed the importance of education and self-education in overcoming patriarchal and capitalist mindsets, highlighting personal commitment and self-development. She also emphasized continuing educational and awareness-raising activities from a women’s liberation perspective.


Women's education and organizing in Europe


Amed said educational initiatives in Europe had developed under the leadership of women such as Binevş Agal and Sakine Cansız, despite state repression and patriarchal attitudes. These experiences helped strengthen cultural activities, assemblies and communal organizing.


She said Kurdish women’s educational experiences had offered important answers to the question of how to build a free life. “Women not only overcame patriarchal oppression but also developed an answer to the question, ‘How should we live?’” she said.


Although conferences, training programs and research projects are being conducted, Amed argued that more needs to be done and that academies and committees must become more involved in community life.


She stressed that Jineolojî must strengthen its connection with the socially grounded and internationalist nature of the women’s liberation struggle. Its work should address society’s needs rather than remain confined to academic settings, integrating education and research with social relationships and grassroots organizing.


Anday: Learning must be part of collective life


Jineolojî Committee member Yasemin Anday discussed more than a decade of educational work and alternative learning methods developed in Europe. She said Jineolojî emerged to expose women’s enslavement as a root cause of social problems and to develop knowledge for a free life.


“The dagger in society’s back was women’s enslavement; no social problem could be fundamentally resolved without removing it. Jineolojî emerged as a science that identifies this dagger, pulls it out and replaces it with the knowledge needed for a free life,” she said.


Anday explained that European initiatives drew on the Kurdish Women’s Movement’s experiences of education and self-education. Activities initially took the form of conferences, seminars and reading groups before reaching a new stage with the first European camp in Germany in 2017. These camps made learning part of a shared way of life in which women lived, debated, researched and shared responsibilities.


Emphasizing that knowledge must be experienced collectively and connected to everyday life, Anday said communal living exposed individualistic habits and social contradictions. Practices such as xwebûn (selfhood), hevaltî (companionship), criticism and self-criticism, and tekmil (collective evaluation) created opportunities for women to reflect on themselves and their relationships.


“Communal life is not simply about sharing a space; it requires continuous effort to think together, take responsibility, confront contradictions and transform relationships,” she said.

title: Pınar Güneş’in öldürülmesiyle ilgili soruşturmada 4 tutuklama
content:
İzmir’in Çeşme ilçesinde, Pınar Güneş’in (28), öldürülmesine ilişkin yürütülen soruşturmada gözaltına alınan 5 şüpheliden 4’ü tutuklandı.

Olay, 14 Ekim’de gece saatlerinde Alaçatı Mahallesi'nde meydana geldi. Pınar Güneş (28) ile Y.U. ve A.M. isimli iki erkek arasında belirlenemeyen nedenle tartışma çıktı. Şüpheliler, Güneş'i tabancayla ateş edip, yaraladı. Çevredekilerin ihbarı üzerine olay yerine sağlık ve polis ekipleri sevk edildi. Olay yerinde ilk müdahalesi yapılan Güneş, ambulansla, Çeşme Alper Çizgenakat Devlet Hastanesine kaldırıldı. Burada tedaviye alınan Güneş, kurtarılamadı.

Olayın ardından kaçan şüpheliler Y.U. ve A.M., polis ve jandarma ekiplerinin ortak çalışması ile Urla ilçesinde suç aleti tabancayla yakalandı. Soruşturmanın devamında G.C., Ö.A. ve M.F. de ekiplerce gözaltına alındı.

İşlemlerinin ardından adliyeye sevk edilen Y.U, A.M, G.C. ve Ö.A. çıkarıldıkları sulh ceza hakimliğince tutuklandı. M.F. ise adli kontrolle serbest bırakıldı. Kadına ateş eden şüphelinin 17 yaşındaki A.M. olduğu öne sürüldü.

author: Rizomatica
title: Abogados del caso Lautaro presentaron recurso de nulidad de sentencia en la Corte de Apelaciones de Temuco
content:
El día jueves 15 de octubre se llevó a cabo la vista de los recursos de nulidad que las defensas de Pelentaro Llaitul, Jorge Caniupil, Juan Carlos Mardones, Luis Menares Chanilao, para que la Corte de Apelaciones invalide la sentencia definitiva del Tribunal Oral de Temuco, que el pasado 13 de julio de este año resolvió condenarlos por ataques incendiarios ocurridos en noviembre del 2022 en dos fundos cercanos a Lautaro, y posteriormente la quema de una camioneta en el sector de Cholchol.


Se solicita a la corte de apelaciones que invalide de sentencia y que dicte sentencia de reemplazo, porque la defensa considera errores jurídicos como condenar dos veces por un mismo delito, o por delitos que no fueron realmente demostrados y considera que están cumpliendo adicionalmente penas que fueron mucho más altas que las que en derecho correspondían.


Según Marco Oñate Escobar, uno de los abogados defensores:


“

Este es un proceso muy sesgado que se llevó a cabo en contra de ellos, solo por ser perteneciente a la Coordinadora Arauco Malleco.


En el juicio oral se pedían penas, que en la sumatoria llegaban casi a 100 años en algunos de los casos. La fiscalía, esta es la historia que no cuentan ellos, fueron derrotados en más de la mitad de sus imputaciones, se recalificaron las figuras penales más gravosas, era una supuesta flagrancia, y entonces intentaron imputar delitos lo máximo que se pudiera a fin de incrementar y elevar las penas y que sean penas de cárcel. Situación que, si bien es cierto, hay condenas, son notoriamente bajas si hacemos un cálculo, una relación con lo que se pedía al comienzo”.


Palabras de Ernesto Llaitul, werken de los presos políticos Mapuche de la CAM:


“

N

osotros, como organización y como comunidades en lucha, he

mos


sido enfático

s


en decir que esto se debe a una persecución política en contra de militantes Mapuche, del movimiento Mapuche


a

utonomista, en específico de nuestra organización, de la coordinadora


Arauco Malleco.


El día de hoy, nosotros no acatamos el fallo, la sentencia condenatoria, no reconocemos tampoco la existencia, la participación de nuestros peñis en este hecho, pero hacemos esta alegación política, como muy bien lo dice el abogado, en relación a circunstancias técnicas o prácticas en las que nosotros tenemos hoy día que desenvolvernos dentro de lo que exige la ley”.


Familiares y comunidad se mantendrán a la espera de que la corte, el día 4 de noviembre de 2026, a las 8 de la mañana, comunique la sentencia donde se acojan los recursos presentados.

author: Unknown
title: Из колонии вышел Василий Куксов, осужденный по делу «Сети» в 2020 году
content:
По данным «Медиазоны», вчера, 16 октября, 38-летний Василий Куксов освободился из колонии №16 в Нижегородской области. Сегодня утром он доехал на поезде до Сердобска в Пензенской области и встретился там с родными.

В 2020 году Куксова, музыканта и инженера-конструктора, приговорили в Пензе к девяти годам колонии по делу «террористического сообщества "Сеть"» (всего обвиняемые по этому делу получили до 18 лет заключения).

Дело возбудили в октябре 2017 года. Сотрудники ФСБ тогда обвинили антифашистов и анархистов, многих из которых объединяло увлечение страйкболом, в том, что они создали «террористическое сообщество» и планировали «раскачать народные массы для дальнейшей дестабилизации политической обстановки в стране».

Тогда в течение месяца силовики задержали Куксова, а также Илью Шакурского, Дмитрия Пчелинцева, Андрея Чернова, Армана Сагынбаева и Егора Зорина. Формальным поводом для начала уголовного преследования стала явка с повинной Зорина. Молодого человека задержали с наркотиками, и он дал показания о террористическом сообществе. Впоследствии дело против него прекратили. В январе 2018 года в Петербурге по тому же делу были задержаны Виктор Филинков и Игорь Шишкин. 11 апреля обвинения предъявили еще одному петербуржцу — Юлию Бояршинову.

Сначала большинство фигурантов дали признательные показания, но позже отказались от них, заявив о пытках. О насилии и применении тока со стороны силовиков сообщали Виктор Филинков, Дмитрий Пчелинцев, Илья Шакурский, Арман Сагынбаев и Андрей Чернов. Следственный комитет не возбудил дело ни по одному заявлению обвиняемых о пытках. О пытках и давлении со стороны силовиков также рассказывали пятеро свидетелей по делу.

Василий Куксов говорил в суде, что сотрудники ФСБ при задержании избили его со словами: «Ты попал, жизнь твоя кончена», — и угрожали отрезать палец. Несмотря на это, он никогда не давал признательных показаний. Во время следствия в пензенском СИЗО-1 у него перед приговором диагностировали открытую форму туберкулеза. Его не госпитализировали и продолжили содержать c другими фигурантами дела. После вступления приговора по делу «Сети» в силу Куксова в ноябре 2020 года доставили в нижегородское ЛИУ-3 для больных туберкулезом. Его выписали в январе 2022 года. В нижегородской ИК-16 после этого его несколько раз отправляли в штрафной изолятор.

author: Andrés
title: No soy amigo de los que cooperan, los quiero fuera fuera fuera
content:
La pierna de un jubilado que cae por el chorro de un hidramte


La decadencia moral y generalizada de un país se mide por la cantidad de recursos empleados en contra de la propia población, y de la vida misma. Que todo gobierno autoritario invierte onerosos recursos en las Armas es un hecho más que probado. De lo que se habla bastante menos es que en países donde el trabajo formal se viene erosionando desde hace tanto, los puestos en las policías y fuerzas armadas los ocupan en amplia mayoría las clases socioeconómicas más vulnerables. Y entonces la extorsión del trabajo estable opera sobre los sujetos al punto de quebrar todo principio, cortar los trazos democráticos y convertir a los “servidores del orden” en cómplices de un poder que no los quiere más que dentro de una institución cuyo funcionamiento mafioso los subordina, los presiona. Y en muchos casos termina descerebrándolos al punto en que ni siquiera pueden abrir los ojos ante la traición que cometen cada vez que apuntan un arma, empuñan un palo, empujan a un compatriota, golpean a un viejo, gasean a una niña, ahorcan entre varios a un hombre solo, disparan a un joven, lo esconden, gasean a la población y lastiman toda posibilidad de concordia. El todos contra todos y cada uno contra sí mismo está a la orden del día bajo esta gestión fascista.

Por Andrés Manrique (ANRed).


El  jubilado golpeado por la presión del hidrante, apuntado por la Policía Federal


Quienes cobran para ir a pegar, disparar y ahogar a estudiantes, a discapacitados, a viejos se cuentan entre lo más bajo de los traidores. Si era el último círculo, cuando además se detenta la fuerza física, se suma una vuelta más.


“Vos te pasaste al otro lado de la vereda”


Tirarle gas a un viejo de camperita, empujarlo.


Pegarle con el puño a toda carrera y por la espalda a un fotorreportero en la cara.


Echarle la moto de alta cilindrada a alguien que va en paz por la vereda.


La Policía Federal agolpeando con el hidrante al jubilado de espaldas


Acorralar a dos fotógrafos en un zaguán y dispararle a quemarropa: contra el abdomen, a las piernas, a la cabeza: en la cara y a los ojos.


Clavarte la rodilla en la espalda cuando estás en el piso, boca abajo, desarmado, reducido por el sobrepeso de aquel al que un trote lo haría infartar, mientras otro te lastima las muñecas con el precinto, y un tercero apoya todo su odio contra las vértebras de tu cuello.


Amedrentar con los escudos, con las tonfas, acelerando las motos, haciendo chasquear las  escopetas, con  bombas de estruendo, postas de goma y armas mal llamadas no letales, con las que no se cansan de matar o herir de gravedad. Revolear bastones, batiendo el aerosol de gas pimienta sobre la cara de una nena, de una anciana, de una vecina que pierde su  bolsa de compras.


“Esa es la diferencia entre la gorra y la visera”


Gasear a pibes con carteles, irse encima de discapacitados. Golpear con la escopeta, salir a cazar a compatriotas que protestan. Salir a cazar fantasmas en manada. Seguir órdenes, aunque vayan en contra de todos los principios. Golpear a alguien indefenso, lastimar entre muchos a uno solo.


Miserable soldadesca del brazo tilingo del poder que nos ahoga. Dése vuelta, reconozca dónde está su enemigo. Identifiquelo, usted sabe que la mano que le pone el sueldo es la misma que lo va a someter a la mazmorra cuando no sirva más.


¿Más traidor que un desclasado?


¿Peor traidor que alguien al que han entrenado para que se odie a sí tanto que odia a todo el que tiene a su alrededor?


Fotos: Andrés Manrique

author: Said Alsaloul
title: My Study of Dystopian Fiction Never Prepared Me for Reality Here in Gaza
content:
As a teacher of English literature in Gaza, I’ve seen my relationship to books be overturned by the violence around me.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

As a 27-year-old English literature graduate and English teacher from Gaza, I have always been passionate about teaching. I enjoy helping my students learn to speak English by reciting stories aloud.

I connect with them through English, so I collected every English-language book my hands could reach. Before October 7, 2023, during my fourth year in university, I used to visit a bookshop in Gaza City to buy English novels for enhancing my linguistic link with my job and the students. In 2022, shortly before I graduated, I wrote a short story about our tough conditions in Gaza and submitted it to a writing competition. It ranked seventh out of 80 stories, and I received a reward. What began as a practice to improve my English turned into a way of life. Whenever I had money, I bought a few novels until I gathered a large collection and built my own English library. Sometimes I purchased novels I would never open, but it felt satisfying to have them on my shelf. I could sense linguistic progress: a future.

After lectures, I went to a park near the university where I enjoyed the shade from trees and a soft breeze. It was my place where I could sit on a bench under a big tree, a cup of coffee in one hand, a novel in my bag. The novels were all fiction. What I loved was the way the writers chose words. That gave me the literary sense to generate a unique language over time.

In that shady spot, I opened The Alchemist by Paulo Coelho and began to read: “Tell your heart that the fear of suffering is worse than the suffering itself.”

I recalled Gaza’s 50 percent unemployment rate. I would graduate after a few months and start desperately seeking a job, competing with tens of thousands of unemployed graduates who were also fighting over the same positions. Young men used to dream of building families and marrying the girl they loved. Now they watch their hopes crumble under occupation and blockade. I recalled the constant wars every two years, the terror and psychological traumas they inflict. The patient people who can’t leave because of the blockade and the exorbitant travel fees. The eight-hour daily electricity cuts that devastated us for years.

Thinking about these forms of suffering is unavoidable. They deteriorate your life. But coexisting could be our only key to survival. We learned to carry the weight without collapsing. We learned to read between the lines of our own destruction. Knowing that everyone is suffering gives one a strange kind of comfort.

“And that no heart has ever suffered when it goes in search of its dreams, because every second of the search is a second’s encounter with God and with eternity,” Coelho wrote.

I believed it. Tomorrow will be better. The suffering is temporary. I let out a breath I didn’t know I was holding and turned the page.

When I closed the novel, I was certain Coelho had written it for Gaza. For us. For the young people who struggle so much until we believe it is part of life to keep suffering. For those who are still dreaming no matter what.

Then I saw the word on the cover: fiction.

What was fiction to the world was not fiction to us.

I took a pen and crossed it out. I wrote: reality.

I started to read fiction not just to escape, but to understand, to see how fictional worlds were constructed, to learn how to change our reality, or at least adapt to it. Reading became my life, not just for language, but as a chain of subplots that I recognized in my own existence.

One day I turned to Shakespeare:

To be, or not to be: that is the question:

Whether ’tis nobler in the mind to suffer

The slings and arrows of outrageous fortune,

Or to take arms against a sea of troubles…

I once saw Shakespeare’s words as distant, beautiful meditations on grief — something to study, not to live by. In university lectures, the beloved professor Refaat Alareer, who was killed by an Israeli airstrike in 2023, always asked us: “How can you relate to this as a Palestinian?”

“We lack freedom, suffer the devastating blockade and limited resources to thrive. We are the exception case for the world’s rules,” students would reply. “So shall we stay silent and say it is okay to suffer or shall we rebel?”

Refaat took up arms with a pen. He wrote our suffering in …

author: Marianne Dhenin
title: California Is Home to 200 Billionaires. Organizers Say It’s Time to Tax Them.
content:
If passed, California’s Proposition 40 would generate funding for health care, education, and food assistance programs.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Thousands of volunteer canvassers are hitting the streets across California, fighting for a first-of-its-kind wealth tax on the state’s ballot on November 3. Those mobilizing for Proposition 40 — which would generate revenue to backfill federal funding cuts to health care, education, and food assistance programs — are up against hundreds of millions in spending on competing ballot measures from the billionaires who would be taxed by Proposition 40. Whether or not it passes, experts told Truthout the citizen-led ballot initiative is a historic measure that could serve as a model for future efforts to tax the ultra-rich.

“Either way, even if it doesn’t, but definitely if it wins, it’s going to set a new standard for the type of tax that people can demand via ballot initiative,” Benjamin Case, project lead on the Ballot Initiatives Project at Arizona University’s Center for Work and Democracy, told Truthout. “It’s the first wealth tax in the U.S., and first wealth tax of its kind in the world, and it’s also the first tax specifically on billionaires.”

The ballot measure was announced last October by high-profile progressive economists Emmanuel Saez and Robert Reich, as well as the Service Employees International Union’s (SEIU) United Healthcare Workers West, which represents 145,000 health care workers across California. Proposition 40, also called the Billionaire Tax Act, would levy a one-time 5 percent tax on the total net wealth of each of the state’s billionaires, using a retroactive residency date of January 1, 2026. It would apply to roughly 200 billionaires, including Silicon Valley titans like Mark Zuckerberg and Peter Thiel. These individuals have seen their average annual income rise 7.5 percent on average per year over the last four decades, while wages for the average American stagnate and a growing number struggle to meet their basic needs.

Most taxes are levied on income or real estate, not wealth. The latter is meant to capture a person’s net worth, including real estate, cash, and stock holdings, minus debts. Wealth taxes remain relatively novel, outside of some examples in European nations. A recent analysis of a similar wealth tax implemented in Norway found that it did not spur significant outmigration of the ultra-rich or deter founders from starting their companies in the country. The relatively few business owners who did leave Norway under the new tax program maintained their businesses and did not stop investing in the country, according to the analysis.

“If you think about the wealthiest billionaires in California, they have a net worth of somewhere in the range of $250 billion, and our highest income tax bracket applies to everybody who makes essentially more than a million dollars. The difference between a million dollars in income and $250 billion in wealth is just astronomical,” Chris Hoene, executive director of the California Budget and Policy Center, told Truthout. “It’s an innovation to try to tax wealth, and you can do it at a very small margin and produce a lot of revenue quickly.”

Proposition 40 is expected to generate about $100 billion over the next five years. About 90 percent of that revenue would be used to replace the tens of billions of dollars that will be stripped from California’s 15 million Medicaid recipients over that same period under President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. That bill slashed taxes for the wealthiest Americans and is expected to undercut health care and social services programs nationwide. The cuts are expected to create a $100 million shortfall in California’s Medi-Cal program alone over the next five years, stripping over a million Californians of coverage and forcing clinics to shutter. SEIU estimates 145,000 health care workers could lose their jobs. The bulk of the cuts are expected to hit after the midterm election, but many across California are already bracing.

“Frontline health care workers that are in the facilities with the patients are already seeing this,” Renee Saldaña, United Healthcare Workers West’s press secretary, told Truthout. “Patients are already getting nervous about things like ‘Am I going to be able to afford my medicine? Am I going to be …

author: Unknown
title: Whereabouts of man summoned by Iranian Revolutionary Guards remain unknown
content:
A 40-year-old man has been detained in the city of Piranshahr in East Kurdistan (Rojhilat) after being summoned by the intelligence service of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). His whereabouts have remained unknown since his detention. The man, Ahmad Mostafanejad, has been denied access to legal counsel and contact with his family.


According to the human rights organization Kolbarnews, Mostafanejad was summoned by telephone to the Revolutionary Guards’ intelligence department in Piranshahr on Wednesday, October 14. After complying with the summons, he was detained and taken to an undisclosed location.


No information has yet emerged about the reasons for his detention or any possible charges against him. His health condition and detention conditions also remain unknown. Iranian authorities have neither disclosed his whereabouts nor allowed him to contact his family.

author: Novara Media
title: China’s Century of Revolutions
content:
For a century, China underwent a series of invasions, revolutions and counter-revolutions. In China, it’s known as the Century of Humiliation.


It was a time of immense upheavals: from the Opium Wars of 1839, through the Taiping Rebellion, the Xinhai Republican Revolution, a Civil War, an invasion by the Japanese which merged into the Second World War; the resumption of the Civil War and, eventually coming to an end with the Communist Revolution of 1949.


Each one transformed the country more comprehensively than seemed possible beforehand.


Rebecca Karl is the author of

China’s Revolutions in the Modern World

, which tells us not only what happened, but how its participants tried to make sense of it all, and why that still matters for understanding China now – after all, the Chinese Communist Party haven’t forgotten any of it.


She joined Richard Hames to discuss the century that destroyed imperial China and set the stage for the largest revolution in history.


There is much more to explore on the map we’re making for this series, which shows all the people, ideas and event that define China’s history, present, and future. Get it

here

author: Unknown
title: Jineolojî Conference: Women’s liberation must become a force for shaping society
content:
How can the ideology of women’s liberation become a politically effective force in society? This question was at the center of the second day of the European Jineolojî Conference in Haelen, the Netherlands. Around 150 delegates discussed building a democratic and communal society, overcoming hierarchical forms of organization, and integrating Jineolojî more deeply into everyday social life. Shortcomings in previous work were also openly addressed.


Alongside Jineolojî activists, the conference brought together representatives of women’s councils, communes, cultural and faith communities, media outlets, and civil society organizations, as well as mothers. The session on the transition from the ideology of women’s liberation to organized political practice featured contributions from scholar Dilar Dirik, Meral Çiçek of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E), and Elif Kaya of the Jineolojî Academy.


Dilar Dirik: ‘Transformation requires courage’


Dilar Dirik raised the question of the internal conditions necessary for social transformation. She argued that simply continuing existing activities or establishing new organizational structures was not enough. Instead, deeply entrenched ways of thinking, taboos, and patriarchal patterns of behavior must also be overcome, she underlined.


Dirik critically examined the state-centered legacy of actually existing socialism, arguing that its failure to sufficiently question its own foundations had led to the emergence of new hierarchies. Contemporary forms of organization, she added, could also unintentionally reproduce social divisions and power relations.


“Transformation requires courage,” Dirik emphasized.


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261017125111_2026-10-17-haelen-jineoloji-konferasi-2-nci-oturum-1.mp4


It was therefore crucial, she argued, not to limit social organizing to political actions. “People must be directly involved in decision-making and be able to develop alternatives that meet their actual needs. This also includes economic opportunities.” Dirik advocated establishing cooperatives and alternative economic models, noting that the need to secure an individual livelihood makes it difficult for many people to participate consistently in social activities.


She also called for closer cooperation with environmental initiatives, migrant movements, and other social forces. Socialism, she argued, must be reflected not only in political objectives but also in interpersonal relationships. “Socialism emerges by responding to the needs of others, through love and affection,” Dirik explained.


Çiçek: Women’s organizing is the foundation of social transformation


Meral Çiçek continued the discussion by raising the question of how the ideology of women’s liberation could be transformed into an organized political force. She argued that social bonds had been increasingly weakened by capitalist living conditions. “Communal organizing must therefore strengthen solidarity, shared responsibility, and collective decision-making processes. The most fundamental characteristic of society is its communal nature,” Çiçek said. Under current conditions, the commune offers a way to preserve social values and communal life, she added.


Referring to the political transformations in the Middle East, she emphasized the importance of the Kurdish people developing an independent capacity for political action. “To defend their achievements and take advantage of new opportunities, Kurds in all four parts of Kurdistan and in the diaspora must develop strong political representation,” Çiçek said, noting that this process is inseparable from women’s organizing. “The democratic transformation of society is only possible through an organized women’s struggle. Women’s liberation must not be limited to political representation but must transform social relationships, decision-making structures, and everyday life,” she stated.


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261017122858_2026-10-17-haelen-jineoloji-konferasi-ikinci-gun-tartismalar_1.mp4


“Democracy means more than participation in elections. Communes must be based on shared needs, act independently, and develop democratic connections with one another,” Çiçek stated. She advocated structures in which representatives of different communes could discuss common issues and make decisions collectively. “Organizing efforts must include diverse social groups: We must embrace all the colors of society and finally overcome …

title: Saturday Mothers demand answers about the disappearance of Fehmi Tosun
content:
At their 1,125th vigil in Galatasaray Square in Istanbul, the Saturday Mothers commemorated Fehmi Tosun, a Kurd from Lice who was abducted in front of his family 31 years ago and has been missing ever since. Holding photographs of their relatives and red carnations, participants once again demanded that cases of enforced disappearance be investigated and those responsible brought to justice.


The gathering focused on the still-unresolved abduction of Tosun, who was 35 years old and a father of five at the time. Ikbal Eren, whose brother Hayrettin Eren also disappeared while in police custody, recalled that numerous people had witnessed Tosun’s abduction and that his family had concrete information about the perpetrators.


On the evening of October 19, 1995, three armed men in civilian clothes brought Tosun to his home in Istanbul’s Avcılar district in a white Renault. When he saw his wife and five children, he shouted, “They are going to kill me!” Before his family could reach him, he was forcibly dragged into the vehicle and taken away.


His wife, Hanım Tosun, immediately reported the abduction to the police and provided officers with the vehicle’s license plate number. Although the officers checked the license plate and made phone calls, they eventually stated that there was nothing they could do. The authorities later denied having taken Tosun into custody. His friend Hüseyin Aydemir, with whom he had eaten breakfast that morning, has also been missing since that day.


Human rights violation acknowledged, investigation closed


Ikbal Eren pointed out that in 2003, during proceedings before the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), the Turkish government acknowledged that the investigation had been inadequate and that it had violated its obligations under Article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights. The government had also pledged to take measures to prevent similar cases.


Nevertheless, Tosun’s disappearance was never effectively investigated. The case was closed on the grounds that the statute of limitations had expired, and the family’s legal appeals were unsuccessful. An individual application to Turkey’s Constitutional Court also failed to shed light on his disappearance.


“The government’s acknowledgment of the rights violation and payment of compensation are no substitute for justice,” Eren stated. She emphasized that the state was obliged to establish the fate of the disappeared and hold those responsible accountable. The practice of paying compensation without ending impunity ultimately encouraged the continuation of such crimes.


‘Why have you put up these barricades?’


Hanım Tosun, the wife of the disappeared man, made a particularly impassioned appeal to the state authorities. She criticized the police barricades that continue to restrict access to Galatasaray Square. “You should not speak of justice, the judiciary, or the law. If you truly speak of justice, then look at Galatasaray. Why have you put up these barricades here?” Tosun asked. She emphasized that the families were not insulting anyone but were simply demanding the truth about their disappeared loved ones.


She called for state archives to be opened, pointing to records that remained in the possession of the authorities. “If you speak of peace and justice, you must first speak about the Saturday Mothers. You must finally show us a grave. You must open your archives. Only then can you speak of justice and peace.”


Tosun reaffirmed that the families would continue their protests until the fate of all those who had disappeared was clarified and the perpetrators were brought to trial.


The vigil concluded with the laying of red carnations in Galatasaray Square.

title: Various Authors - Products of Desire
content:
Author

: Various Authors

Title

: Products of Desire

Subtitle

: On Loving the Unreal

Date

: 2019

Source

: <

littleblackcart.com/index.php?dispatch=products.view&product_id=625

> [Even though the website says the book is in stock, the book publisher is no longer.]


 


 This work features excerpts from three pieces which explore the ways a desire for the impossible changes the way we see reality itself. Patrick Galbraith explores affection for anime characters as resistance to society, J. Keith Vincent looks at the queerness of a desire that “decouple[s] sexual desire from social identities and naturalized bodies”, and Toshio Okada (of Gainax fame) and Kaichiro Morikawa debate fans as anti-social vs. fans as customers.


 


Moe:

 Exploring Virtual Potential in Post-Millennial Japan


 Original article at

https://www.academia.edu/3665389/Moe_Exploring_ Virtual_Potential_in_Post-Millennial_Japan


Making it Real: Fiction, Desire, and the Queerness of the Beautiful Fighting Girl by Keith Vincent, from

Beautiful Fighting Girl

 by Tamaki Saitou, tr. Keith Vincent and Dawn Lawson, University of Minnesota Press, 2011


Otaku Talk


 original article located at

https://www.gwern.net/docs/eva/2004-okada


** Products of Desire


**On Loving the Unreal**


 


 I hesitated to make this pamphlet because it’s about something so ridiculous yet intimate. Despite the often academic prose of these articles, it’s hard not to feel a bit exposed by their contents. If you’ve ever seen one of those iconic images of a fan’s bedroom— those immaculately decorated exemplars of horror vacui with every inch covered in (often lewd) posters and (often expensive) figures—this is the territory we’re stepping into. In a way, however abstract the writing may sometimes be, I’m inviting you into my bedroom. At the heart of this writing is always this space of intense desire. Perhaps this is a space you’re already familiar with—maybe it’s your bedroom too, or maybe you’ve only caught glimpses of it in the shadier portions of the internet. Perhaps you just felt weird watching Disney’s Robin Hood when you were younger.


 The desire discussed here is focused on otaku (anime fans) because of the richness of critical examinations surrounding them (as well as because of the specific interests of this author), but the ideas discussed could apply to cartoon fans in general, to furries, or to any of the many circles in which deep affection is felt for the unreal. The point is to explore that desire, however briefly, to see what it does and where it goes.


 A subject of interest to two of the authors contained herein is how love for the unreal implicates any stable concept of reality itself. For J. Keith Vincent, writing about Tamaki Saitou’s

[1]

 Beautiful Fighting Girl (Saitou himself drawing on Lacanian theories around perceiving reality), there is a queerness to this attraction that “decouple[s] sexual desire from social identities and naturalized

bodies”. Patrick

 Galbraith’s

[2]

 treatment of moe (pronounced mo-ay and defined by him in short as an intense emotional response to a fantasy character) finds in this desire for the unreal a “certain refusal” of dominant forms of life founded in the home and family, and connects this (however briefly) to Lee Edelmen’s refusal of “reproductive futurism”. Vincent’s piece offers a more comfortable vision of the desiring subject (ultimately “there is a little otaku in all of us”) to Galbraith’s more expansive and transgressive moe, but both give us different and insightful takes on similar subject matter.


 Our final piece, an excerpt from a discussion between Toshio Okada

[3]

 and Kaichiro Morikawa

[4]

 and moderated by Takashi Murakami

[5]

, further highlights a tension that the reader will see in both of the aforementioned pieces: the question of how different these people actually are, despite their exotic tastes. The otaku’s response to dominant reality is debated—Morikawa claiming that moe, rather than more clearly political or utopian thinking in science fiction, “has replaced the future.” Morikawa also characterizes otaku as those who gravitate towards socially unacceptable things. Okada however describes them as merely a different kind of consumer: “tough customers who demand high standards,” discerning consumers who value quality.


 In the end, the desires featured in these articles don’t appear to be a way out—in some cases far from it. We are presented again and again with …

title: Tora Pekin: Süreklileştirilmiş bir darbenin gölgesindeyiz, yasal tutukluluk süreleri aşıldı
content:
Sayın Başkan, Sayın Üyeler öncelikle bu ek savunmalarla ilgili olarak da tabii ki kendi aramızda değerlendireceğiz ve gerekli beyanlarda bulunacağız ama asıl olan müvekkilimin 4. gününde yapmış olduğu savunma. Geçen buradan içerikten sonra tekrar size beyanda bulunacağız.


Şimdi 578 gündür süren bir tutuklamanın gölgesi altında müvekkilim Sayın Ekrem İmamoğlu'nun sorgusuna ek beyanlar için söz aldım. Öncelikle aslında ben almamalıydım bu sözü. Sözü Avukat Mehmet Pehlivan almalıydı. Hem bir hukukçu, hem savcılıkta o vardı. Şüpheli evresinde, savcılıkta benim müvekkilimle birlikte o vardı.


O da burada olmalıydı, bu savunmayı da o yapmalıydı, ben de bunu kendisine diye düşünüyorum. Bununla ilgili olarak ek beyanlarımı aktarmam gerek. Evet, tutuklamanın gölgesinde söz aldım diye söyledim ama üzerimize düşen tek gölge değil. Biz 19 Mart'tan bu yana süren sürekli kılınan bir darbenin gölgesi altındayız. Bu ülkede sayın İmamoğlu ve yargılananların çoğu bunları dile getirdiler, davasıyla da. Şimdi bu dava bitecek mi? Yoksa Adalet Bakanının da ifade ettiği gibi ek iddianamelerle sonsuza kadar sürecek mi, bunu bilmiyoruz.


Bu belirsizliklerin gölgesi altındayız. Bunu sayın İmamoğlu söylemişti. Ben ekliyorum; sizin de bildiğinizi düşünüyorum, sizin de zorlandığınızı düşünüyorum. Neden çıkartıldı bu söylem de demeyeceğim çünkü bu beyanla beraber duruşma saatleri bir normale geldi.


Duruşma saatlerimiz gece yarılarından doğru 10'a kadar çekilmişti herhalde o da bence normal saat değil ama bu beyandan sonra biraz daha rahatladınız. Yani tamam ben bu yargılamayı sıktıracağım diyorsunuz ondan sonra da takdir edenler gerçekten dediğiniz gibi itirazımız da olsa. Ama 400'den fazla yargılananı dinlediniz, beyanını sorguladınız.


İddianame sayısı


O aşama bu beyanın arkasından o hız, yine bitirelim dediniz bence zaten hani fazla da uzatmamışız ama makul saatlere geldi, 6'ya, 7'ye geldi saatler. Ben biraz sezgisel, şöyle düşündüğünüzü düşünüyorum yani: Ya sürekli bana ek iddianame göndereceklerse, 2 gün gönderiyorlar. Yaptığına sonrasında basının yayın, daire başkanlıkları. 


İddianamesi geldi, siz de kabul ettiniz. Sürekli buradaki sayı artacaksa, yargılanan sayısı ve bu sayısı artacaksa, gece yarılarına kadar yapmaya gerek yok yani. İşi bitiremiyoruz. Ondan sonra o makul saatlere geldi, 18.00'e dedik, 19.00'a dedik, ona gerek yok diye düşünüyorsunuz diye düşünüyorum, tahminimce.


Şöyle; evet, bu gölgeleri anlattım. Nelerin üzerimize gölge düşürdüğünü anlattım ama bu kısır döngü sonsuza kadar gidebilir. Çok kötü bir dönemde, dava denilmeyecek bir zor kullanmayla karşı karşıyayız Sayın Başkan, Sayın Araştırmacılar. Şimdi bence bu zor kullanmaya karşı, bu darbeye karşı sürekli kılınmıştır. Bir darbeye karşı asıl olan Sayın İmamoğlu'nun 4. günündeki söyledikleridir. Yani sorgu aşamasında bu beyanın üzerine daha fazla söz söylemeye anlam da yok diye bunu düşündüm. Tabii sorgunun bitmesi sırasında Sayın Başkanım, siz kurmadan, biz çalışıyorduk.


Orada bir dile getirilmesi var, 4. gün dile getirilmesi var, yüreklere seslenen bir dile getirilmesi var. Doğrusu isterseniz bunun üzerine, bu sesi yankılamak dışında, daha fazla bir şey söyleyelim söylenmez mi? Bunu düşündüm. Bu soru, beni başka bir soruya götürdü.


O da şu; Sayın İmamoğlu, vekaletimi üstlendiğimden beri doğal olarak, en şık dosya. En başlarda aynen. İlk FETÖ operasyonu olduğu zaman doğal olarak her operasyonda doğal bir reflekstir, her şeyi inceleyip varsa yalan söylenen bir şey. Niye alındı, yani müvekkilim niye alındı? Bir şey var mı? Yani dosyada bir şey var mı, 2 tane soru.


Bu soruyu ilk duyduğum andan itibaren, iddia edenin yanıtı şuydu: Ha tamam, aynen bu yanlış. FETÖ'nün abisi veya sözcüsü izlemiş biliyorsunuz kendilerini söyledikleri öyle bir ilgisi var, delili var. Ki şu an hakikat, bu konuştuğumuzun başlamasından itibaren, önce FETÖ. Sonra geçen hafta, ATV kapanacak, onlar yok falan filan sadece suçlama falan.


Bir şey soracaksa soracak aynen. Sinem Hanım niye alındı? 1,5 senedir anlatıyor çocuklar. Bu soru yanlış bir soru. Niye alındı sorusu yanlış bir soru. Dosyada bir şey var mı sorusu yanlış bir soru. Tamam mı? Dosyada bir şey yok. Yokluğunu değil, ama yanlış bir soru. Bu soruyu sormak bizi muhalefet iktidarına götürür.

Anthropologists have yet to give up their calipers

Secret history, or shaky historiography?

Occult Features of Occult Features

I have been sitting on this review for quite a while. This short book comes up quite often when combing through anarchist literature on occultism (and vice-versa). With the release of more than a million documents from the Epstein files bringing new relevancy to the issue of conspiracy theories, I think the most fortuitous time to publish it has come. Or went, because I again sat on this review for many months.

Occult Features of Anarchism, by Erica Lagalisse, concerns the alleged roots of classical anarchism (and the wider radical milieu) in Western esotericism and in particular, the late antique Corpus Hermeticum. This is combined with an anthropological analysis of conspiracy theories, loosely (indeed, very loosely) connected through the Masonic tradition.

Lagalisse begins Occult Features with two pastiches in her activist and fieldwork. First, she recounts dissuading a fellow activist from accepting an antisemitic conspiracy theory during an EZLN event in Montreal (pg. 3). Then, she observes Montreal anarchists marginalizing an Indigenous Mexican woman named Magdalena – on a speaking tour organized by the EZLN – due to a combination of gendered and racial prejudice (pg. 6). These events left her deeply changed, and her research interests shifted to the influence of theosophy and Freemasonry on classical anarchism (pg. 8). Through this analysis, she hopes to “illustrat[e] the cosmology of classical anarchism” and thus complicate anarchism's alleged relation to secularity (pg. 11). For Lagalisse, this sort of analysis is central to “a decolonized anarchism that properly challenges gendered power”, in which the modes in which the modern colonial state privatizes religion and gender – while reproducing its own cosmology and patriarchal structure – are studied (pg. 12). Thus her focus on esotericism: “any inquiry into the gender of the modern revolutionary left that digs farther back in history than the union movements of the masculine wageworking proletarian [...] necessarily stumbles upon the institution of Freemasonry, among other clandestine fraternities” (pg. 8).

Her first premise is that anarchism, like all Western political theory, is innately tied up with theology, following from Schmitt and Sahlins – particularly, the dialectic between the immanence and transcendence of God. Utopian socialism, anarchism, and Marxism rely on a “cosmology that is incipient in the Middle Ages, changing and crystallizing in the Renaissance, and gradually given a scientific makeover throughout the Enlightenment and up to the twentieth century” (pg. 18). A crucial point for Lagalisse here is the “shift from the spontaneous millenarian movement to the organized heretical one” which is related to the “dissemination of diverse mystical doctrines” that began in Europe during the Crusades – the Corpus Hermeticum is a “largely unrecognized” source of modern leftist politics (pg …

content:

author: Ross Kirshenbaum
title: Washington State Invests My Pension in Genocide. I’m Demanding Divestment.
content:
Workers across the US are demanding divestment from firms that profit from weapons and surveillance. I’m one of them.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Last month, I joined more than 45 bus drivers, teachers, and government workers to testify before the Washington State Investment Board, demanding responsible investment of our pension funds. I arrived grateful to be surrounded by fellow pensioners who were grounded in a shared commitment to fighting for investments that reflect our values.

Quickly it became clear that the Washington State Investment Board was going to strictly enforce the 45-person speaker limit that it implemented last year after beneficiaries began regularly demanding divestment at their meetings. This meant that my friend, a Palestinian member of my union who had taken off the day to testify, was barred from speaking. I had a minute to speak and yielded my time to him. We would not allow their bureaucratic procedures to silence us. We spoke out because we believe our state’s investments should earn money for our retirement funds without compromising our values.

This mobilization of beneficiaries began with Washington’s Cut Ties with Genocide campaign, launched by Washington for Peace and Justice and Jewish Voice for Peace Seattle. Sitting in an early meeting of the campaign, I was heartbroken to learn that the Washington State Investment Board invests my pension money into companies that enable genocide abroad, surveil and warehouse my neighbors, and contribute to climate chaos around the world. When I began my career as a bus driver in 2016, I was proud to have a pension. Now I felt like my pension was tainted. I could see clearly that my future financial stability was built on the destruction of other people’s futures.

What are these harmful investments? The Washington State Investment Board has invested over $204 million in Lockheed Martin, one of the world’s leading weapons manufacturers. Lockheed Martin produces the F-35 fighter jets that have been crucial to the Israeli military’s genocide in Gaza. These jets have the capacity to carry and detonate 2,000-pound bombs — bombs that destroy whole families, buildings, and neighborhoods in Gaza, leaving behind craters in the earth. In just one horrifying example from 2024, the Israeli military used F-35 jets to drop three 2,000-pound bombs on an Israeli designated “safe zone” in Khan Younis, killing 90 Palestinians and injuring hundreds.

The Washington State Investment Board has also invested more than $73 million in Palantir, a secretive data and AI company whose technology enables mass surveillance in the U.S. and across the world. In March, immediately after the horrifying Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) occupation of Minneapolis, the ACLU reported that Palantir technologies “form the backbone for ICE’s mass deportation regime.” Palantir’s leaders embrace surveillance and provide essential data to Donald Trump’s fascist forces. When the Washington State Investment Board invests in these companies, us pensioners are conscripted into complicity with Israel’s genocide against Palestinians, the mass deportations of our neighbors, and global climate devastation.

As a pension beneficiary, I care deeply about ensuring that our state’s public investments are both moral and profitable. The Washington State Investment Board manages over $230 billion in assets, which include retirement funds of public employee pensions for over 600,000 workers like me. Studies show that ethical investing can generate about the same or even more income than investing in war profiteers and human rights abusers.

The Washington State Investment Board has invested over $204 million in Lockheed Martin, one of the world’s leading weapons manufacturers.

We in Washington are not alone in our call: We’re part of a movement across the country of pensioners demanding that our retirement stop enabling human rights violations.

In Maryland, the Baltimore Teachers Union has joined community allies to demand an end to the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System’s investment in Israel Bonds.

Pensioners in Maine have been involved in a legislative push to get Maine’s state pension fund to divest from corporations and countries enabling severe human rights violations — companies like Lockheed Martin.

author: Ariana Figueroa
title: Immigrants From Ukraine and Sudan Could Soon Lose Their Protected Status
content:
The Trump administration has moved to eliminate legal protections for more than 1 million immigrants that have TPS.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

More than 100,000 Ukrainians and roughly 2,000 Sudanese immigrants are bracing for the possibility they’ll lose their humanitarian protections by Monday.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has not indicated if he will renew protections for Ukrainians, who first received Temporary Protected Status after Russia invaded their country in 2022, and for Sudanese nationals, who were granted the designation several times, most recently in 2022, because of an ongoing civil war.

The Trump administration has moved to eliminate legal protections for more than 1 million immigrants that have TPS. Of the 17 countries with the designation at the start of the second Trump administration, the only remaining protections are for Ukraine and Sudan, which are set to end on Monday, and Lebanon, which is set to expire Nov. 27.

Mullin is supposed to declare his decision at least 60 days before a TPS designation expires, but he’s made no announcement.

The lack of an announcement would put Ukrainian and Sudanese TPS holders in the same situation as 200,000 Salvadorians, who are still in limbo after DHS did not renew protections set to expire on Sept. 9.

If no decision is made, an automatic six-month extension kicks in. DHS has not confirmed whether the extension is in place, only that Salvadorians have deportation protections and work authorization, for now.

DHS did not respond to States Newsroom’s request for comment about TPS extension for Ukraine or Sudan.

TPS is granted when a person hails from a country deemed too dangerous to return to because of conflict, natural disaster or another destabilizing event. The Trump administration has sought to wind the program down, especially after the U.S. Supreme Court this summer determined that decisions by the executive branch regarding TPS designations could not be challenged in court.

Immigration advocates say the rationale for providing TPS to Ukrainians has not changed.

“With the war in Ukraine still ongoing and conditions remaining unsafe, the administration should extend TPS for Ukrainians,” Jennie Murray, president and CEO of the advocacy group National Immigration Forum, said in a statement. “Forcing people to return to Ukraine in these circumstances is dangerous and a departure from longstanding U.S. policy.”

If Mullin ends TPS for Ukraine, it wouldn’t be the first time Ukrainians have lost humanitarian protections under the second Trump administration.

Last year, the Trump administration moved to end new applicants for a humanitarian program created by the Biden administration that allowed more than 220,000 Ukrainians to enter the U.S.

The State Department has a do-not-travel advisory, its highest advisory level, for Ukraine and Sudan.

Fraught relations between President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy further complicate the issue as Monday’s deadline approaches.

Trump has grown frustrated with the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, and has blamed Ukraine for a spike in oil prices, ignoring the effect of his war in Iran.

On Oct. 9, Trump moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Zelenskyy called the decision “a weak decision by strong partners,” according to The Associated Press.

On Oct. 10, Trump told reporters that Ukraine should “get a new leader.”

In an interview with NPR, Zelenskyy said the Trump administration said unless Ukraine stops long-range drone strikes on oil refineries in Russia, it could cut off U.S. intelligence-sharing with Ukraine.

The two leaders have clashed in the past.

In February 2025, during a visit to the White House, the president got into a heated exchange with Zelenskyy, appearing to break with Ukraine and its resistance to Russia’s invasion.

Trump’s relationship with Ukraine was also the center of his first impeachment, after a U.S. House inquiry found the president threatened to withhold military aid unless Ukraine investigated his political opponent at the time, Joe Biden.

The U.S. Senate acquitted Trump in an impeachment trial.

There is a bipartisan congressional push to extend protections for Ukrainians at least until the end of 2029.

title: Süper güçleri olan 5 hayvan:'Marvel kahramanlarına taş çıkartan canlılar
content:
Hasan Can Bilici [email protected]

Kendi vücut ağırlığının binlerce katına dayanabilen canlılardan kopan uzuvlarını yeniden oluşturabilen hayvanlara kadar doğa, bilim kurgu filmlerini aratmayan yeteneklerle dolu. Bazı canlıların geliştirdiği biyolojik mekanizmalar, insanın teknolojiyle bile taklit etmekte zorlandığı özellikler sunuyor.

Doğada hayatta kalmak, her canlı için farklı bir mücadele anlamına geliyor. Kimi hayvanlar avcılarından kaçmak için olağanüstü hızlara ulaşırken kimileri görünmez olmayı, ölümcül darbeler indirmeyi veya ağır çevre koşullarına dayanmayı sağlayan özel mekanizmalar geliştirdi.

Bu özelliklerin bazıları, çizgi romanlardaki süper kahramanların yeteneklerini andırıyor. Ancak bunlar doğaüstü güçler değil; milyonlarca yıllık evrim sonucunda ortaya çıkan biyolojik uyumların ürünü.

İşte Marvel kahramanlarını aratmayan yetenekleriyle dikkat çeken beş hayvan ve onların bilim dünyasını şaşırtan özellikleri.

author: Unknown
title: Yurttaş mevcut siyasetten umutsuz, çareyi ‘halk meclislerinde’ arıyor
content:
Fotoğraf: Elif Ekin Saltık/ Evrensel

Elif Ekin Saltık [email protected]

Saha Araştırmaları Merkezi (SAMER), “Yurttaşların Siyaset Algısı, Alternatif Siyaset Arayışı ve Demokratik Katılım Olanakları” başlıklı araştırma raporunun sonuçlarını paylaştı. 14 kentte 428 kişiyle çevrim içi ortamda gerçekleştirilen araştırma, temsili siyasete yönelik derinleşen krizi, yurttaşların mevcut siyasal işleyişe olan tepkisini ve doğrudan demokrasi arayışını verilerle ortaya koydu.

Araştırmaya göre katılımcıların yüzde 45,1’i siyasi kararların alınma biçiminden “memnun değilim”, yüzde 33,9’u ise “hiç memnun değilim” yanıtını verdi. Mevcut işleyişten memnun olmayanların toplam oranı yüzde 79’a ulaşırken, memnun olanların oranı yalnızca yüzde 6’da kaldı.

Öte yandan yurttaşların yüzde 73,1’i siyasete katılımın sadece sandıktan ibaret olmadığını, seçim dışı yolların da varlığını kabul ediyor. Hak arama yöntemleri arasında ise barışçıl gösteri ve yürüyüşe katılmak (yüzde 36,2), sivil toplum kuruluşlarına katılmak (yüzde 26,2) ve imza kampanyaları (yüzde 21) öne çıktı.

Yurttaşlar, siyasetin yalnızca siyasi partiler ve seçilmişler eliyle yürütülmesini yetersiz buldu. Katılımcıların yüzde 77,3’ü, yerel kararlarda bölge halkının görüşünün doğrudan alınması gerektiğini savundu.

Araştırmanın en çarpıcı sonuçlarından biri ise “halk meclisleri”ne olan destek. Yurttaşların yüzde 84,1’i mahalle ve yerel konulardaki kararların doğrudan halk meclislerinde alınmasını “gerekli” veya “çok gerekli” buluyor. Yurttaşların yüzde 73,9’u, böyle bir meclis ya da toplantı kurulması halinde kesinlikle veya muhtemelen katılacağını beyan etti. Ancak bu güçlü talebe karşın, halkın doğrudan katılımına dayalı bir siyasetin Türkiye’de yaygınlaşma olasılığı düşük (yüzde 61) görüldü. Bu durum, katılım talebiyle siyasetin gerçekte dönüşebileceğine duyulan güven arasındaki uçurumu yansıttı.

Mahalledeki önemli bir sorunun çözümü için yurttaşların inisiyatif alma eğilimi (yüzde 39,7) yüksek olsa da bu durum doğrudan aktif ve örgütlü siyasete tahvil edilemiyor.

Aktif siyasetin önündeki en büyük engeller şöyle sıralandı: Yüzde 15,4 ile “katılımın etkili olduğunu düşünmeme”, yüzde 15,2 ile “baskı ve korku ortamı”, yüzde 14 ile “zaman yetersizliği” ve yüzde 10,3 ile “yeterli bilgi ve donanıma sahip olmama”. Katılımcıların yüzde 26,2’si ise doğrudan siyasete katılmak istemediğini belirtiyor.

Rapor, siyaset mekanizmalarındaki toplumsal cinsiyet ve yaş eşitsizliklerine de ayna tuttu. Kadınların yüzde 33’ü aktif katılım hakları konusunda hiç bilgisi olmadığını veya çok az bilgisi olduğunu belirtirken, bu oran erkeklerde yüzde 11,8’de kaldı. Aktif siyasete katılmak istemediğini belirten kadınların oranı (yüzde 39,3), erkeklerin oranının (yüzde 18,1) iki katından fazla.

Gençlerde ise güvensizlik ve uzaklaşma eğilimi dikkat çekti. 18-24 yaş arası gençlerin yüzde 47,6’sı aktif siyasete katılmak istemediğini belirtirken, halk meclisi veya halk toplantısına katılma isteği gençlerde yüzde 56,3 düzeyinde kaldı. Bu oran, yaş ilerledikçe artış gösteriyor ve 65 yaş üzerinde yüzde 100’e yaklaşıyor.

Araştırma sonucu, halkın karar alma süreçlerine doğrudan müdahale edebileceği demokratik, eşitlikçi, güvenilir ve sonuç üreten mekanizmaların kurumsallaştırılmasına duyulan ihtiyacı ortaya koyuyor. Katılımcıların beklentilerinin ilk sıralarında katılım mekanizmalarının artırılması, siyasi haklar konusunda bilgilendirme ve örgütlenme olanaklarının güçlendirilmesi yer alıyor.

Raporun tamamına ulaşmak için tıklayın.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: İzmir Barosu Olağan Genel Kurulu başladı: 'Hukukun üstünlüğünü savunmaya devam edeceğiz'
content:
İzmir- İzmir Barosu 2026-2028 Olağan Genel Kurulu, Bayraklı’daki Mustafa Kemal Atatürk Spor Salonu’nda başladı.

14.670 avukatın üye olduğu baro yönetiminin belirleneceği genel kurulun ilk gününde avukatlar, mesleki sorunlarını tartışmak ve yeni dönem yönetimini seçmek üzere bir araya geldi.

Dört adayın yarıştığı seçimlerde Çağdaş Avukatlar Grubu’nun adayı Emre Öktem, Cumhuriyetçi Avukatlar Grubu’nun adayı Serhat Sökmen, İzmir Avukat Hareketi’nin adayı Volkan Gültekin ve bağımsız aday Tacettin Çolak yarışıyor.

Genel kurul saygı duruşuyla başladı. Saygı duruşunun ardından oy birliği ile divan seçildi.

İzmir Barosu Genel Kurulu’nun divanı adına konuşan Av. Çetin Turan, baronun hak ihlallerine karşı mücadelesine dikkat çekerek, “İzmir Barosu hukukun her alanında yapılan hak ihlallerinin karşısında çıkmıştır. İnsan, çevre haklarını savunmak İzmir Barosunun görevleri arasına girmiştir” dedi.

Ülkedeki hukuki ve siyasi tabloya değinen Turan, mevcut yönetimin hukuk kurallarına uygun hareket ettiğini söylemenin mümkün olmadığını belirtti. Anayasal güvencelerin fiilen ortadan kaldırıldığını ifade eden Turan, yargı organlarının kararlarının uygulanmadığını, bağımsız olması gereken mahkemelerin görev alanlarını aşarak kararlar verdiğini söyledi.

Sulh ceza hâkimlerinin otomatik tutuklama hâkimlerine dönüştüğünü, yurttaşların yasalar karşısında eşit olmadığını belirten Turan, “Yasalar kimine uygulanıyor, kimine uygulanmıyor. Hukuki güvence kavramı terk edilmiş. Gazeteciler tutuklanıyor, televizyon kanalları kapatılıyor. Avukatlık mesleği günlük geçim sorunu dışında müdafiliğini yapamıyor” dedi.

İzmir Barosunun barışı ve toplumsal değerleri savunduğunu vurgulayan Turan, güncel gelişmeler karşısında baronun söyleyecek sözünün olacağını belirtti. Barışa ilişkin tartışmalara değinen Turan, İzmir Barosunun tek adam rejimlerine karşı çıktığını ve hukukun üstünlüğünü esas alan parlamenter sistemi savunduğunu söyledi.

Turan, “Bu karanlığın elbet dağılacağına inanıyoruz. Gelecekten umudumuzu kesmiş değiliz çünkü haklıyız, tarihsel akışın doğru tarafındayız” diye konuştu.

Dünyanın çok sayıda siyasi dava gördüğünü hatırlatan Turan, Türkiye Barolar Birliği kurucu başkanının 1971’de siyasi davalara ilişkin yaptığı tespiti anımsattı. Turan, “Sokrates’i ölüme mahkûm eden hâkimlerden hiçbiri bugüne kadar ulaşamadı ama Sokrates’in savunması devam ediyor” sözleriyle konuşmasını tamamladı.

İzmir Barosu 2026-2028 Olağan Genel Kurulu’nda açılış konuşmasını yapan Baro Başkanı Av. Sefa Yılmaz, hukukun üstünlüğü, savunma mesleğinin karşı karşıya olduğu sorunlar ve ülkedeki hak ihlallerine dikkat çekerek, “Anayasası olan bir ülkeyiz ama anayasanın hiçbir hakka ilişkin maddeleri uygulanmaz. Anayasal bir ülke değiliz” dedi.

Savunma mesleğinin adil yargılanma hakkı ve adalete erişim açısından vazgeçilmez olduğunu vurgulayan Yılmaz, “Savunma mesleğinin olmadığı yerde adil yargılanma hakkından bahsedilemez, adalete erişimden bahsedilemez. İzmir Barosu her zaman savunma mesleğini önceleyen ama hiçbir zaman hukukun üstünlüğünden ödün vermeyen bir anlayışı hayata geçirmek için çalışmıştır” dedi.

Türkiye’nin uzun süredir ağır bir hukuksuzluk döneminden geçtiğini söyleyen Yılmaz, 2010 ve 2017 anayasa değişikliklerinin bu sürecin önünü açtığını ifade etti. Tek adam rejimine geçişle birlikte hukuksuzlukların ve yolsuzlukların gündelik hayatın sıradan olayları gibi karşılanmaya başladığını belirten Yılmaz, “Artık bu ülkede nefes almak bile zor. Bu ülke dört yanı demir parmaklıklarla çevrilmiş cezaevi” dedi.

Yılmaz, insanların söyledikleri sözler nedeniyle gözaltına alınıp tutuklandığını, hatta neden tutuklandıklarını bilmediklerini ifade ederek, “Hukuksuzlukların temelinde bu tek adam rejiminin olduğunu biliyoruz. Faşizm konuşma yasağı değil, söyleme mecburiyetidir” diye konuştu.

İzmir Barosunun toplumsal olaylar karşısında aldığı tutumun yalnızca yönetimlerin değil, bütün meslektaşlarının katkısıyla oluştuğunu belirten Yılmaz, baronun bugün kamuoyunda sözleri merak edilen bir kurum olmasının bu ortak mücadeleyle mümkün olduğunu söyledi.

Yılmaz, Ankara 2 Nolu Baro Başkan Adayı Gökhan Ağdemir’in 10 gün önce yaptığı, “son iki yıl içinde 70 hâkim ve savcı kazandırdıklarına, tavsiye ettiklerine ve görüştüklerine”ilişkin açıklamasını hatırlatarak, bu konuda suç duyurusunda bulunduklarını belirtti. author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: Govt scrambles to solve fuel crisis without clear end in sight, divided on fava bean import ban; Quintet tries to balance competing political initiatives; RSF continues Blue Nile push; Military sets sights on Darfur
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

 here

.


The struggling wartime economy took center stage this week in Sudan with a pair of issues at the heart of daily life.


The first is a fuel crisis that has grown increasingly worse in recent weeks as gas stations have become makeshift campsites and prices have skyrocketed. While the government has projected an outward image of assurance, behind closed doors, the wheels are turning to try to bring fuel to the nine states under military control.


The plan has two axes, sources informed of the discussion told Mada Masr. The first is essentially a triage: tighten fuel allocations and movement to where it is needed. Various government bodies have tried their hand at centralizing authority to better streamline decision-making, but Sudan’s fractured executive apparatus has seen more attempts than results.


The second part of the plan would require solving the issue at its source: bringing in new supplies to offset the non-performing domestic oil sector. For this, Transitional Sovereignty Council chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan is holding talks with Saudi Arabia. But as an informed TSF source told Mada Masr, the government cannot commit to a timeline to end the crisis until external agreements are finalized and the necessary financial guarantees are in place.


Alongside the fuel crisis, more potential trouble looms on the horizon, and this one is of the government’s own making. At the beginning of October, the Agriculture Ministry announced it would implement a prime ministerial decree banning fava bean imports in order to bolster domestic production and save foreign currency. In the last two weeks, the move has come in for fierce public criticism, which has been mirrored by criticism from the government and traders, sources in both arenas told Mada Masr.


The concern centers on whether a domestic agriculture sector strained by war and the fuel crisis can realistically carry the burden of producing enough supply of the daily food staple. Government sources told Mada Masr that the process in announcing the decision was flawed, and the Cabinet does not have the required data to ensure the ban won’t have disastrous effects. State-level administrative officials and traders chimed in to argue that the timing of the decision hasn’t given farmers enough time to adjust this season’s production plan to bolster supply.


While a source in Prime Minister Kamel Idris’s office projected confidence that the Agriculture Ministry has the necessary data to back up the soundness of the ban, a source in the ministry said that officials are already discussing contingency plans.


The political front this week saw yet another spin on the merry-go-round of political initiatives. The Quintet — which comprises the African Union, the United Nations, the Arab League, the European Union and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development — is trying to carefully engage with all competing political initiatives without endorsing any. This comes amid increasing divides between civilian political groups and the preparatory committee leading the government-sponsored internal dialogue over who gets to set its terms and who gets to participate. Both sides of the divide are trying to influence the AU to gain a leg up.


On the military front, the Rapid Support Forces continued this week to push for greater control of the Blue Nile locality of Wad al-Mahi. The military was able to push the advance back in a counteroffensive on October 9.


On the western front, the military launched airstrikes on RSF positions as it looked to translate its control of North Kordofan into a stronger position in West Kordofan to take the strategic city of Nuhud. Control of Nuhud would open the door to North Darfur, on which they already have their sights set, military sources told Mada Masr.


From within Darfur, the military made strategic gains this week, with the joint forces advancing from their remaining garrisons in the north of the region down into West Darfur, where they seized control of the agriculturally rich area of Bir Keleikil.
